0.content:
Alatyr (also: Alatyr Village): Alatyr is a remote village in Snezhnaya, abandoned several years before the Traveler arrives, and the hometown of the Rokot hunter Alyosha. A brutal winter bandit raid left its people destitute; when no help came, some villagers became highwaymen. The village cannot be visited in the game.

It had no train station and lay so far out that official aid would take days to arrive. Alyosha says that, years later, nobody lives there; Alatyr's former residents scattered to other towns and cities.

History: In a particularly harsh winter, when Alyosha was still young, a gang of bandits robbed Alatyr and spared no household. Alyosha, using the hunting skills his father had taught him, hunted the bandits down and recovered the stolen goods, but the raiders had owned nothing worth taking back, so the village still could not rebuild and neighbouring villages could not help either. Some villagers then planned to become highwaymen themselves, and Alyosha took charge reluctantly, setting one rule: ordinary travellers are never to be touched.

Alyosha's character stories call the target travellers 'fowl' (merchants and ordinary people) and the armed highwaymen and gangs 'beasts', and say he steered the group to prey only on 'beasts', so that they would not draw the attention of the Druzhna. The household's finances were crushed by medical bills and his parents' lost livelihood, and Alyosha's father had insisted he learn to count coins and weigh grain as well as shoot.

People: Former townspeople named in canon are Alyosha and his parents, Repnina (an elderly woman from the same village who now lives in Sretomorozsk; her memory is failing and Alyosha visits her, sharing fond memories of the place) and Taras (one of the highwaymen, described in Alyosha's stories as a man who could barely hold his rifle straight yet grew eager to join the attacks). Alyosha's hunting dog, Tugarin, is also from this period.

Travel: Not accessible. Alatyr is a place people mention rather than visit.

Status as of 7.1: Abandoned and inaccessible as of 7.1. It is only known through Alyosha's story and the Sretomorozsk episode of Chapter VII.

1.content: In Sretomorozsk the liaison officer Shishkin was caught with stashed Kresnik Kristall and claimed he took it for his elderly parents in Alatyr, a village with no train station where deliveries had stopped. Alyosha cut in: Alatyr is empty and has been for years, and the missing Kristall was far more than Shishkin admitted. This exposed Shishkin and the Sretomorozsk mayor, who had been selling stolen Kristall. Polonsky later thanked Alyosha and remarked that the tale was probably meant to shield the mayor.

2.content:
Armory Palace (also: Royal Armory Palace): The Armory Palace, formally the Royal Armory Palace, is the Snezhnayan institution that develops weapons. Sandrone manages it, and it lies deep underground within Glupov, the Fatui's seat. It is closed to outsiders, guarded by Fatui troops and the Special Assignments Battalion, and is where the Landcruisers were engineered and where Project Mistilteinn's experiments take place.

Its secrecy is practical as well as political: the research there feeds the Tsaritsa's plan to be able to resist the Heavenly Principles. In the Version 7.0 Archon Quest Mistilteinn the Traveler and Odette break in to rescue Paimon, and the facility turns out to be the epicentre of the Ruler of Death's Curse of Death.

It is also where Mitya works when he is not slipping away to the theater, and where, in 7.1, the Armory Palace's newest invention, the Mirror of Remembrance, is used to examine the Curse of Death.

Geography: The Armory Palace is hidden deep inside Glupov, reached by taking an elevator down from the surface. The complex is large and spreads over many floors and chambers, including a restricted outer area with guard posts, corridors lined with automatic turret mechanisms, laboratories and an enormous deep chamber with heavy machinery. Odette remarks that the style does not look like Fatui construction and guesses that structures from an earlier civilisation were requisitioned and also serve as a disguise.

In the deepest parts a large circular elevator takes visitors down to Mitya's laboratory, and a cell-like room off it was where Paimon was kept during the incident. A broad gap on the route is crossed by activating a Starlight Prism-like object that replays images of the past.

Places: Known areas: the guarded gates near Glupov; the research halls; a turret chamber; a prism room; the heavy machinery hall where the large-scale experiment runs; and Mitya's laboratory below it.

In 7.1 a room houses the large Mirror of Remembrance prism. The 7.1 prism is presented by Pierro as a recent Armory Palace innovation made by enhancing and solidifying an ordinary prism.

People: Sandrone manages the institution. Mitya is the researcher most closely tied to it, and Valeriy, a member of the Special Assignments Battalion, is tasked with guarding and keeping tabs on him. Pierro, the Jester, oversees the experiments of Project Mistilteinn and visits in person. Odette, who knows the Fatui's inner workings, guides the Traveler through it.

Other named staff: Zinenko, another Special Assignments Battalion guard. Historically the wiki also lists the deceased researchers Preobrazhensky and Anton Zarkovich Karnatsky, whose rivalry led to a disaster in the Nothing Passage in Nod-Krai.

Governance: Sandrone manages the Armory Palace, though Pierro, the Fatui's Director, takes personal oversight of Project Mistilteinn there and Mitya reports to him. The wiki says its administrative system is allegedly rather complex (item text).

The Special Assignments Battalion belongs to the Armory Palace Royal Grenadier Guards and protects important figures such as Mitya while also keeping watch on them.

Culture: Staff are researchers and soldiers under strict secrecy. Outsiders are forbidden, so the effects of the Curse of Death went unnoticed outside for a long time. The name echoes the Kremlin Armoury in Moscow, which began as a royal arsenal. Armory Palace staff speak of 'breakthroughs' and 'verified hypotheses' in a scientific register; Mitya answers to evidence rather than rank, as when he recommends suspending the project 'purely as a scientist, guided by reason alone'.

History: The Armory Palace first appears in Version 6.0 (Luna I) content and is best known for developing the Landcruisers, automated war machines used by the Fatui across Snezhnaya and Nod-Krai.

The Adventurer Handbook says Landcruisers were first engineered by its finest engineers as armed ships that cruise on land. Cyclic Military Kuuvahki Core item text ties the Landcruisers to the Kuuvahki Experimental Design Bureau, a joint effort with the Fatui.

According to item text cited by the wiki, two Armory Palace researchers, Preobrazhensky and Anton Zarkovich Karnatsky, were sent to research kuuvahki in the Nothing Passage of Nod-Krai; their rivalry ended in a disaster that killed them and the entire Fatui Sixth Company except Smirnova. In Version 7.0 the Armory Palace became the setting of Project Mistilteinn's experiments, which required enormous energy that Project Stuzha was gathering. When Pierro took Paimon here, Mitya used the same energy to cancel the experimental effects on her. The Ruler of Death's Curse of Death had been killing researchers whenever a technological breakthrough threatened the Heavenly Principles, which explained earlier reports of memory loss. In 7.1 the Tsaritsa endorsed halting the project until the Ruler of Death was dealt with; after Ronova's fall the restrictions were lifted.

Atmosphere: A vast, cold, humming facility of spotless corridors, guard calls and turret mechanisms that track movement, with the sense that something large is being built just out of sight. Researchers are polite and curious even towards intruders.

Guards shout warnings, but at least one researcher recognises Odette as a star of the theater and does not realise the visitors are intruders. When the large-scale experiment starts the whole complex shakes, and moments later the Curse of Death strikes.

Dangers: Fatui guards, Oprichniki troops, turret mechanisms and Landcruisers defend it. The greatest hazard is the Curse of Death, which kills everyone in the vicinity whenever Snezhnaya's technology approaches a breakthrough; its victims wake in an afterlife and later return to life with their memories of death gone.

Even a stray experiment can kill and revive the whole staff, as Mitya found when a final-phase energy experiment brought the curse down on everyone present. In 7.0 he judged that no breakthrough was possible without eliminating the Ruler of Death.

Travel: There is no public access. Entry is through Glupov's guarded gates and a long elevator ride down. The Traveler first goes there as an intruder and later as a guest of Pierro and the Tsaritsa.

Mitya says outsiders are forbidden, which is why the Curse of Death's effects stayed within the Armory Palace for so long.

Quests: Archon Quests: Mistilteinn (Chapter VII Act II, 7.0), in which the Traveler and Odette storm the Armory Palace; Light and Shadow, Intertwined (Act III, 7.1), in which Pierro presents the Mirror of Remembrance. It also appears in the background of Wraith's Nocturne, where Odette finds Mitya dead there before he returns to life.

Mistilteinn is also the quest where Project Mistilteinn is first named.

Status as of 7.1: Active. As of 7.1 Project Mistilteinn is free to move forward after Ronova's fall, and the Armory Palace is investigating the application of life force.

In 7.1 the Tsaritsa tasked Mitya with researching life-force applications, which are important to restoring Project Mistilteinn, and Vesna extracted 'Seals of Life' at the Armory Palace using her small authority.

Canon still does not state what Project Mistilteinn finally builds.

3.content:
The Special Assignments Battalion is a division of the Armory Palace Royal Grenadier Guards. It protects important figures such as Mitya and keeps tabs on them. Valeriy and Zinenko are among its members.

Alyosha says Valeriy visits the theater only to look for Mitya, who sneaks off there when he should be at work. Valeriy later serves as the Traveler's assist character in Wraith's Nocturne.

4.content:
Landcruisers are automated war machines developed by the Armory Palace, described as armed ships that cruise on land. They appear in Nod-Krai and Snezhnaya as common enemies, from scouts and storm models to the Super-Heavy Landrover: Mechanized Fortress, and are tied to the Kuuvahki Experimental Design Bureau.

Landcruisers guard the Armory Palace itself in the Mistilteinn quest.

5.content:
After Pierro takes the sleeping Paimon, the Traveler and Odette force their way into the Armory Palace through its guards and turret chambers. Deep inside the heavy machinery starts a large-scale experiment and the Curse of Death kills the Traveler, Odette and the staff. The Traveler wakes first, finds Mitya, then Ronova arrives and tries to claim Paimon until Pierro blocks her. Mitya concludes that Ronova's curse triggers on technological progress and recommends suspending Project Mistilteinn; Pierro agrees.

Pierro and Mitya also used their energy to cancel what made Paimon unwell. The Traveler suspects Odette's Cor Ignis helped guide their soul back from the afterlife.

6.content:
Pierro calls the Mirror of Remembrance a recent Armory Palace innovation made by enhancing and solidifying an ordinary prism so that it can store memories and, to a limited degree, collect memories from its surroundings. It is used in the Armory Palace to review snippets that show Ronova collaborating with Rhinedottir.

With Vesna's small authority of life, the Armory Palace also extracts Seals of Life as a possible way to counter death.

7.content:
Bratskaya (also: Bratskaya shop, Berezka): "Bratskaya" is a small general-goods shop in Zolnyy, the Ash District of Snezhnograd, in Snezhnaya. Its owner, Grigory, sells cooking ingredients and treats his regulars as neighbours rather than just customers.

The shop is open at all hours and its stock is restocked daily. Its customers are mostly nearby residents of Zolnyy. Next door in the same district stands the beverage shop Kvasnik.

People: Grigory is the owner. In his shop dialogue he says a purchase is final once the customer leaves the counter and that in principle he does not sell on credit, "in principle" being the operative words. He frames credit as a favour for struggling villagers rather than a service for travellers who can afford to pay.

Grigory is on friendly, familiar terms with Alyosha, the Snezhnayan hunter. He packs jerky, flatbread and fruit for Alyosha's trips and says he often relies on Alyosha's help while out making deliveries. Alyosha answers formally; Grigory teases him for it and asks him to turn back if a hunt turns dangerous. Alyosha's companion Tugarin is mentioned as always knowing the quickest way out.

Culture: Grigory says credit has become more common lately and that "around these parts" misfortune is always waiting round the corner, so the shop acts partly as a safety net for the people who live nearby. The sign over the door is written in Snezhnayan script and, per the wiki, reads "Berezka".

Atmosphere: A cramped neighbourhood shop in an industrial district: shelves of staples, a cheerful but practical owner who jokes with customers, and the cold outside never far from the conversation.

Gameplay: Game mechanics: Grigory's stock of cooking ingredients refreshes daily. With Alyosha in the party, a first conversation gives a small gift of Golden Ferns and Rimecurrants.

8.content:
Central Station (also: Snezhnograd Central Station, Central Railway Hub, Central Train Station): Central Station is the largest railway station in Snezhnaya, in the capital Snezhnograd. The official map text calls the railways the nation's veins and the Central Station the heart of a 'titan of cold iron and steel'. Arriving passengers pass inspections by Snezhnaya Royal Railway Transport Bureau staff, then ride an elevator up to the heart of Snezhnograd.

The West, East and North public train routes all start here.

Geography: The station is split into an Exit Level, where passengers leave the station and meet inspectors and news sellers, and a Platform Level with the tracks. An elevator lifts people from the station to the core of Snezhnograd.

The viewpoint named 'Central Railway Hub' is located here.

People: Transport Bureau personnel include Safety Officers Gurevikov, Iliana and Sochikov; Conductors Kholodnaya, Aryna, Bazhenov, Kira and Rudov; and the Ticket Agent Voskresensky. Newsies Laktionov and Katia work the concourse. Mamontov is a freelance writer. Other NPCs include Andrevich, Chagina, Emma, Kholmogorov, Leonie, Tsvetkov, Uliana, Urusov and Vedomek on the Exit Level, and Arseny, Daniil, Dobronravov, Fyodor, Gerard, Ilya, Nadyushenka, Pecherskaya, Shemyakin, Svetlana, Veronika and Vikhrov on the Platform Level.

The Bureau also has train announcers such as Agapov and Kasova on the public trains; they announce stops such as Morepesok to passengers.

Governance: The Snezhnaya Royal Railway Transport Bureau, also called the Transport Bureau, runs Snezhnaya's railway system, and its staff inspect arrivals here. The Bureau answers to Zapolyarny Palace according to the wiki's infobox.

The wiki also notes the Bureau is sometimes called Chicota, based on a weapon description.

Culture: Newsies sell papers on the concourse, and passengers pass inspection before they enter the city.

Travel: Public trains are managed by the Transportation Bureau and make all stops on a route. The West route runs Central Station, Morepesok, Rankova Zorya; the East route runs Central Station, Svetloledovka, Sretomorozsk, Rankova Zorya; the North route's other stations are not yet known.

To call a public train, players select 'Wait for the train to arrive at the station' at a station sign. This is a gameplay option; it is not part of the world setting.

Atmosphere: Official map text compares the place to the ever-pounding heart of a nation of cold iron and steel, with the railways as its veins.

Quests: In the Archon Quest One Move Left to Make (7.1), the group learns that someone has possibly stolen Seals of Life from the frail and elderly, and they come to Central Station, where Alyosha, made up to look old, approaches a suspicious man named Avaz.

Alyosha pretends he wants his life extended. If Avaz is convinced, he leads Alyosha outside the station and asks for payment in a few days; if not, he tries to flee and the Traveler catches him.

Status as of 7.1: Running. The station remains the Snezhnograd entry point for rail travel, with inspections still in place.

9.comment: Central Station: Snezhnaya Royal Railway Transport Bureau
9.content:
The Snezhnaya Royal Railway Transport Bureau, often shortened to the Transport Bureau, is the organisation in charge of Snezhnaya's railway system. At Central Station its safety officers, conductors and ticket agent are posted, and its staff inspect arrivals before they enter Snezhnograd.

The wiki's faction page is a stub; it lists the Bureau as affiliated with Zapolyarny Palace and based in Novokitezhgrad.

10.content:
Cloudborne Altar (also: Cloudborne Palace): The Cloudborne Altar is a summit ritual site above the clouds, high over the House of Hesperides in Fellfrost Peak. Pavlina, the Snegurochka Grand Duchess, used it for the last stage of a rite meant to take the power of the Eye of Graeae. The Traveler reached it in the quest Bell Ringing at Dusk and stopped her there.

The altar is reached by climbing past the Frozen Fulgurbranch and the Rumblebranch, ice formations that draw lightning, so a visit means ascending through a frozen storm.

Geography: Part of the House of Hesperides area (map level "Cloudborne Palace"), above the mansion's chapel and far above the cloud layer. The route up goes through a lift, past a teleport waypoint at the Frozen Fulgurbranch, and then up an incomplete Rumblebranch, which has to be completed by gathering two smaller branches (Rumbletwigs) before the way to the altar opens. The altar itself is described by Paimon as gorgeous.

The Eye of Graeae explains why Pavlina needed this height: the chapel inside the house is only for the part of the ritual that receives power, while giving power across a wide area needs somewhere much higher. Lightning is drawn down from the clouds toward the site.

History: In Bell Ringing at Dusk, the Traveler and Paimon arrive uninvited (the Traveler holds an invitation, which Pavlina says was never meant to be sent). Pavlina fights them. Aksinya then steps out of a portal to the Shadow Realm, saying she has finally broken free of Pavlina's traps, and joins in stopping the rite. After the fight Pavlina and Aksinya speak: Pavlina wants the power to give her people, the Snegovik, a whole soul; Aksinya wants it kept for a different plan. Pavlina disintegrates into icy mist and the union ritual is left complete without the offering having been made.

The Eye of Graeae says that its fragmented parts re-crystallized after the ritual. Aksinya hands over a part of the Eye's body and explains that the Snegovik can only achieve completion through rituals, which is what Pavlina's endless rites were for. She also says Pavlina's success would have been the greatest defeat for the world, while granting that Pavlina acted out of love for her own people. This dialogue is from a world quest and the details of Aksinya's own plan are covered in Court of Eternal Bliss.

People: Pavlina is the central figure here. Aksinya appears at the end of the quest. The Traveler is accompanied by Paimon and by the Eye of Graeae, which supplies the guidance on the route.

Atmosphere: High, bright and cold: an open platform above the cloud layer, with branches of frozen lightning below and a sense that the storm itself has been made part of the ritual. Beautiful, but the Eye of Graeae warns that even the most pleasant places may hide danger.

Dangers: Pavlina herself is the only threat shown at the altar. On the way up, falling lightning is a concern raised by Paimon and the Eye.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the ritual here has been stopped and no later content in the sources changes that. Pavlina is gone from the House of Hesperides after Bell Ringing at Dusk.

11.content:
Court of Eternal Bliss (also: Court of Bliss, Courtyard of Carefree Light): The Court of Eternal Bliss, also called the Court of Bliss, is a chamber in the Pale Crown Palace where the Belyi Tsar's body lies sealed. Aksinya, the Tsar's former court jester, wanted to use it for a rite that would complete the Primordial Human and bring about a "Courtyard of Carefree Light". The Traveler stopped that rite here in the quest An Ark That Used to Be a Soul.

Entering it is the climax of the world-quest chain that began at the ruined Hvergelmir, and it contains the Tsar's White Birch, the living remainder of the Belyi Tsar's body.

Geography: The entrance is a door on the upper level of the ruined Hvergelmir, within the Pale Crown Palace. It is blocked by the Tsar's White Birch and cannot be opened until all three fragments of the Eye of Graeae's power have been recovered, which means finishing the world-quest series Hesperides of Love and Hate, In the Dwelling of Life and On One Side a Palace, On the Other a Tomb. The Traveler then performs a return ceremony, spending Kresnik Energy to open it. Inside is a cold courtyard under the Tsar's White Birch.

Aksinya describes the White Birch as the ever-growing nerves of the Tsar's husk, a shell that never truly perished. The chamber also holds the Tsar's original body, which the Traveler first sees beneath the birch as a huge mechanical-looking form, and a portal from it leads into a Shadow Realm arena where a train carries the party.

History: After the fragments are gathered, the Eye of Graeae vanishes as the door is opened and Aksinya appears. She tells the Traveler that the Eye was built to host the "Proto-Man" and that its body and power are to be assimilated into the Belyi Tsar's body so that he can become the Primordial Human. She teleports away, the party chases her through the Shadow Realm, and in the court the Tsar's body begins to transform. Aksinya returns the Eye as an empty shell and says its consciousness is now the core of the Primordial Human. The Primordial Human wakes, claims to remember everything and asks to be stopped. After a boss fight the door to the new world is shut and the being that remains has the appearance of the Tsar in his youth.

Before the fight the Primordial Human asks the Traveler what they would do if their sibling had become someone else. The Traveler answers that they would learn to love them again. Afterwards Aksinya and the Primordial Human fall together into the Shadow Realm, and Aksinya says she was freed from it earlier by Izmaylov's help. The Primordial Human admits he incited Koshchei, Pavlina and Alvis to divide him up and betray Aksinya, because he wanted to avoid becoming the Primordial Human.

People: Aksinya, the Tsar's court jester and creator of the Eye of Graeae, is the antagonist. The Primordial Human, the Eye of Graeae, Paimon and the Traveler are the other participants. The Belyi Tsar is present only as a body and as the form the Primordial Human takes.

Koshchei, Pavlina and Alvis, whom Aksinya counted as allies, have already been stopped or have turned against her before the court is entered.

Atmosphere: A frozen courtyard that feels like a tomb and a temple at once, dominated by the white birch growing out of the Tsar's body. The mood is grief and finality rather than menace: Aksinya speaks sadly and politely, and the conflict is between two ideas of love.

Dangers: The fight is against Aksinya and then the Primordial Human. During the Shadow Realm chase the Eye of Graeae's gadget is removed from the Traveler, so the Cold accumulation guard is gone and exposure builds quickly (a gameplay detail of the quest).

Quests: Only one quest uses it, An Ark That Used to Be a Soul, which is the first and only quest of the chapter Her Palace Collapses Into the Blizzard.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the rite has been stopped and the Court of Bliss as a world has not been created. The sources do not show it changing in 7.1.

12.content:
Druzhna HQ (also: Druzhna Headquarters, Headquarters of the Druzhna): Druzhna HQ is the headquarters of the Druzhna in Snezhnograd, the capital of Snezhnaya. The Druzhna is the Tsaritsa's personal guard, led by Commander Vesna and made up mostly of Vila. The building is where the Tsaritsa's special recruitment drive to clear Shadow Realms is run by the officer Yarovaya.

The Druzhna also contains Shadow Realm breaches as part of its duties, which is why a dedicated operation to recruit gunners is based here.

People: Yarovaya, a "Druzhna" Podporuchik, runs the Shadow Realm operations from here. The wiki lists Malinina, Musina, Rozhdestvensky and Shakhovskaya as other NPCs stationed at the headquarters. Yarovaya is a Vila with blonde hair, green eyes and small round glasses, in the Druzhna uniform.

Yarovaya's duties span verifying public reports of anomalies, processing intelligence from the Royal Energy Commission of Snezhnaya, setting containment perimeters, and finally entering the Shadow Realm to carry out clearing operations.

Governance: The Druzhna answers only to the Tsaritsa. Vesna commands it, and the Druzhna works alongside the Fatui. The Belyi Tsar founded it, and the Tsaritsa kept it as her personal guard rather than using it to suppress revolts against her authority; she raised the Fatui for that instead, according to "A Brief History of the Pale Starborn".

Akvilina, a Druzhna officer, tells the Veche in 7.0 that the Druzhna's workload is heavy and that supervising Tartaglia's proposed regional data collection might prove difficult.

History: Historically the Druzhna was subordinate to the Belyi Tsar and its commander was Filipov. It remains active as the Tsaritsa's guard.

The special recruitment project run from the headquarters was arranged by the Tsaritsa herself, who believes talent is hidden among the populace. Yarovaya admits to a superior that the Druzhna is "severely short-handed" and normally would handle such missions itself.

Quests: A Special Selection (World Quest, 7.0): the Traveler passes a recruitment test and Yarovaya offers a Shadow Realm clearing job, with Kristall for villagers as a stipend. It unlocks Special Recruitment Project: Cycle Training, in which Yarovaya gives weekly Shadow Realm missions. The follow-up world quest series is Looming Shadows, Parts I to VI.

Applicants are tested on their shooting, and the Druzhna wants only people strong enough for what Yarovaya calls "a matter of life and death". Many applicants join for the pay, which rumour says includes Kristall. A senior woman later says the Tsaritsa has other plans for the new recruits beyond filling gaps in the official forces.

Atmosphere: A uniformed, disciplined place with queues of nervous applicants, short curt verdicts ("Next!") and officers who treat Shadow Realm work as life-or-death business.

Status as of 7.1: Open and recruiting, with weekly Shadow Realm training missions available through Yarovaya.

13.content:
The Special Recruitment Project is the Tsaritsa's initiative to recruit capable shooters to enter Shadow Realms and clear them. Yarovaya assigns each week's training missions. The game text describes Shadow Realms as strange zones that appear suddenly in Snezhnaya's tundra like bubbles in water; people swallowed by one vanish and are warped into monsters.

The map text suggests that helping Yarovaya might even earn the favour of the figure on the throne of Zapolyarny Palace.

14.content:
Everfrozen Earth (also: Everfrozen Earth region, Yongning Dongtu): Everfrozen Earth is the frozen northern region of Snezhnaya (first seen in 7.0). It holds the capital Snezhnograd, the Fatui headquarters city Glupov inside it, the fishing port of Morepesok and the Prime Ice mining station Svetloledovka. The ground is permanently frozen soil; the region is known for its birch forestry, a trade humanity carved out during Snezhnaya's pioneering era that still runs today.

The in-game description calls the north's frozen soil the home of Morepesok, the only port city on the northern coast. Snezhnograd and its Fatui satellite city Glupov are the political centre of the nation, which makes the region the backdrop for the opening of the Snezhnaya Archon Quest.

Geography: Frozen ground and snow country on the northern coast. Morepesok is a seaside port whose people live by fishing; Svetloledovka sits by a Prime Ice mine; Snezhnograd lies inland as the capital. Birch groves are the region's famous feature. Local specialties include Flockingweed, Frostfairy Flower and Golden Fern, and an Immortal Construct is the area's notable boss enemy.

Snezhnograd has its own district, Zolnyy, and landmarks such as the Zapolyarny Palace, the Podvorye Restaurant and the Northland Bank. A Snezhnaya train line links the capital with Svetloledovka, where Prime Ice miners who live in the city commute to work, and with Morepesok and Rankova Zorya.

Places: Snezhnograd: capital of Snezhnaya. Glupov: a satellite city inside Snezhnograd and the Fatui's headquarters. Morepesok: northern fishing port and a Fatui Harbinger's hometown. Svetloledovka: Prime Ice mining station beneath the frozen mountains.

Glupov was founded when the Tsaritsa ordered the Fatui to build a fortress near the capital (an account in a history book places this in the 799th cycle) and its name means "city of fools". Morepesok's people compare catches after each outing, and an in-game remark suggests becoming a Fatui Harbinger might impress them. Svetloledovka's name can be read as "Light-Ice Village".

Dangers: Deep cold, blizzards and Fatui presence in the capital. Wildlife and chimeric constructs roam outside settlements. Svetloledovka's mine has been closed by monsters (Bandersnatch) after the events of the Archon Quest.

Quests: Archon Quest Chapter VII, Act I "Everwinter Without Mercy" passes through the region: in "Great Deeds on the Tundra" the Traveler reaches Snezhnograd by train, meets the Fatui in Glupov and Zapolyarny and then rushes to Svetloledovka to help people trapped at the Prime Ice mine.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the region is intact and open; nothing after 7.0 is recorded as changing it.

15.comment: Everfrozen Earth: Svetloledovka and the Prime Ice Mine
15.content:
Svetloledovka is a mining town and train station built in the shadow of the frozen peaks, where workers dig Prime Ice. Many commute by train from Snezhnograd. During the Archon Quest the mine was cut off and people trapped inside had to be rescued; afterward a notice records that mining is suspended because of monsters inside. Its tavern and workers (engineers, a safety officer) appear in side content.

An in-game puzzle has a miner nearly frozen to death who thanks the Traveler with Glaciafruit sent by his family. The area description of Fellfrost Peak says the mountain's foot hosts a mining town, so some sources treat Svetloledovka as belonging to that mountain's economy.

16.content: Morepesok is a small seaside port and station on the northern coast, the only port city there. It is the hometown of the Harbinger Tartaglia. Fishing is the livelihood and its harbour hosts the vessel "The Sea Tsar" (Captain Vyazemskaya, First Mate Yazykov). Local folklore and rumour about the nearby Flamefeather Valley make it the staging point for the valley quests.

17.content:
Fellfrost Peak (also: Fellfrost Mountain): Fellfrost Peak is a giant snow-sloped mountain south of Snezhnograd. On its summit stands the House of Hesperides, the mountain manor of the Snegovik and their Grand Duchess, said to own the whole mountain. A Prime Ice mining town lies at its foot and the fae Jack Frosts keep a hidden village on its slopes. Blizzards and a ban on unauthorised hiking keep visitors away.

The Grand Duchess Pavlina held the mountain but seldom appeared in public. In the 7.0 world quests the Traveler climbs to the manor and becomes entangled in a doomed series of wedding rituals there.

Geography: A giant, snow-sloped mountain with fierce storms and extreme cold. A notice board on the path warns that the House of Hesperides is closed to unauthorised entry and that hiking is strictly prohibited because of the snowstorm. Caves along the route offer shelter from the weather. Local specialties are Flockingweed and Frostfairy Flower.

Notable sites: the House of Hesperides at the summit with its chapel, Jack Frost Village (a hidden fae settlement on the mountain) and Tidesong Cavern, a secluded cave used by the fae Vodyanitsa as her private practice space. A boss fight with a Guardian Blade of Drifting Snow takes place on the slopes, and elite enemies include Volkodlak Lobbers, Raiders and Sharpshooters.

Places: House of Hesperides: mansion on the summit, home of the Snegovik and their Grand Duchess. Jack Frost Village: hidden fae homeland, besieged by Volkodlak and relieved by the Traveler. Tidesong Cavern: Vodyanitsa's hidden practice cave. Svetloledovka: the mining town at the mountain's foot (placement disputed, see uncertainties).

The manor has an upper floor of documents, a rooftop and a chapel where the wedding rituals take place. Prime Ice and Kresnik Kristall can be gathered around the House of Hesperides. Jack Frost Village is the former home of the Geo Jack Frost Lumi, where Linnea first met her.

People: The Snegovik, whose leaders are called Snegurochka, live in the House of Hesperides; Pavlina was their Grand Duchess. Jack Frosts are small fae. The Volkodlak are hostile raiders on the slopes.

A powerful Snegurochka knight once served Pavlina and parted ways with her after she became Grand Duchess because their paths no longer matched. Pavlina earlier kept a cat named Lara at her laboratory in the Pale Crown Palace, from her time as a researcher of the Hvergelmir institute.

History: The mountain is the Snegurochka's domain. A fragment of the Eye of Graeae's lost power lay in the House of Hesperides, which is why the Traveler and the Eye came here. Pavlina had been Grand Duchess since before the Cataclysm, five hundred years ago.

Pavlina was an alchemist and, under the Belyi Tsar, a researcher at the Hvergelmir institute together with Koshchei, Alvis and Aksinya. After Aksinya's plan was thwarted and she was cast into the Shadow Realm, the Eye of Graeae was split into three. Pavlina sought to use its power to give the Snegovik complete souls and began performing wedding rituals with Ikhor, a being formed from one of the fragments.

Atmosphere: Blizzards that plaster snow over a climber's face, stinging cold, and a lone lamp blessed by a fae that makes the storm ease around it. The summit manor is formal, brittle and haunted by ritual.

Dangers: Whiteouts and extreme cold, starvation for the lost, Volkodlak war bands, winged knight constructs, glacial wardens and glaciomancers, chimeric beasts and the Guardian Blade of Drifting Snow boss.

Quests: The world quest series "Hesperides of Love and Hate" (Through the Gates of Ivory; Procrustes' Iron Bed with its parts The Sun's Gilded Apple and House of the Soulless; Bell Ringing at Dusk) is set here. A separate quest, "Small Jack Frost, Big Problems", defends Jack Frost Village from Volkodlak. Tidesong Cavern's dialogue opens after "Like a Land Where the Tide's Song Whispers".

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the mountain is open to explore, but its Grand Duchess Pavlina has died.

Pavlina was defeated at the Cloudborne site by Aksinya and the Traveler after taking Ikhor's power, and disintegrated as the last ritual finished, leaving a fragment of the Eye of Graeae's power. Who leads the Snegovik now is not stated.

18.content:
The House of Hesperides is the mountain manor at the top of Fellfrost Peak where the Snegovik and their Grand Duchess live. It contains a chapel, a mansion with an upper floor of documents and a rooftop, and Prime Ice artisanry. In the quest "Through the Gates of Ivory" a lamp blessed long ago by a fae eases the cold on the climb.

Pavlina's journal says the Snegovik follow the ancestor Yalyane Morevna's decree that their leader must have a complete soul, found through true love, and that an ancient Snegurochka told Pavlina that the throne sometimes passes without it.

19.content: Jack Frost Village is the hidden homeland of the Jack Frosts on Fellfrost Peak, recently besieged by Volkodlak until the Traveler fended them off in "Small Jack Frost, Big Problems". It is also the former home of the Geo Jack Frost Lumi, where Linnea first met her. The quest unlocks the Jack Frosts' Goodies Shop, and a discarded cardboard Jack Frost face in a broken igloo seems to have been used as a disguise by some creature.

20.content: Tidesong Cavern is a secluded cave on Fellfrost Peak that the fae Vodyanitsa uses as her personal practice space, and the site of a Meeting Point of the same name. Dialogue there unlocks after the quest "Like a Land Where the Tide's Song Whispers" and involves Vodyanitsa with Odette, Alyosha and the Traveler.

21.content:
Flamefeather Valley (also: Fiery Plumage Valley): Flamefeather Valley is a strange valley west of Snezhnograd that was once home to humans. Now almost nothing remains but a small town that turns up in ghost stories. It is named for the tall trees with leaves like flaming feathers, and for the bird-shaped monsters with crimson pinions that survivors report. Many curious explorers have gone in and never come back, though no official order forbids it.

The town is Okurov, a warm, abandoned village whose past is tied to the experiments of the bio-alchemist Koshchei. In the 7.0 world quests the Traveler learns what happened there.

Geography: A valley with an unnaturally warm microclimate compared with the rest of Snezhnaya, filled with tall trees whose crimson leaves look like flaming feathers. A train tunnel, caved in at the entrance, leads to Okurov, and a flooded drainage sewer lies beneath the village.

Okurov has an assembly hall (with a "Hall of Prayers"), a tall building with an elevator and Nastya's home. Local specialty: Golden Fern. Enemies include chimeric armored beasts and winged elephants, Rugged Elder Leshy and Juvenile Tree Segment elites.

Places: Okurov: abandoned village in a warm climate, with a dark history. Teeming Mire: the area where the guardian Zhara is finally fought. Nastya's home and the assembly hall: key buildings in Okurov.

People: By the time the Traveler arrives, only a few remain: the girl Nastya, the woman Furiosa, and a handful of Leshy (tree-like beings who were once townsfolk), among them Aunt LePuy and "No-Nose" Ove. Zhara watches over the valley, and a Volkodlak gang led by "The Anvil" has been looting and kidnapping.

The villagers had been persuaded that becoming trees and joining "one family" would end pain. The experiment's mastermind posed as a healer called Doctor Moreau or "Doctor Birdie", but was in fact Koshchei the Deathless.

History: Okurov was once a village of ordinary people. Koshchei, a bio-alchemist who had worked in the Belyi Tsar's Hvergelmir institute, used it to try to create a "Perfect Tree" through a final ceremony that would turn everyone into embryos of a new, emotionless existence. Those who took part dissolved into blue algae, including Koshchei himself. After the Cataclysm the town stayed sparsely populated, with a few Leshy, Furiosa and Nastya remaining.

Furiosa and Ove came to see Koshchei's real intent and tried to keep other villagers from entering the assembly hall; Zhara, a winged Immortal-Construct-like guardian, kept out any "Badbugs", her word for outsiders, for several centuries. The Eye of Graeae said one fragment of its power lay in the valley.

Atmosphere: Warm, humid and eerie: neat crimson foliage over silent houses, lullaby-like talk of "family", and a child's cheerful games that turn out to be about burning outsiders.

Dangers: Zhara, mindless Leshy, Volkodlak bandits, chimeric beasts and traps inside the assembly hall. In Okurov the game switches to a third-person shooter mode. Locals and rumour say nobody who enters Okurov returns.

Travel: The quest chain starts at Morepesok's train station and passes through a train tunnel. Okurov itself unlocks by progressing the world quest "Transplanted From Yesterday to Tomorrow".

Quests: The world quest series "In the Dwelling of Life": A Sprout Without a Gardener, Transplanted From "Yesterday" to "Tomorrow", Down in the Dumps, Back on One's Feet, Forbidding Doors of Melancholy, To Rest in a Forgotten Field and Chorus of Solace. It begins in Morepesok and follows Nastya's escort home.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the valley is quiet: Zhara and the Perfect Tree experiment are finished, and the village is empty.

22.content:
Okurov is an abandoned village in a warm climate with a dark history. A newspaper in the train tunnel praises its weather, its excellent doctor and its welcome to travellers. In the story its residents were persuaded to grow branches and leaves and call themselves one family, believing it would heal their sorrows.

The village's name echoes a 1908 Russian novel. Its assembly hall holds a relief of Zhara, an elevator and a final "home" chamber with records revealing the experiment.

23.content: Zhara is the guardian of Okurov, a huge winged creature with leaf-feathers who attacks the Traveler and Paimon as supposed Badbugs. Her name is the Russian word for "heat" and her look nods to the Firebird of Russian fairy tales. She is a variant of the Immortal Construct, with a humanoid upper body and long blonde hair.

24.content: Nastya is a young girl found unconscious with tree branches growing from her head, escorted home by the Traveler. She admires Furiosa and Doctor Moreau, believes herself the cleverest child in town and cheerfully talks about catching Badbugs. The truth about her home slowly emerges during the quests.

25.content:
Frozen Fulgurbranch: The Frozen Fulgurbranch is a bolt of lightning that froze solid mid-fall above the House of Hesperides in Fellfrost Peak. It is a teleport waypoint on the way up to the Cloudborne Altar. The Snegovik Larisa's grief and fury, raised as a blizzard in her last hours, is said to have frozen it.

In the quest Bell Ringing at Dusk, Paimon notices the lightning is frozen and recalls that Aglaya told them the blizzard on the day Larisa died could freeze lightning mid-fall. The Eye of Graeae concludes the final site of Pavlina's ritual lies at the summit above the clouds.

Geography: A formation of frozen lightning shaped like a branch, with a teleport waypoint at its base, above the main mansion of the House of Hesperides. From here the climb continues to the Rumblebranch and then to the Cloudborne Altar.

The wiki lists the Rumblebranch as one of the area's exploration features. In the quest it is an ice branch that draws lightning down from the sky. Its upper branch is incomplete until the Traveler collects two smaller branches (Rumbletwigs), after which lightning begins to flow.

History: According to Pavlina's document in the mansion, Larisa's Prime Ice magic joined with her fury at her betrothed's desertion during the wedding ritual and raised a blizzard that stopped even the clouds and thunder. The wiki's Larisa page credits that blizzard with forming both this branch and the Cloudborne Palace.

Pavlina raced toward Larisa through the storm, but Larisa's body had become fragile and dissolved into snow-foam. Pavlina later used the lightning-bearing summit for her own ritual, drawing lightning and power from above.

Atmosphere: Eerie and sad: a thunderbolt held still in ice, a monument to one instant of rage. It is part of a storm that never ends.

Dangers: Paimon fears the lightning could fall on the Traveler, and the Eye of Graeae agrees it very well might; the quest warns the Traveler to be careful on the climb.

Quests: Bell Ringing at Dusk.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the branch remains frozen. Pavlina's ritual at the summit has been stopped.

26.content:
Frozen Royal Hall: The Frozen Royal Hall was the Belyi Tsar's throne room in the Pale Crown Palace. It still holds what the Eye of Graeae calls the very first Kresnik's Torch, a prototype that can be re-lit. The Traveler enters it in the quest The Stone Beasts, Like Ghouls Seated while looking for a fragment of the Eye's power.

The room is also guarded: lighting the torch wakes Zver, the Tsar's beast, which sends man-made chimeric monsters against intruders.

Geography: A hall behind a snow-buried gate, reached by a side route the Eye of Graeae identifies. A door inside the palace leads into the hall, and a statue must be returned to its place to open it. Inside there is a throne with a barrier in front of it, a prototype Kresnik's Torch, and a door behind the throne that stays shut until two stone statues of a two-headed beast, the guardian of the Tsar's corpse, are returned to a mechanism before the throne.

A tutorial for the "Prototype Kresnik's Torch" appears in this room. The torch's start mechanism no longer works, but a knock on its crystal component triggers an emergency startup. Later parts of the quest lead up a Suspended Tower and an elevator to Zver and on to the ruined Hvergelmir.

History: The Eye of Graeae says the torch is the first of its kind. The wiki's Kresnik's Torch page says the Belyi Tsar created the torches to help humans survive Snezhnaya's cold. When the Traveler lights it, a voice swears loyalty in the name of Zver and the guards attack. Once the statues are in position, a flashback plays: Aksinya reports to the Tsar that the first experiments are complete, that test subjects entered a realm of boundless joy, and that none woke up again; the Tsar asks if this is the world she dreams of, and Aksinya answers that his will is hers. He leaves for the front, saying Zver will go with him.

Notes by a Certain Noble Individual (I), found here, are credited by the wiki to the Tsar. The author writes of a passage that has opened at a heavy price, of the Shadow Realm being the ruins of Hyperborea, a lost homeland he has long sought, and of a long-time acquaintance he found already present there. The note does not name him.

People: No named residents. Zver, the Tsar's beast, appears at the end of the sequence. Aksinya and the Tsar are seen only in the flashback.

Atmosphere: A cold, grand and long-silent hall: ice over a throne, shut doors and carved beast statues, a torch that once warmed a court. The wiki shows two states, a cold one and a warm one after the torch is lit.

Dangers: Lighting the torch summons Chimeric Winged Elephants and other man-made monsters, the "stone beasts" of the quest title. The route up involves ice puzzles and more of the same enemies.

Quests: The Stone Beasts, Like Ghouls Seated.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the hall is still frozen apart from the torch the Traveler lit. No later content in the sources changes it.

27.content:
Garden Bathed in Radiant Dew: The Garden Bathed in Radiant Dew is a garden at the House of Hesperides in Fellfrost Peak, kept alive amid the blizzard. It thrived under the care of Larisa, a Snegurochka who died during her own wedding, and its great tree has borne no fruit since. A fragment of the Eye of Graeae's power is hidden in that tree.

The Snegovik guard Ladon keeps visitors out, saying the garden is under maintenance and open only to fae helpers.

Geography: A garden behind a guarded entrance, with a large tree at its centre. Prime Ice constructs stand among the plants and block the line of sight of the Jack Frosts who patrol it, which the Eye of Graeae points out the Traveler can exploit.

The garden can be viewed from outside, and the guard invites visitors to look from the entrance and tell him stories instead of entering.

People: Ladon, a Snegovik, stands guard at the entrance and is friendly and talkative. Jack Frosts work inside as helpers. Larisa, who is dead, used to come and do work there.

Ladon says that when Larisa was alive the big tree bore the biggest and most beautiful fruit. He has tried everything since her death and nothing makes it bear fruit again.

History: In the quest The Sun's Gilded Apple, the Eye of Graeae senses that a fragment of its power lies in the great tree. Paimon keeps Ladon talking while the Traveler sneaks around to the garden, avoids the Jack Frosts and takes the fragment (a Severed Fragment of Ikhor) from the tree.

Larisa is the Snegurochka who tended the plants and who, according to the wiki's profile, raised a blizzard in her final hours; the garden stands in that blizzard. The wiki gives her as a candidate for Grand Duchess whom her kin considered the most pure-minded among them.

Atmosphere: A hushed, carefully tended place that still carries the mark of the person who loved it; the guard is gentle and nostalgic rather than hostile.

Dangers: Jack Frosts patrol the grounds, and getting in takes stealth because Ladon will not allow visitors. If the timer in the quest runs out before the fragment is taken, the quest returns to its first step.

Quests: The Sun's Gilded Apple.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the garden is closed to the public for maintenance and the Traveler has taken the fragment from the tree.

28.content:
Glupov (also: City of Fools, Fatui Headquarters): Glupov is a fortress-city in Snezhnaya, described as a satellite city within Snezhnograd, and the headquarters of the Fatui. Its name means "the city of fools". Its present Mayor is Pulcinella, "The Rooster", the Fifth of the Fatui Harbingers.

In the 7.0 Archon Quest Alyosha describes it as the block adjacent to Zapolyarny Palace, "kind of a city in its own right", and says it contains the Armory Palace, a munitions factory. The Fatui raised it on the Tsaritsa Anastasya's command in the fourth year of the 799th Cycle, a year after she created the Fatui to take the lands of the rebellious fae princes.

History: In the first year of the 799th Cycle Anastasya was crowned Tsaritsa after the death of Emperor Monomakh, the Belyi Tsar. In the third year she used a new force, the Fatui, rather than the old Druzhna to subdue the princes who had defied her. In the fourth year she had the Fatui build a fortress near Snezhnograd and named it Glupov. The next significant act the same book records is the founding of the Snezhnograd Veche two years later.

The book that records this, A Brief History of the Pale Starborn, gives no further account of Glupov's construction. The Fatui have been described since as the organisation that acts as Snezhnaya's government, diplomatic corps and military, with the city as their base. Pulcinella's own profile ties him to both cities: he is Mayor of Snezhnograd and, per the Guiding Notes, of Glupov, and he took the Snezhnograd mayoralty after his mentor.

People: Mayor: Pulcinella. NPCs the wiki places in Glupov are ordinary Fatui personnel: Anton (former acting captain of the Ninth Company), Oktyabrskaya (field medic), Sereda (mess chef), Stepanyan, Tikhon (sapper), Trofimova (maintenance technician), Uspensky and Uvarov (trainees), Zinenko (quartermaster) and Zinoviy (drillmaster). They give the place a barracks feel: drills, canteens, repairs and recruits.

Atmosphere: Think of a fortress that is also a workplace: drill grounds and mess halls, orderly Fatui in uniform, field medics, sappers, trainees and a quartermaster going about their work. Pulcinella had a cold, stoic portrait of the Tsaritsa commissioned and, with her approval, hung through Glupov's halls, so her image presides over the place.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Glupov remains the Fatui's headquarters under Mayor Pulcinella. No later change to its role is established.

29.content:
Haeresys: Haeresys is an underground arena operated by the Fatui. It appears only in the official Genshin Impact manga, where captured test subjects are brought to fight unknown creatures as part of experiments.

Il Dottore and his menial Krupp carried out these experiments there. The manga's one named subject is Anthony, a boy from Mondstadt who was captured and entered as Contender 139. The place is not reachable in the game.

History: In the manga, Krupp first appears at Haeresys. Dottore calls his work pathetic and threatens to make Krupp a test subject too; Krupp saves himself by pointing out an invitation to Mondstadt's Ludi Harpastum festival, suggesting more subjects could be recruited from there. The pair then visit Dawn Winery, where Diluc is holding a party.

Later in the manga, Diluc interrogates Krupp in the winery basement and mentions Anthony, who had worked at a bakery in Mondstadt before being taken. Anthony was sent into the arena against an unidentified tentacled creature and died.

Atmosphere: A sealed underground arena with fights set up as experiments, overseen by a cold scientist and a frightened subordinate.

30.content:
Hall of Prayers (also: assembly hall, Grand Hall of Prayer, Koshchei's Hall): The Hall of Prayers, also called the assembly hall, is a ceremonial hall in the abandoned village of Okurov in Flamefeather Valley. The townspeople used to gather here and recite prayers that Doctor Moreau wrote for Zhara.

In the quest In the Dwelling of Life, the Traveler and Nastya reach it after defeating Furiosa near its bridge. Notes inside show that the doctor behind the prayers is actually Koshchei the Deathless.

Places: The hall is reached by lift and a bridge. Inside, the way forward is blocked by mechanisms the party must work: a chandelier on a rope, curtain switches and a locked door that Nastya opens. Beyond it lies the Teeming Mire.

History: Two sets of papers lie in the hall. The Yellowed Records are a researcher's notes about the fae, about bodies formed from trees that regrow and grow stronger but lose language, and about experiments carried out in the sewers; they say the next step is to get townspeople to accept the "treatment", with Furiosa as an example. Less-Than-Legible Notes describe a "final ceremony" in which everyone will be reborn from an embryo like the writer, argue that an eternal view makes pain and joy alike meaningless, and mention Aksinya. The Eye of Graeae compares the handwriting and identifies the author as Koshchei.

People: Furiosa guards the approach and had refused the doctor's "gift". Zhara, for whom the prayers were written, attacks the Traveler as a "Badbug". Nastya, a young child of the village, guides the Traveler and treats Furiosa as her idol.

Atmosphere: A grand but melancholy hall with heavy curtains and a chandelier, abandoned, its quiet broken only by echoing footsteps and the weight of what happened here.

Quests: The hall is the setting of Forbidding Doors of Melancholy, the fifth quest of In the Dwelling of Life. The next quest is To Rest in a Forgotten Field.

31.content:
House of Hesperides (also: Hesperides mansion, Hesperides manor, mountain manor of the Snegovik): The House of Hesperides is a remote mountain manor on Fellfrost Peak in Snezhnaya, the home of the Snegovik (snow fae) and their Grand Duchess. It was built thousands of years ago, and until Bell Ringing at Dusk it belonged to Pavlina, the Grand Duchess of the Snegurochka, who ruled its other residents.

In the quest series Hesperides of Love and Hate the manor hosts a 'wedding' that is really a ritual to give the Snegovik souls, with a human sacrifice as its price.

Geography: The manor stands alone on a snowy summit above the cloud line, reached by climbing the peak. It has a front hall, a main hall, a VIP lounge, an upper floor of private rooms and a rooftop, plus a chapel used for ceremonial 'rituals'. A garden and its courtyard surround the building, guarded by Jack Frosts.

Higher up the mountain the Cloudborne Altar and the Cloudborne Palace lie beyond the manor, where the final ritual takes place.

Places: Front Hall (reception), Main Hall (the wedding and entertainment), VIP Lounge, Mountain Mansion 2F (private rooms with the brittle document written by Pavlina), a rooftop with a hidden attic, the Chapel and the Garden Bathed in Radiant Dew. Kresnik Kristall, Kresnik's Torches, Prime Ice and a Rumblebranch are all found here.

The garden is out of bounds, 'under maintenance' except for fae help, and the Eye of Graeae's fragment is hidden there in the quest The Sun's Gilded Apple.

People: Residents and staff are Snegovik, with a few visitors. Aglaya is a Snegovik receptionist who appears after Bell Ringing at Dusk; Ladon bars the way into the garden; other named residents include Bogdana, Liubov, Pletnev, Raduzhnaya, Safonov, Saltykov and Taisiia in the Front Hall. Pavlina was the Grand Duchess of the Snegurochka.

Ikhor, a quest-exclusive young man whose appearance is that of the young Belyi Tsar and who is the 'groom' of the ritual, is one of the three fragments of the Eye of Graeae.

Governance: The Grand Duchess of the Snegurochka rules from here. According to the document written by Pavlina, the Snegovik ancestor Morevna decreed that the one leading the Snegovik must have a complete soul, which can only be gained through true love. When Pavlina was installed as princess no such love was required, which angered her.

Another Snegurochka, held in high esteem, told Pavlina at her ceremony that 'these things also happen'. Pavlina read this as meaning that Larisa's sacrifice had been pointless.

Culture: A Snegovik's love is described in Pavlina's document as a sacrifice, a voluntary exchange in which one gives all and expects the beloved to give all in return. Prime Ice artisanry, ceremonial skill and etiquette are valued, as are flower-tending and elegance.

Larisa, Pavlina's rival, said that the greatest misfortune in the world is to love no one at all.

History: According to the receptionist Raduzhnaya, the House of Hesperides was built thousands of years ago by the first Grand Duchess of the Snegovik, after the Belyi Tsar unified the north and set up the Pale Star Court.

Pavlina, who the wiki says had lived for centuries before the Cataclysm 500 years ago and was a researcher of Hvergelmir, later became Grand Duchess. She contended with Larisa for the title. Larisa brought a human to the manor to marry and complete her soul; he fled the ceremony and she died. Pavlina swore on Larisa's sword that her own wedding to Ikhor would succeed.

The ritual repeated for an unknown number of times, trapping the manor in a loop of Pavlina's wedding day, until she forgot Ikhor had willingly helped and shackled him instead. Aksinya appeared and objected; Pavlina warned that her tricks would only gain time before another ritual.

Atmosphere: The in-game viewpoint calls it 'a lonely mansion against the whiteout'. Guests are welcomed with entertainment and told the house's dos and don'ts; behind the festive surface is a ritual, and the mood tilts to uneasy once the ceremony begins.

Rooftop notes by a human named Myshkin describe days that never end.

Dangers: Chimeric armoured beasts on the approach, Glacial Wardens and Glaciomancers (Snegovik warriors and mages) inside, and Jack Frosts in the garden. When the ritual runs out of control, the manor's Snegovik turn on visitors.

Pavlina herself, the 'Guardian of the Hesperides', fights as a boss at the Cloudborne Altar.

Travel: Visitors need an invitation, which an Invitation to the 'Ritual' provides; it can be obtained in several ways in the open world. After the quests the receptionist and other Snegovik welcome guests as normal. A Teleport Waypoint at the Frozen Fulgurbranch and the Cloudborne Altar are unlocked in the series.

Quests: The World Quest series Hesperides of Love and Hate: Through the Gates of Ivory, Procrustes' Iron Bed (with sub-quests House of the Soulless and The Sun's Gilded Apple) and Bell Ringing at Dusk. It runs alongside On One Side a Palace, On the Other a Tomb and In the Dwelling of Life, and leads into An Ark That Used to Be a Soul.

In Through the Gates of Ivory, the Traveler follows Ikhor to the manor, shows the invitation at the statue, meets Aglaya, enjoys the entertainment and takes a seat in the chapel. In Procrustes' Iron Bed, Pavlina tries to sacrifice Ikhor but is thwarted by Aksinya, and out-of-control Snegovik must be defeated. In Bell Ringing at Dusk, the Traveler climbs through the clouds to the Cloudborne Altar and stops Pavlina.

Status as of 7.1: Open as of 7.1. Pavlina is gone, the loop is broken and Aglaya works at the reception. Patch notes for 7.1 mention a Jack Frost catching challenge and a time trial offered by an NPC named Vershina in the manor.

32.comment: House of Hesperides: Pavlina's Wedding Ritual
32.content:
Pavlina, Grand Duchess of the Snegurochka, performs a 'wedding' with Ikhor to gather the Eye of Graeae's scattered power and so give her people souls. The Snegovik lack souls, so she treats the marriage as a ritual of sacrifice. Aksinya and the Traveler stop it in Bell Ringing at Dusk.

In the document written by Pavlina, her bitterness over the doomed ceremony of Larisa's husband drives her. She swears that hers will not fail.

33.comment: House of Hesperides: Aglaya and Myshkin
33.content:
Aglaya is a Snegovik receptionist at the manor. She fell in love with Myshkin, a human who stayed in the manor, and during Pavlina's looping ritual they promised to flee together once the wedding was over. Myshkin grew old and died in a hidden attic.

Once the loop is broken Aglaya, who had forgotten his death, learns of it again. Notes found on the rooftop in his hand ask her to forget his name.

34.comment: House of Hesperides: Document with Yellowed Pages
34.content:
A stiff, brittle document in the second-floor rooms, written in Pavlina's cold hand. She says she has no love for Larisa, who equalled her in Prime Ice artisanry and surpassed her in ceremony, and whom every Snegovik loved. She watched Larisa choose a human lover, resented him, and then watched him flee the ritual, after which Larisa's body dissolved into snow in the storm.

After becoming princess, Pavlina resolves to find a way out of the rules that bind her kin, 'for Larisa, for whom I held no love'.

35.content:
Huntsman's Cabin (also: Hunter's Cabin, Workshop Beneath the Huntsman's Cabin): The Huntsman's Cabin is a cabin in the Volkodlak Tundra, Snezhnaya, where the hunter Alyosha's Meeting Point sits in a workshop beneath it. A fae gang once held it while guarding a prototype Kresnik's Torch and Shadow Realm antiques; after Alyosha and the Traveler clear it out, the torch warms a shelter for villagers who risk freezing.

In public Chaplina is credited with founding the shelter, while Alyosha keeps a low profile as a member of the Rokot.

Geography: The cabin stands on the snowy tundra. Behind a locked door and a freshly formed ice barrier lies a cavern leading to a hidden chamber with a Shadow Realm barrier device and a large machine, which proves to be a prototype Kresnik's Torch. The workshop beneath the cabin holds the Meeting Point. A pedestal found with the barrier opens the Firearm Accessory Archive.

Part of the ice must be melted with a basic heat source or Pyro to proceed, and a second set of pipes must be freed to get the furnace working.

Places: The cabin proper, the hidden cavern with its barrier, the furnace chamber warmed by the prototype Kresnik's Torch, and the workshop beneath the cabin where Alyosha's Meeting Point is. A Shadow Realm pedestal nearby opens the Firearm Accessory Archive once the Eye of Graeae establishes user permissions.

People: Alyosha, the young hunter, with his dog Tugarin. Chaplina, publicly the shelter's founder. NPCs in the workshop include Aksakov, Belsky, Bystrov, Plate, Serebrov, Whistle and Zhemchuzhina, and Trapeznikov appears after Remnants of the Shadow Realm. Bystrov is Belsky's father and is busy looking for work; Whistle is a strong dog who trained with Tugarin.

Trapeznikov, a friend of Alyosha in the Rokot, is an expert on Shadow Realm technology. Fae gang members in the story speak of an 'Old Sire' who is dead, of Zmei and Lady Voronina, and of the Izmaylov family and a High Table.

Governance: Fae gangs claim loot by their own rules, and the Rokot keep their involvement anonymous. Alyosha asks Chaplina to keep to the story that she established the shelter.

Culture: A hard-pressed rural community: villagers freeze, Kristall is scarce and smugglers trade in it. Alyosha, a hunter, goes after smugglers rumoured to have connections at the Royal Energy Commission, hoping to give their Kristall to freezing villagers, and calls himself 'just one crook robbing another'.

Alyosha tells the Traveler a hunter turns back once the prey is caught, while an adventurer goes the extra step further.

History: In Hunter on the Snowfields, Alyosha stalks a fae gang rumoured to hoard Kristall, and the Traveler joins him. They defeat the gang at the cabin, find a Shadow Realm Vault Access Card, melt a barrier, and discover Belyi Tsar era devices. A gang member returns with a modified detonator and is subdued by Tugarin.

Alyosha decides to use the prototype Kristall furnace as a shelter, rather than chase the gangs' schemes. The Traveler keeps the access card and the weapon parts found there.

Atmosphere: A snowbound hideout turned warm refuge: Alyosha says the furnace can warm the whole area, and villagers at risk of freezing are brought there.

Dangers: Volkodlak gang members (bashers, lobbers, sharpshooters and raiders), explosives rigged in the cavern and ice barriers.

Quests: World quests: Hunter on the Snowfields (unlocks the Meeting Point); Many Hands Make Light Work (requires Meeting Point level 5); Remnants of the Shadow Realm Parts 1 to 3 (unlocks the Firearm Accessory Archive); Childhood Happiness.

In Childhood Happiness, Belsky dog-sleds with Whistle while Alyosha fills in for Bystrov. In Many Hands Make Light Work, Chaplina reports the furnace burns Kristall more efficiently and that no gang members have come lately.

Status as of 7.1: The shelter is stable: output is steady, Kristall shortages persist, but the stock is enough pooled together, and no gang has returned.

36.comment: Huntsman's Cabin: The Prototype Kresnik's Torch
36.content:
The prototype is a furnace of the Belyi Tsar's era, heat-giving and stronger than any Kristall-powered furnace Alyosha has seen. The fae gang sought it for 'the plan' of their boss. Alyosha repurposes it to warm a shelter.

Chaplina says Kristall burns much more efficiently with this design, and the output stabilised after maintenance.

37.comment: Huntsman's Cabin: Alyosha and the Rokot
37.content:
Alyosha is a hunter and a member of the Rokot; he says keeping a low profile is a matter of principle. His dog Tugarin goes with him on hunts.

Trapeznikov, from the Rokot, helps decode the Shadow Realm pedestal and its archive.

38.content:
Hyperborea (also: Golden Hyperborea, Golden City, Hyperborean ruins): Hyperborea, called the Golden City, was a kingdom of Teyvat's ancient unified civilization, located where Snezhnaya lies today. Under the angel Koitar and the voyager Anacharsis it grew into a place of astonishing technology and then rose against the Heavenly Principles of Celestia. A Celestial Nail destroyed it, and its ruins sank into the Shadow Realm. Its survivors became the ancestors of the Frostmoon Scions of Nod-Krai.

Hyperborea is not a place the Traveler can simply walk to. Only fragments appear in the game: a ruined sacred structure with murals in a quest domain (Phantom of the Sanctuary, 6.2) and the Shadow Realm ruins that the Belyi Tsar and the Hvergelmir institute later explored.

Geography: Hyperborea stood in the far north, in the region that is now Snezhnaya. In its prime it was a prosperous city with a holy citadel and a golden tower; accounts hint it may have been a main centre with satellite cities around it. At the end of its history the whole region and its ley lines were frozen by Prime Ice, which is credited as the origin of Snezhnaya's icy landscape. Its ruins now lie in the Shadow Realm as a place of white dust and storms with no true substance in it.

The Belyi Tsar's notes describe walking through a storm of fine white dust to reach a strange castle among the ruins, and say that the Shadow Realm's interior is the reverse of what happens outside, with none of the Abyss's foul blood found there. Part of Hyperborea can be visited as the quest domain Phantom of the Sanctuary on Hiisi Island, whose ruined sacred place and murals show Nibelung with the weaponised Three Moons and the moons shattered after the War of Funerary Flame, with only the Frost Moon intact.

Places: Known features are the holy citadel, the golden tower that the Elysium Project tried to extend up to Celestia, and the sanctuary of the moons. The high priest held the sacred weapon Dawnstar of Shahar, given by Koitar. The Hyperborean facility later called the Phantom of the Sanctuary is a surviving structure.

Hyperborean devices recovered by later ages include the SAMPO orb, which rearranges matter at the subatomic scale to produce limitless food; the Arrow of Terpikeraunas, a weapon that solidifies Light Realm energy and fires it; flying vehicles; and time capsules powered by the primordial forces of Teyvat. One capsule held an infant, Aksinya, who survived the city's fall in suspended animation.

People: Koitar, an Archangel of Celestia, and Anacharsis, an interstellar voyager who took possession of a young man there, led the city in its last decades. Other angels such as Nicole lived among the Hyperboreans. The people were human, and they created the Snowland Fae as attendants.

After the fall, survivors who had been far from the cities fled into a cold wasteland, and a few angels like Nicole guided them to safety. The goddess Canon led them to Nod-Krai, where they became the Frostmoon Scions. Aksinya, the Hyperborean infant later raised by the Belyi Tsar, is the other known survivor of the city itself. Hyperborean names are said to derive from Old Iranian, Avestan or Ancient Greek roots.

Governance: Originally the city followed the Heavenly Principles and took guidance from their divine envoys, and Koitar was its link to Celestia. Once Anacharsis and Koitar chose defiance, they ruled as its leaders and directed the city's plans together.

The chief priest was the one who sent Anacharsis, then a young debater who had refuted the city's arguments, to Koitar to plead the case. Koitar's crown, a shackle placed by the Heavenly Principles, shattered when Anacharsis told her the secrets of the world's origins; the two pledged themselves to each other and swore an oath of defiance witnessed by the Three Moons.

Culture: Hyperboreans prized knowledge and made unprecedented advances after receiving secret knowledge from the angels and from Anacharsis. They built their own scientific vocabulary, such as Tekhneikos processes and Mekhaneikos apparatuses, to record their work. They honoured the moons, and their religion and name later echoed through the Frostmoon Scions.

Their knowledge covered bioengineering, including the forbidden creation of new life, and genetics (the Sanctum of the Oathbearer notes mention phenotypic stability and inbreeding depression). They also dreamed of breaching the False Sky to explore the sea of stars. A Tower of Ipsissimus description attributed to the Narzissenkreuz Ordo names Hyperborea as the first stage of human spiritual evolution, symbolising the loss of paradise.

History: Roughly 6,000 years ago Anacharsis arrived and, with Koitar, started projects meant to save the city from a fate the Heavenly Principles had already decreed: the Elysium Project (a paradise for humanity without divine blessing or judgement), the Shadow Realm, the creation of the Snowland Fae and the Primordial Human project. The last, using the remains of the Cryo Dragon, failed to contain its power; thirty years after Anacharsis' arrival Prime Ice covered the region and the Heavenly Principles launched a Celestial Nail. The Hyperboreans faced it with their arrows aimed at Celestia, joined, according to item texts, by dragons. The city was destroyed and sank into the Shadow Realm.

Hyperborea's fall led directly into the War of Funerary Flame, when the dragons carried on fighting Celestia and were joined by their returned king Nibelung. Afterwards the Heavenly Principles expelled and cursed the angels for Koitar's rebellion: she lost her memories and the others had to give up wisdom or power. About a thousand years later Monomakh stepped out of the Cryo Dragon's remains and became the Belyi Tsar of the later Pale Star Court. His expeditions into the Shadow Realm found the Hyperborean ruins, which showed him what he was and set his fate toward becoming the Cryo Archon. The Frostmoon Scions built a tower in Nod-Krai to preserve Mekhaneikos devices and attempted the generations-long Sacred Heir Project; five hundred years ago Aila reformed the faith, erasing mentions of Hyperborea in favour of Kuutar and kindness.

Atmosphere: A scene in the ruins is white, hushed and strange: fine white dust in motion, great storms, a silence in which every machine seems to be listening. Sight of the golden tower or the moons would feel more sorrowful than grand, because every visible trace belongs to a civilisation that chose to meet its end on its feet.

Dangers: The Shadow Realm, where the ruins now lie, is not threatened by Abyss contamination, but it is a place of storms, trapped memories and isolation, and travellers can be pulled out of time into past scenes. Wilderness Hunters, the warriors' spirits corrupted by Abyssal taint, remain a hazard.

Travel: Hyperborea is not accessible in the open world. A fragment appears in the Phantom of the Sanctuary domain during the Nod-Krai Archon Quest (6.2), and the Hyperborean ruins in the Shadow Realm are discussed in Pale Crown Palace texts (7.0).

Quests: Where Does Her Name Rest? (Nod-Krai Archon Quest) takes the party into the Phantom of the Sanctuary; The wiki also cites Ripples That Will Never Reach, Light and Shadow, Intertwined and The First Sliver of Moonlight for Hyperborean history. The Snezhnaya chapter (7.0) adds the Belyi Tsar's notes and the Hvergelmir material.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Hyperborea remains destroyed. No Hyperboreans live in the ruins and its history is held mainly by the Frostmoon Scions, the Belyi Tsar's notes and fragmentary item text.

The Belyi Tsar's Hvergelmir institute, led by his ward Aksinya, once mined the ruins for knowledge. Aksinya remains trapped in the Shadow Realm after the Traveler defeated her in the Snezhnaya world quest series that ends at the Pale Crown Palace (7.0).

39.content: Anacharsis, an interstellar voyager, cast his consciousness into Teyvat about 6,000 years ago and possessed a young Hyperborean man, then won debates against the city's thinkers and was sent to the Archangel Koitar. Learning from him the secrets of the world, Koitar doubted Celestia; her crown of the Heavenly Principles shattered and the two pledged themselves to each other. They launched the Elysium Project, which aimed to turn Teyvat into a paradise without relying on the Heavenly Principles, and prepared for war. When the Celestial Nail fell, Koitar urged Anacharsis to return to his own world, and she declared war on the Heavenly Principles from the steps of the golden tower.

40.content: The Primordial Human project, a bid to create a being rivalling the Heavenly Principles from the remains of the Cryo Dragon, failed to contain the dragon's innate power; Prime Ice froze the region and its ley lines. The Heavenly Principles answered with a Celestial Nail. Hyperboreans spent their last hours arming themselves, even the newborn fae, and the dragons joined their rebellion. The Nail killed the vast majority of the population and vaporised most of the fae; the city fell into the Shadow Realm.

41.content: Hyperborean engineers wrote about Tekhneikos processes and Mekhaneikos apparatuses. They created the Snowland Fae by engraving the Frost Moon's light on the bones of giant beasts, tried to engineer elemental augmented humans, built the SAMPO to make food, the Arrow of Terpikeraunas to turn Light Realm energy into projectiles, and sophisticated time capsules. Later explorers from Hvergelmir recovered such devices and adapted them into firearms; the Leshy, a late creation, is noted as a more stable form of life than the fae made with Embryonic-Ichoric-Telluric-Rudiment.

42.comment: Hyperborea: Survivors and the Frostmoon Scions
42.content: Those who survived were away from the cities. Canon pitied them and led them to Nod-Krai, according to legend giving them antlered crowns. They named themselves the Frostmoon Scions in her honour and kept their beliefs after her death. They built a tower in Nod-Krai holding Mekhaneikos devices and pursued the Sacred Heir Project, an effort to breed a prophesied heir to Elysium. Its disastrous results five hundred years ago led Aila to reform the faith, replacing Hyperborea with dedications to nature, kindness and the newborn goddess Kuutar.

43.content:
Inverted Glacier: The Inverted Glacier is a Domain of Blessing in the Everfrozen Earth, the northern tundra of Snezhnaya. The domain text describes a barren mountain scourged by endless winter storms, where neither monsters nor outlaws can survive long in the ancient, desolate cold. Scoundrels who dwell there guard precious artifacts for anyone able to beat them.

The domain's longer description draws on fae legend: in the oldest tales the dead tundra was once covered in lush greenery and the frozen sea ran with sweet honey. Not even the eldest fae ever saw that paradise. Everywhere the eye turns there are only blizzards that grind down the land and the fragile but stubborn souls clinging to it. It was added in version 7.0 with the Snezhnaya region.

In game the domain pays out artifacts (Scarlet Proof, Heart of the Furnace, The Exile and Brave Heart) and is staffed with Volkodlak Bashers, Glaciomancers, Glacial Wardens and several Chimeric beasts (a winged elephant, burrowbeast, armoured beast and horned bear). Its Ley Line Disorder rewards Cryo-related reactions with a team-wide Elemental Mastery boost. These are labelled game mechanics, not lore.

Atmosphere: Howling storm and bare, ice-scoured rock; a place that feels lifeless and old. A scene here should stress cold, wind and the sense of a promised green land that no one alive ever saw.

Dangers: Eternal winter storms; Volkodlak outlaws; Glaciomancers and Glacial Wardens; aberrant Chimeric beasts. The domain text says neither monster nor outlaw can long survive the cold, and that scoundrels lurk there.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 it is a permanent domain in Snezhnaya. Canon gives no named occupant, owner or history beyond the flavour text.

44.content:
Jack Frost Village (also: Fae's Hidden Settlement): Jack Frost Village is the hidden homeland of the Jack Frosts, a small settlement on Fellfrost Peak in Snezhnaya. It was recently under siege by Volkodlaks until the Traveler helped the villagers fend them off, and it is the former home of the Geo Jack Frost Lumi, who now travels with Linnea.

The Jack Frosts here cannot speak in sentences; they cry 'Ya-ho' and gesture. The village head, a somewhat larger Jack Frost, can write brief words on a wooden slate.

Geography: The village lies on Fellfrost Peak, the great snow-sloped mountain south of Snezhnograd.
