Volkodlaks reach it along at least two paths into the settlement, which is why the Jack Frosts wanted defences along those routes. Its waypoint stands in the village; a broken igloo to the north-east holds a discarded Jack Frost disguise.

The siege defence uses Prime Ice constructs: snowball launchers and blockade spikes that the Traveler sets up as Prime Ice constructs.

People: The Jack Frost Village Head, who answers to 'Chief' and says that is both his job and his name, speaks in broken words written on a slate ('Volkodlaks. Invaded. Bullied.'). Other Jack Frosts include one in a blue three-pointed hat, one who looks confused and several that are stuck in snow when the Traveler arrives. After the defence, the Jack Frosts open a goods shop run from the village.

Lumi is the best-known former resident. Unlike other Jack Frosts she looks earthy (Geo), and she was bullied for standing out: other Jack Frosts chased her from her sleeping places and took her food. Linnea found her and, after working up the courage, asked whether she would travel with her; Lumi agreed and left her disguise at her old home here.

Dangers: Volkodlaks raid the village, take what they like and leave a mess. They say they will return with the whole pack, which is why the Traveler helps build a second layer of defences.

Quests: The World Quest 'Small Jack Frost, Big Problems' starts when the Traveler frees two trapped Jack Frosts. It leads to the Prime Ice defences, three waves of Volkodlak attackers and, at the end, the unlocking of the Jack Frosts' Goodies Shop. Linnea's Alcyon Chapter later adds the 'Strange Jack Frost's Paper Bag' near the broken igloo (the wiki flags the exact trigger as unverified).

Status as of 7.1: Inhabited by Jack Frosts as of 7.1. Its defences hold, and it has a shop open to adventurers.

45.comment: Jack Frost Village: Lumi and Linnea at Jack Frost Village
45.content: Lumi lived at the village before Linnea. A Jack Frost with Geo colouring, she was teased by her kin and used a cardboard disguise at times. Linnea met her here, and Lumi eventually joined her travels; their story is told in Linnea's profile and the Alcyon Chapter.

46.content:
Jack Frosts' Goodies Shop (also: Goodies Shop, Jack Frost goodies shop): The Jack Frosts' Goodies Shop is a trading post in Jack Frost Village where Jack Frosts swap goods they treat as "goodies" for uniquely crafted precision buttons. It is run by the Jack Frost Village Head.

Mora means nothing to the Jack Frosts: the village head says it is heavy and bad, while buttons are light and pretty to wear. The shop becomes available after the Traveler helps the village in Small Jack Frost, Big Problems.

People: The Jack Frost Village Head is a somewhat large Jack Frost who communicates by writing short messages on a wooden slate, calling itself simply the village chief. It uses its own words, calling buttons "bite-ons".

History: In the quest, Volkodlak had invaded the village and bullied the Jack Frosts. Helping them earns the Traveler a first handful of buttons and unlocks the shop. The Eye of Graeae then records a message about the buttons that Jack Frosts love.

Gameplay: Game mechanics: the shop sells various materials and other items, including a Construct appearance, in exchange for Intricately Patterned Buttons; the quest awards ten buttons.

47.content:
The Korolevskiy Theater (also: Korolevskiy Theater, Korolevskiy Theatre, Royal Theater of Snezhnograd): The Korolevskiy Theater is the main theater of Snezhnograd, where the Korolevskiy Troupe stages ballet, opera and musical performances. It is favoured by the Fatui Harbingers and by Mitya, and it is the daily base of the prima ballerina Odette and the prima donna Vodyanitsa. Odette's Meeting Point is in the dressing room behind the stage.

In the Version 7.0 Archon Quest Wraith's Nocturne a snowstorm traps the Traveler and the audience in the theater, where people begin dying one by one.

Geography: The theater sits in Snezhnograd. The interior has a lobby with four purple sofas, an auditorium with 44 blue three-seat sofas for a capacity of 312, a stage, a dressing room behind it, an administrative room and a cellar that opens during Winter's Mysterious Silence.

Security is tight: staff such as Kulish inspect every visitor at the entrance, since Snezhnaya's business and political leaders pass through.

People: Odette (prima ballerina) and Vodyanitsa (prima donna) are the Troupe's stars. Staff in the Archon Quests include Kulish (entrance inspection) and Dymov; the theater's NPCs inside include Arkady, Istomina, Ksenia, Leanid, Lev, Marat, Olenina and Taisia, and the wider area has Balkonov, Osipova, Pisemsky and others. Chugunov, a factory owner, attends performances.

Valeriy comes looking for Mitya, who hides in the theater when he should be at the Armory Palace. After the incident, dialogues may include Tartaglia, Vesna, Alyosha, Mitya and Arlecchino and Sandrone in the open world.

Culture: The official description says the relentless toil backstage is secondary to giving the audience a momentary escape into a beautiful illusion. The Troupe's repertoire includes the classic Snezhnayan ballet 'Spirit Seeker' and the new 'Black Snow Swan', a test of dancers' technique and emotional understanding.

Odette's schedule collides with the Fatui missions she insists on taking; Vodyanitsa nags her to rest.

Atmosphere: A well-guarded public theater: visitors queue for ticket and security checks, wealthy patrons like Chugunov grumble at latecomers, and a performance leaves the audience entranced. During the afterlife incident the same hall turns into shelter against a relentless storm, where people sleep wherever they find space, eat the food Vodyanitsa hands out and gather on the stage each night.

History: The wiki speculates the name comes from Nepla Korolevitsna, the late wife of the fae Filipov, but this is not confirmed.

Opening night of 'Spirit Seeker' in Wraith's Nocturne brings a rehearsal and group photo, after which a blizzard prevents anyone leaving. Over several days the staff and audience die in pairs, then singly, Mitya's reasoning leading to the conclusion that everyone is dead and living in an afterlife theater, an echo of Ronova's Curse of Death. When Ronova's disguise is destroyed, everyone wakes in the real world, with the theater's Ley Lines letting people keep memories.

Quests: Archon Quest: Silence Alone is Disfavored (Alyosha brings the Traveler to a performance and then to the greenroom), and Wraith's Nocturne (The White Curtain Falls, Lelek's Confession, Winter's Mysterious Silence, Wraith's Nocturne, Mistilteinn). World quests include Variations on Belyi and Chernyi and the quest 'One Yet to Take a Bow'.

Variations on Belyi and Chernyi has the Traveler help schedule Odette's days before the 'Black Snow Swan' premiere. In 7.1 One Move Left to Make brings a captured suspect, dragged back from Central Station, to the theater.

Status as of 7.1: Open and running performances. Odette's Meeting Point is in the dressing room, and open-world dialogue with the Troupe and visitors unlocks after Mistilteinn.

48.comment: The Korolevskiy Theater: The Afterlife Theater Incident
48.content:
During a rehearsal of 'Spirit Seeker', Ronova's Curse of Death kills everyone in the theater and gathers them in an afterlife theater, where they believe a snowstorm keeps them inside. The dead appear to be murdered in pairs during the night. The Traveler learns that Mitya, Shram (a ghost from the past), and a girl calling herself Tonia, really named Ptashka, are among the dead, and that the extra person in the staff logbook was Shram. Odette admits she is Lelek, the Rokot's infamous member.

The incident ends when Mitya and the Traveler unmask Ronova, who had taken on the form of Alyosha. Everyone awakens, though Mitya's carved symbol on his soul lets him remember. Chugunov says that he will shut down his factory.

49.comment: The Korolevskiy Theater: Variations on Belyi and Chernyi
49.content:
A world quest in the theater in which the Traveler helps plan Odette's schedule for two weeks before the Black Snow Swan premiere. Vodyanitsa complains that Odette keeps taking Fatui monster-slaying missions during rehearsal time.

Odette picks the Traveler because they proved trustworthy while trapped together in the theater, and because they know how the Fatui operate; Vodyanitsa objects that she has known Odette far longer.

50.content:
Kresnik's Burning Heart (also: Ever-Burning Hearth Core, Central Kresnik's Torch chamber): Kresnik's Burning Heart is a large chamber under the central plaza of Snezhnograd, the capital of Snezhnaya. It holds the nation's most important Kresnik's Torch, a furnace that burns Kresnik Kristall ore to keep the city habitable. Staff of the Royal Energy Commission work there.

It is the central Torch referred to in-world as the most important in all of Snezhnaya. A map viewpoint at the site is titled "Ever-Burning Hearth Core".

Geography: The chamber lies beneath the central plaza of Snezhnograd, in the Everfrozen Earth area of Snezhnaya. The Torch inside is far larger than the small "civilian model" Torches scattered across the country and the medium ones found in towns, and is described by an attendant as an enormous machine that needs constant human upkeep.

Kresnik Kristall reaches it by rail from the mines of Novokitezhgrad, according to the attendant Yelagina.

People: Five open-world NPCs of the Royal Energy Commission work here as of 7.0 to 7.1:
- Zarechnaya, the Acting Chair (sent temporarily from Zapolyarny Palace);
- Zaretsky, the Vice President, who carries much of the real workload;
- Zavyalov, a staff member who knew the late president well;
- Zybina, an overworked technician-type employee;
- Yelagina, who keeps the day-to-day log of the Torch.

Mood among them: the previous president, the Domovoy Izmaylov, has died, and staff talk about him fondly (Zavyalov and Zybina) or with unease about what he left behind (Zaretsky, Zarechnaya). Zybina says a former "technical expert" colleague was reassigned elsewhere, leaving her alone with technical problems.

Governance: Responsibility for the Torches and for the transport and use of Kresnik Kristall lies with the Royal Energy Commission of Snezhnaya. The Commission's leadership is currently an acting chair appointed by the palace rather than a permanent president.

History: According to Yelagina, construction of the central Torch began almost immediately after the Belyi Tsar completed his experiments in the Pale Crown Palace; it has run ever since, kept going by generations of workers. Loading-screen text credits the Belyi Tsar with building the Torches to help humans survive Snezhnaya's cold. The Prototype Torches remain in the Pale Crown Palace.

The viewpoint text records a saying that the Belyi Tsar himself granted ordinary people the right to use Kresnik Kristall, and that to Snezhnayans he was both the biting frost and the dawn that brought warmth.

Atmosphere: A warm, industrial interior in contrast to the blizzards above, with the steady hum of a furnace and staff completing logs, paperwork and maintenance. The tone is bureaucratic and a little uneasy: grieving colleagues, an acting chair who senses things have been "carefully hidden", and a deputy who sighs about gangs and the High Table.

Dangers: Zavyalov notes that Commission staff travelling to maintain Torches sometimes stumble into the Shadow Realm; the rule is to get out safely and report it to the Druzhna. This is a hazard of the job in general, not a danger inside this chamber.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Torch is running normally and the Commission is under Acting Chair Zarechnaya after the sudden death of its long-serving president. The NPCs say he died of illness; his death is treated differently in quest content, so do not assert a cause from the chamber staff alone.

51.content: Kresnik's Torch is an artificial heat source that burns Kresnik Kristall ore. Most Snezhnayan cities are built around one or more large Torches, which hold a Normal Temperature Zone against the storms; small civilian Torches stand across the land. The most important one is in Kresnik's Burning Heart beneath Snezhnograd. The Royal Energy Commission maintains them. Loading-screen text credits the Belyi Tsar with building them for humans.

52.comment: Kresnik's Burning Heart: Royal Energy Commission staff of the central Torch
52.content: Open-world NPCs at Kresnik's Burning Heart: Yelagina (Torch log-keeper), Zarechnaya (Acting Chair), Zaretsky (Vice President), Zavyalov and Zybina (staff). All were affected by the death of the previous president, the Domovoy Izmaylov. Their remarks are idle conversation: the hints of hidden ledgers or leftover problems are speculation voiced by the characters, not confirmed plot.

53.content:
Kuznets (also: Kuznets smithy, Kuznets Workshop): "Kuznets" ("Blacksmith") is the smithy in Snezhnograd run by Kuzmichev, a domovoy blacksmith. It sits near the city's front gate.

Kuzmichev forges and sells weapons and takes pride in quality: he keeps checking his furnace temperature because, he says, small differences decide whether a weapon succeeds or fails.

People: Kuzmichev is a domovoy who works as the town's smith. He is proud and jovial and addresses customers as "dear customer". He tells of once tapping a boastful man's cheek with a shovel until the man could barely summon any Prime Ice, as his argument that steel in hand beats relying on Prime Ice alone.

He has dealings with Alyosha the hunter, who asked him for hunting traps. The wiki also notes a bulletin-board message hinting that Kuzmichev is in his fifties.

Culture: Smithing here is a craft of temperature and detail. The shop is a place where weapons are bought, commissioned and made, in a city where many people also rely on Prime Ice for protection.

Gameplay: Game mechanics: Kuzmichev forges certain four-star weapons and weapon-enhancement materials, and sells low-rarity weapons and forging diagrams.

54.content:
Kvasnik (also: Kvasnik beverage shop): Kvasnik is a well-known beverage shop in Zolnyy, the Ash District of Snezhnograd, run by Zyryanov, a volkodlak. Its map description says the owner always claims that only his shop serves the most authentic kvass.

The same text adds a wry note: long-lived locals all know the drink came first, and only then did the shop named after it appear. The word kvasnik is also Russian for a traditional ceramic vessel used to store and serve kvass.

People: Zyryanov, a volkodlak, owns the shop. He calls out his "tasty and affordable" drinks, offers free ice-cream samples, and says he came up with a new ice-cream recipe himself.

Zyryanov reacts differently to famous Snezhnayan visitors: he stammers with nervous respect when Odette appears, and he greets Alyosha as someone he knows, asking how his last hunt went.

Culture: Kvass is an everyday Snezhnayan drink, and shops like this are neighbourhood fixtures where affordability matters. The shop also sells food and recipes.

Gameplay: Game mechanics: the stock of food refreshes daily; a daily free ice cream is offered, and Snezhnayan party members trigger unique themed ice creams.

55.content:
Lofty Clock Tower: The Lofty Clock Tower is a bell tower at the House of Hesperides, the Snegovik mountain manor in Fellfrost Peak. It stands on the manor's upper floors and holds large bells that can be rung. A guardian named Tsvetaev, an "Expedition Returner", defends it.

Canon material for it is thin: the wiki describes it only as a bell tower, and its significance comes from a hidden exploration objective, A Secret in the Chimes (an unofficial name).

Geography: The tower is on the third floor level of the mountain mansion (Mountain Mansion 3F map level). The gate cannot be opened before the objective is done. After the fight the Traveler uses a link mechanism to reach the top, uses the Eye of Graeae to remove a Prime Ice surface, and drops down to ring bells.

Ringing the bells guides a Seelie, which unlocks Elemental Monuments that are then activated, opening chests below. Ringing one of the bells at the top of the tower for the first time earns an achievement the wiki lists as "Wedding Bell".

People: Tsvetaev, a Glacial Warden labelled "Expedition Returner", guards the tower. He says visitors should not enter without leave. When defeated he wonders when he will hear "the true bell" again.

History: The sources say nothing of the tower's origin. The wiki says only that it is a bell tower at the House of Hesperides.

Completing A Secret in the Chimes yields the achievement "For Whom It Tolls" and unlocks one of the five paintings needed for the separate hidden objective Paintings of Hesperides.

Atmosphere: A tall, echoing tower of chimes in a house famous for ceremony; guarded by a polite but firm sentinel.

Dangers: The Glacial Warden fight at the entrance. Tsvetaev says mid-fight that the clock tower is "the only thing that..." but the line is cut off in the wiki record and flagged there as unverified.

Quests: No quest in the quest category. Only the hidden objective A Secret in the Chimes uses it.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the tower is a visitable bell tower with bells that can be rung; no later content changes it.

56.content:
Morepesok (also: Sea-Sand): Morepesok ("Sea-Sand") is a fishing settlement on the northern coast of Snezhnaya, in the Everfrozen Earth, and the hometown of Tartaglia (Childe), the Eleventh Fatui Harbinger. Boats go out from its harbor and a railway station links it to the rest of the country. Tartaglia's family, including his sister Tonia and youngest brother Teucer, lives here.

Fishing is the way of life, and the fisherfolk are proud of it: they compare catches after each outing, and the biggest catch earns the most respect. The official description jokes that the surest shortcut to impressing them is to be a Fatui Harbinger, which Tartaglia is.

Geography: Morepesok sits on the frozen northern shore of the Everfrozen Earth, the area that holds Snezhnograd. Its two public hubs are a harbor, where fishing boats and a larger ship, the "Sea Tsar", dock, and a train station that connects it to inland Snezhnaya. The Expedition text singles out the birch trees that grow in this part of the north.

Ice fishing is practised here as well as sea fishing (Tartaglia plans an ice-fishing trip with Teucer in one of his anecdotes). A tunnel and old railway line leading from Morepesok's station toward the abandoned town of Okurov in Flamefeather Valley are the subject of a local rumour (see the Okurov entry below).

Places: Harbor: fishing boats and the ship "The Sea Tsar", whose captain is Vyazemskaya and first mate Yazykov. Train station: a platform area with a waypoint, where the engineer Jary and his fiancee Vinezka can be met. Tartaglia's Home: the family house, where Tonia and Teucer are found. A fishing-supplies vendor, Zherebtsov, works as the local angler.

People: Named residents include Dozorov, Gorchakov, Gorshkov, Lugovskoy, Rakitina, Razumovsky and Shatalov, plus Tartaglia's siblings Tonia and Teucer. At the harbor: Korsakov, Pweza, Smirnova, Vyazemskaya and Yazykov. At the station: Jary, Vinezka and Znamensky. The sources read give little more than names for most of them.

The Tartaglia family is the best-known household. In Tartaglia's character stories his father worried about the third son, who as a boy kept stirring up fights around the village. Tartaglia now brings home gifts and medicine for his family and has said that missing a family dinner for a mission weighs on him.

Economy: Fishing supplies the village; the ship and station also move goods and people. Burtsev, a resident of Sretomorozsk, says he has family in Morepesok who can buy about twice his town's allotment of Kresnik Kristall, hinting that the coast is better supplied than the inland borderlands. Tartaglia, however, says life in Morepesok is not going well either under the energy policy of Project Stuzha.

Culture: Seafaring pride is central: a good catch is respected, and official text calls the local fisherfolk warriors who face the raging sea in simple fishing craft and do not flinch before sea monsters the size of mountains. Treat this as local self-image and tall-tale tone, not a documented bestiary.

Atmosphere: Cold wind off the grey northern sea, moored boats creaking, birches on the shore and an unhurried railway halt; people who talk about catches the way others talk about weather. This is an atmospheric suggestion, not a canon description.

History: The sources read give no founding history for Morepesok. What canon records is Tartaglia's youth here: as a boy he ran away at fourteen into the snowy forest, fell into an Abyss-touched chasm and was trained there by a mysterious swordswoman before being found by his mother and sisters. When he came home he brought fights and squabbles to the village.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Morepesok is a living fishing town. Tartaglia visits when his duties allow and, in the Travelers' Tales anecdotes added in 7.1, is shown buying gifts, planning to take Teucer ice fishing and promising Tonia to stay home longer next time.

He told the Traveler he is from Morepesok while discussing Project Stuzha in Snezhnograd (Archon Quest Chapter VII, Act I). No attack on, or disaster at, Morepesok is shown up to 7.1.

57.content:
Tartaglia's Home is the Tartaglia family house in Morepesok. Tonia and Teucer, his sister and youngest brother, are found here. Their personal details belong to their own entries.

In the 7.1 anecdote "Tartaglia: A Promise", he hands Tonia a bag with their father's medicine and snacks for Teucer and says he will follow once his work is done and stay longer this time; Tonia answers that their mother has been asking after him and that he must not let the family down again.

58.content: Three hidden Travelers' Tales anecdotes (Snowstride Chapter, 7.1) are set in Morepesok. In "Back Home" Tartaglia, at the station, sorts out tickets for Tonia, toys for Teucer, a scarf for his mother and boots for his father as apology gifts for missing the last family dinner because of a sudden mission. In "Ice Fishing" he is at the harbor, free for once, gathering gear for an ice-fishing trip and deciding to take Teucer along, which means he needs extra stove fuel. "A Promise" takes place at the family house (see Tartaglia's Home).

59.comment: Morepesok: The Okurov rumour at Morepesok Station
59.content: At the station the engineer Jary has been hired by outsiders to blast open a tunnel toward the abandoned town of Okurov. His fiancee Vinezka begs him not to go, citing the local belief that nobody who enters Okurov ever comes back and a tale of a beautiful firebird that lures people deep into the valley. Jary says he is bound by a contract with a heavy penalty. The Traveler can take over the job, which starts the World Quest series "In the Dwelling of Life".

60.content:
Nastya's Home: Nastya's Home is a house in the abandoned village of Okurov where the young girl Nastya lived with her mother. "Nastya's Home" is an unofficial name for the place.

In Back on One's Feet, Nastya points to it and says she and her mother used to live there. The Traveler can enter it after a hidden exploration objective about a being called "Shar".

Places: Inside the house is a worn old photograph of Nastya with her mother. After the quest Chorus of Solace, a blue algae in the house also plays Nastya's thoughts.

People: The only NPC is "Shar", whose name is the Russian word for "ball". It resembles a Juvenile Tree Segment, with clothing and a red ribbon attached to its branch. In its dialogue it repeatedly says new friends can be family too; if the Traveler declines it says it will play with the doll alone.

Through the blue algae Nastya says the little bed, blanket, pillow and toys are now used by "another life", and that although her mother's hug feels different she can feel her mother's hand stroking her hair.

History: Nastya and her mother lived in Okurov, a village closed off from the rest of Snezhnaya. Other residents included Furiosa and Zhara. Nastya remembers a doctor called Moreau, who is actually Koshchei. By the time of the quest line she says she has slept for an unknown time, and most of the villagers have gone missing.

Atmosphere: A small, quiet house with a child's bed and toys, a family photograph, and an unsettling companion who treats the Traveler as a new member of the family.

61.content:
Novokitezhgrad (also: New Kitezh, New Kitezhgrad, New Kitezh City): Novokitezhgrad ('New Kitezh') is a city in Snezhnaya southeast of Snezhnograd. It is famed for its liquor and its mining, above all of Kresnik Kristall, and many Snowland fae live there alongside humans. It was founded to replace Kitezhgrad, the old imperial capital destroyed by the Abyss. Players cannot visit it as of 7.1.

Its Kristall travels from here by rail to the rest of the country. A character named Netochka says she even saw Novokitezhgrad liquor being drunk in Nod-Krai and that 'we' are known for liquor as much as mining, which suggests she speaks as someone from the city or its region.

Geography: Southeast of Snezhnograd. The trail between Nasha Town and Novokitezhgrad is called a tough one by Tolfin, a character in a Nod-Krai quest.

People: Humans live alongside plenty of Snowland fae. Netochka remarks that she assumed there would be plenty of fae in other places too, 'like back home'.

The Domovoy Grand Duke Alvis oversaw the construction of the city.

Economy: Two industries stand out: liquor and mining. Most Kresnik Kristall, which heats Snezhnaya, is mined here and sent out by rail, under oversight of the Royal Energy Commission.

Alvis had monopolised mining in old Kitezhgrad since its founding, and Novokitezhgrad shares the trade. Foundryman's Calculus says he had wanted the new city to serve as the cornerstone of his standing in the Tsaritsa's new regime.

History: The old Kitezhgrad was founded by Monomakh Snezhnyi before he became the Belyi Tsar and was the imperial capital of the Pale Star court and the first city of Snezhnaya. After the king of the Volkodlak, Miscislav, was killed, the Emperor took the name Belyi Tsar and eventually moved the seat of government to Snezhnograd. The Abyss later destroyed Kitezhgrad, and Novokitezhgrad was built to replace it.

Foundryman's Calculus presents Alvis as wanting the construction of Novokitezhgrad to serve as the cornerstone of his standing in the Tsaritsa's new regime, and says that when he returned from Novokitezhgrad he found the Royal Energy Commission already had a new master.

Travel: Not accessible; known only from dialogue, loading-screen text and item descriptions. The city's direction from Snezhnograd and the difficulty of its trail are mentioned only in dialogue.

Status as of 7.1: Exists and works as a mining and liquor centre as of 7.1; never shown on screen.

62.content: Kitezhgrad (Kitezh) was the first city of Snezhnaya, an imperial capital built in the fae manner and the seat of the Pale Star court under Monomakh. It stayed the centre of power over the frozen lands until the Emperor, having pardoned humanity and taken them into his realm, moved his seat to Snezhnograd. Its destruction by the Abyss is the reason for Novokitezhgrad.

63.content:
Okurov (also: Okurov Village): Okurov is an abandoned little town in Flamefeather Valley, Snezhnaya, with a warm climate and a dark history. Old stories say that nobody who goes in comes out. The whole area is played in third-person shooter mode.

Locals in Morepesok remember Okurov as a place with warm weather and a famous doctor, where moving in once seemed the natural thing to do, until people noticed that no one who went there ever came back. A folk tale of a beautiful firebird that lures people deep into the valley grew up around it.

Geography: Okurov lies in Flamefeather Valley, a warm pocket among the snow, and is reached through the old railway tunnel and broken carriages by the valley's train line. Unnatural warmth is noticeable at the end of the tunnel. The town has a station, an assembly hall (the 'home' of the town's religion-like community) and thick trees and blue algae; a huge winged creature guards it.

Nearby are tracks, stashes left by Volkodlak gangs, and pieces of Shadow Realm machinery. The assembly hall (Hall of Prayers) is entered by a small gap in its iron door and holds a mechanism that can lift visitors to the 'home' beneath it.

People: The resident the Traveler escorts home is a child, Nastya, who has tree branches growing from her head. The location page also lists an NPC named "Shar". The rest of her 'family' are tall, mostly mindless Leshy-like beings who respond to her, including one she calls Aunt LePuy. A mysterious guardian called Zhara is a giant winged creature, the 'firebird' of the stories. The town's doctor, 'Doctor Moreau', is the alchemist Koshchei.

Others met include Furiosa (Nastya's idol, who warns visitors away) and Ove, a hostile neighbour who hides the elevator control wheel. A newspaper article in the Snezhnaya Vestnik, found in a train carriage, once praised Okurov's warm weather, its exceptional doctor and its open-door policy for all travellers.

History: Okurov was once an inviting town. A doctor there attracted residents with the promise of cures; the town's people adopted a belief that becoming trees, all one family, was the cure for pain and the path to an eternal courtyard. Over time no one who went in came out.

The documents in the assembly hall reveal that the experiments were conducted by Koshchei the Deathless posing as Doctor Moreau, who sought a form of eternity by changing people into a 'Perfect Tree' that gives strength but wears away speech and emotion. The final ceremony aimed to turn everyone into embryos of a new, emotionless existence.

Dangers: Rugged Elder Leshy and Juvenile Tree Segments, Chimeric Armored Beasts and Chimeric Winged Elephants; Shadow Realm rifts; and Zhara, the winged guardian, who attacks intruders. Visitors must also pass old railway infrastructure and drainage tunnels.

Travel: Reached only by following the 'In the Dwelling of Life' series from Flamefeather Valley after unlocking the town in 'Transplanted From Yesterday to Tomorrow'. Local specialty: Golden Fern. Features: Prime Ice, Shadow Wingdrop, Shadow Realm.

Atmosphere: A warm, damp, too-quiet place: smoke on the horizon, blue algae glowing in the dark, trees that are 'strong and healthy' because of Zhara, and children's games ('Catch the Bug', with a 'Badbug' to be caught) that hint at something wrong. The name references the 1908 Gorky novel 'The City of Okurov'.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Okurov stands abandoned. By the wiki's summary of the series, the experiments are exposed, the Eye of Graeae holds a crystal fragment of the ritual's power and Nastya has gone into the Perfect Tree.

64.comment: Okurov: Nastya and the Catch the Bug game
64.content: Nastya is a girl with branches growing from her head, found in a crate during the Traveler's trip to Okurov. She treats 'Catch the Bug' as the welcoming ritual for new friends: she plays the Badbug, the visitors are 'Doctor Birdie', and the Doctor said every step of the rite matters. The game hides a darker idea, that Badbugs (outsiders and the old friends who turned against the Doctor) are burned so that new family can grow from the ashes.

65.content:
Outdoor Hot Spring: The Outdoor Hot Spring is a facility in Everfrozen Earth built around a hot spring that appeared by accident. Humans and fae alike come here to enjoy a rare bit of warmth. It is kept up by an NPC named Kleyeva and is free for everyone.

The notice at the entrance sets house rules by species and tells visitors not to report the spring to the Energy Commission.

Geography: An open-air pool with a deck beside it, and a building with a first room whose pool also restores health. The spring's southern entrance has a flight of stairs leading up to a notice board. Neither the pool nor the interior counts as a low-temperature zone.

A second copy of the notice board stands on the deck. The wiki notes the Eye of Graeae's energy does not drain while the Traveler is here, a gameplay effect of the warm area.

People: Kleyeva maintains the spring and lets everyone use it for free. Thieving Jack Frost is a Jack Frost who stole her clothes in a hidden objective; the wiki ties their dialogue to the hidden objective "Hot Spring Clothing Caper". In Come Out Now!, Kintutu, a Natlan tourist, visits with her Flowfire Bird Javita.

The wiki infers that Kleyeva has had several unpleasant Vila guests, since the notice singles out Vila for complaining.

Culture: The notice says the spring was created by the runoff of pipes, is therefore everyone's common property, and must be looked after, and "under no circumstances" be reported to the Energy Commission. Humans should wash before entering. Volkodlak should remove loose fur. Vila should not come if they are going to complain. Jack Frosts and Snegovik should watch how long they stay to avoid fainting from overexposure.

After Come Out Now! the notice adds, in a larger and thicker hand, that Flowcurrent Birds and Flowfire Birds are not allowed in.

History: In the hidden objective Come Out Now! the Flowfire Bird Javita, a Natlanese tourist's companion, grows livelier in the spring and breaks the railings while running around. The Traveler calms her by creating a Prime Ice cube in the gap. Kintutu then takes her bird home; the Flowcurrent Birds that were swimming vanish with them.

Kintutu says Javita was gloomy on arrival in Snezhnaya, and that she took the locals' advice to try the hot spring. The bird looks dejected when calmed, as though realising the place is not home. After the visit Kleyeva banned the birds because they had made her Jack Frost guests uncomfortable.

Atmosphere: Steamy and unexpectedly homely in a frozen land: a small, slightly shabby public bath with hand-written rules. Being warm is a luxury and everyone treats it as one.

Dangers: No fighting. Jack Frosts and Snegovik can overheat if they stay too long, according to the notice.

Quests: No main quest. The hidden objectives Come Out Now! and the one involving Kleyeva's clothing involve it.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the spring is open and Kleyeva still maintains it. Flowcurrent and Flowfire Birds are banned.

66.content:
Pale Crown Palace (also: Palace of the Pale Crown, Belyi Tsar's mausoleum): The Pale Crown Palace is the Belyi Tsar's mausoleum in White Birch Snowgrave, Snezhnaya. Once one of his palaces, it became his tomb after he died in the Cataclysm 500 years ago, and his body grew into the Tsar's White Birch, a pale mass of 'nerves' over the ruin. A hidden train line leads to it.

The Eye of Graeae says it was created here in the research facility Hvergelmir, and in the 7.0 quests the Traveler recovers a fragment of its power and fights the palace's guardian, Zver.

Geography: The palace lies beneath the Tsar's White Birch. Its map layers are the Hall of the Tsar's Palace, the Hanging Corridor, the Spiraling Tower, 'Where the Hidden Door Was Knocked' and 'Once, the Court of Bliss'. Inside are a Frozen Royal Hall with a throne, a Suspended Tower, sealed gates and a lift to the upper levels, and the Ruined Hvergelmir.

The gates and doors are blocked by Prime Ice and by the White Birch's tendrils, and are opened with statues, heat pipes and prototype Kresnik's Torches.

Places: The Frozen Royal Hall, where two stone statues belong in front of the throne; the Suspended Tower, which must be rotated to connect heat pipes; the Ruined Hvergelmir below; and the Court of Eternal Bliss, entered through a door that the White Birch keeps regrowing over until all three Eye fragments are gathered.

A prototype Kresnik's Torch in the palace recalls the Tsar's experiments, and the palace is where Kresnik's flame was first kindled before it spread across Snezhnaya.

People: No living residents. The Belyi Tsar lies in the White Birch. Zver, his two-headed winged lion companion created by Koshchei, guarded the remains for 500 years. Pavlina and Koshchei once worked in the Hvergelmir laboratories here, and Aksinya, the Tsar's adoptive child, appears in the palace's flashbacks.

In the To Gaze quest the Traveler glimpses two past researchers, Izmaylov and Azazel, and Pavlina's cat Lara, which she left in the researchers' care.

Governance: The wiki calls it the Belyi Tsar's private residence and, in the quest text, his itinerant court, where he welcomed humans alongside the fae. His research institute Hvergelmir worked beneath him here.

History: The Belyi Tsar welcomed humans and fae in this palace, and Kresnik's flame was first lit here. After he fell fighting the Abyss and its beasts during the Cataclysm, his remains were returned to the palace.

Zver carried the Tsar's body home and guarded it for five centuries. The research facility Hvergelmir, where the Eye of Graeae was made, was hidden inside the palace.

The researchers' notes found inside describe experiments on prisoners and Snegovik concerning 'love', and show Izmaylov worrying that the new Tsaritsa's rumored ban on alchemy would end Hvergelmir's bio-alchemy research and the Tsar's last aspiration. By its own account, the Eye of Graeae realised the danger of Aksinya's experiment, asked to be divided into three segments, and persuaded Koshchei, Pavlina and Alvis to stop her.

Atmosphere: A silent snow-buried grave: frozen halls, ice-locked doors and a pale tree-like growth creeping through the rooms. The Train's navigation text calls it 'a stop at which no one arrives, a snow-covered grave'.

Dangers: Chimeric monsters such as armoured beasts, winged elephants and horned bears; Winged Soarer Knights, Winged Halberd-Knights, Glaciomancers, Glacial Wardens and a Rugged Elder Leshy; the White Birch, which drains the Eye of Graeae's energy if the Traveler stands too close; and the boss Zver.

Travel: Reached by a hidden railway summoned by a mechanism and an old prototype train operated by the Eye of Graeae. The Traveler's own Train has a navigation stop there.

Quests: Quest series On One Side a Palace, On the Other a Tomb: To Gaze Upon the Dreaming Pale Crown, and The Stone Beasts, Like Ghouls Seated. The finale, An Ark That Used to Be a Soul, forms the series Her Palace Collapses Into the Blizzard.

In The Stone Beasts, Like Ghouls Seated, the Traveler restores statues, shoots a prototype Kresnik's Torch, passes the Suspended Tower and defeats Zver before reaching the Ruined Hvergelmir to recover the fragment.

Status as of 7.1: Abandoned and accessible. Its guardian is dead and the Court of Eternal Bliss has been entered.

67.content:
Zver is a Chimeric Winged Lion made by Koshchei: a lion and a bird embryo fused so that it has two heads. Because it had some sentience, the Belyi Tsar spared it and brought it into his court; it became the commander of the Aberrant Chimeric Monsters in the war against the Abyss. After the Tsar's death it guarded the palace.

When the Traveler defeated Zver in 7.0, it mocked the Eye of Graeae and asked the Tsar if it could finally follow him into the afterlife.

68.comment: Pale Crown Palace: Tsar's White Birch
68.content:
An overgrowth of nerves from the Belyi Tsar's corpse that grows over the ruin and saps energy from the Eye of Graeae if someone stands too close. Part of his body became the White Birch after he was buried five hundred years ago.

The in-game train description says the Tsar's body 'continues to protect all who dwell in Snezhnaya'.

69.content:
Pilgrimage to the Sacred Gorge: The Pilgrimage to the Sacred Gorge is a snowy mountain gorge in the White Birch Snowgrave of Snezhnaya, on the way to the Pale Crown Palace, the Belyi Tsar's mausoleum. The route is blocked by a collapse that looks like an artificial avalanche, and official signs say the Royal Energy Commission and the Railway Transport Bureau are investigating.

The notes found there reveal that the sabotage was itself ordered by someone the writer calls the Old Sire and carried out by Energy Commission staff in disguise, so the investigation notices are partly a cover.

Geography: A cold, narrow mountain approach in the northern snowfields, part of the White Birch Snowgrave, the former itinerant court of the Belyi Tsar that became his burial ground. A railway line runs along it toward the Pale Crown Palace and stretches of it have collapsed. Prime Ice, Seelies and Tsar's White Birch are found here, with Frostfairy Flower as a local specialty.

The gorge lies in the same area as the Palace, whose in-game description speaks of a stop where no one arrives and a snow-covered grave.

Places: The notable sites are the blocked rail line with its notice board and a control console left near the staged collapse. The point of the gorge is its role as the road to the Palace.

People: No residents are shown. The notes mention three groups: the Royal Energy Commission of Snezhnaya, the Snezhnaya Royal Railway Transport Bureau, and brigands who want to plunder the Palace.

A Transport Bureau investigator concludes the avalanche was triggered by hand and suspects someone in the Commission is hiding something or tampering with the Palace. The Commission-side writer treats the closure as an order from the Old Sire and remarks that earlier custom would have used the High Table, suggesting he is unwell and that his adopted children cannot hold out much longer.

Governance: Two bodies have a hand here: the Energy Commission, which put up the warning sign, and the Transport Bureau, which polices the railway and expects reports. The Orderbearer note shows the Commission acting on an order from above without telling the Bureau.

History: The collapse is recent as of the Traveler's visit. The Pale Crown Palace itself is the Belyi Tsar's mausoleum, once one of his palaces, left behind after he died in the cataclysm five hundred years ago.

Atmosphere: Freezing wind, deep snow, damaged track and officious warning signs; a sense that the official story hides something.

Dangers: Chimeric Armored Beasts, Chimeric Horned Bears, Winged Halberd-Knights and Winged Soarer Knights roam the area, with the Frostarm Lawachurl as an elite enemy. Further collapses from structural damage are warned of on the notice board.

Travel: The gorge is on the route to the Pale Crown Palace, and the sign asks visitors to take care until the railway is fully repaired.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the route to the Palace is still blocked and the investigation notice stands.

The notes do not say whether the sabotage will be reversed.

70.comment: Pilgrimage to the Sacred Gorge: The Sabotaged Route and the Old Sire
70.content: The notice board blames deliberate sabotage of the route to the Pale Crown Palace and says the Energy Commission and the Transport Bureau are investigating. An investigator's note judges the avalanche was triggered by hand and, finding the Commission's sign odd, suspects a cover-up or tampering with the Palace, while hoping brigands who try to plunder it regret it. A second note, the Records of the Orderbearer, says that on the Old Sire's orders a small blockage was introduced, that this would normally have been given to the High Table, and that using Commission staff for field work may be meant to keep the matter beyond the reach of gangsters. Treat the Old Sire's identity as unknown.

71.content:
Podvorye Restaurant (also: Podvorye, Ресторан «Подворье»): Podvorye Restaurant is a long-established eatery in front of Snezhnograd Square in Snezhnaya. It serves refined versions of traditional local dishes and Fire-Water, and its owner and entire staff are Volkodlak and other fae, who are long-lived. The owner, Nefedov, keeps it a dine-in house where food is served piping hot.

Odette and Vodyanitsa, performers of the Korolevskiy Troupe, are regulars whom the staff greet by name. The name is Russian for "courtyard" or "homestead".

Places: Guests come in from the square to a dining room with numbered tables, a bar and a busy kitchen. Servers (Buturlina and Eliseev) work the floor, and Smirnov tends the bar. Nefedov, the owner, oversees orders, and Gromov cooks. Surikov and Menshikov, two regulars, drink inside, while Hussaina and Samir stand outside.

Buturlina runs the restaurant's shop: cooked food and ingredients, with the dishes refreshed daily and ingredients weekly. It sells the Podvorye Smoked Sausage recipe, and its stock includes borscht and medovik.

People: Every member of staff is a Volkodlak (beast fae of Snezhnaya). Nefedov, the owner, is a brisk, practical boss who says his Volkodlak-founded house serves everyone in Snezhnaya. Buturlina, a server, is courteous and proud of the menu. Eliseev, also a server, gets sleepier when the weather changes, which he says varies among Volkodlak. Smirnov is a polite bartender who recommends Fire-Water from a Novokitezh distillery and says his clawed paws handle bottles steadily. Gromov is a nervous young cook who was an apprentice until his mentor took leave for back pain.

Surikov and Menshikov drink together inside; Surikov boasts of his hunting past when drunk and Menshikov tells him to drink water. A drunk named Vanya sleeps in the alley next to the restaurant (the Hidden Exploration Objective "Fire-Water, Oh Fire-Water..." has the Traveler wake him). Hussaina and Samir have no stories told.

Culture: The house rule is that guests eat at the restaurant so the food arrives hot: according to Gromov, the boss refused requests for take-out, as is done in Mondstadt. Reservations are not taken, though Buturlina hints that an advance word can get a table assigned. Staff keep fur out of the cooking, and a dish with a stray hair is replaced.

The signature dish is the Podvorye Smoked Sausage, sliced and eaten as a shared starter. Odette is a regular who gets Snowball Blooms Atop Snowfields and a small ice cream. Vodyanitsa orders double meat and extra ice cream. The restaurant also serves Rimecurrant Ice Cream, medovik and stroganina.

History: No founding date is given. Staff note that the restaurant has long existed with Volkodlak founders, and that the present boss has been head chef for a very long time.

Atmosphere: A lively working restaurant: orders called out, a bar with bottles of Fire-Water, and flustered or sleepy staff with tails and paws. It feels homely rather than formal, but serious about food.

Status as of 7.1: Open and busy as of 7.1.

A 7.1 Travelers' Tales anecdote, "Odette: Food Is No Small Matter", starts when the player enters the restaurant. Odette eats her special diet and Vodyanitsa tries to tempt her with sweets on her cheat day.

72.content: Podvorye Restaurant staff are all Volkodlak. Nefedov: owner, whose house keeps food dine-in so it stays hot. Buturlina: server and shopkeeper. Eliseev: server who tires in weather changes. Gromov: apprentice cook, likely to take over the main entree. Smirnov: bartender who recommends Fire-Water from Novokitezh. Their wiki profiles are otherwise empty.

73.comment: Podvorye Restaurant: Odette at Podvorye Restaurant
73.content: In the open world Odette is found at the restaurant considering her order; once she asks for Snowball Blooms Atop Snowfields and is told they are out, and elsewhere she says "same as yesterday". In the 7.1 anecdote "Odette: Food Is No Small Matter" she is eating snowball flowers, rimecurrants, beets, cheese, egg, chicken, fish and rice. This is a special diet from the Fontaine nurse Sigewinne, with cheat days. She rejects Vodyanitsa's ice cream, medovik and stroganina, but Vodyanitsa has the kitchen make a dessert, checked by letter with Sigewinne, and congratulates her on a rehearsal.

74.content:
Port Belovodye (also: Belovodye): Port Belovodye is a port in Snezhnaya that earns enormous sums. It is known chiefly from one historical episode: in the Tsaritsa's second year, its human inhabitants declared self-governance and rebelled against the fae princes, and in her third year the newly created Fatui brought them back, ending the revolt by negotiation.

Canon does not show the port in game as of 7.1. Its name echoes the folklore realm Belovodye, 'land of white waters'.

History: In the winter of the second year after Anastasya became Tsaritsa of All Snezhnaya, the humans of Port Belovodye used the death of the Belyi Tsar as their chance to declare self-governance. The fae Grand Duke Drevogorye marched on them and failed. The following year the Tsaritsa sent troops of the new Fatui, occupying the lands of several fae clans on the way, to attack the independent government. On the tenth day of the third month she sent envoys, who calmed the separatists and asked them to hand over the instigators, promising amnesty to everyone else. They accepted, and the port was spared from being levelled.

The same chronicle (A Brief History of the Pale Starborn) records that the Tsaritsa did not muster the older Druzhna but founded the Fatui for the campaign, that the Drevogorye, Volkhovan and Cirnareka clans lost their princely titles for negligence, and that Grand Duke Drevogorye accused the Tsaritsa herself of treason and died fighting the Fatui. Thirteen days later, on the twenty-third day of the same month, she demanded that the absent fae princes surrender their authority for honorary titles.

Economy: The port is very profitable. Someone's Research Notes, written by an unnamed boastful researcher, claim that even 5 per cent of the port's income would be an acceptable reward for his work.

Status as of 7.1: No events beyond the old revolt are shown; the port is not accessible in the game as of 7.1.

75.content:
Rankova Zorya: Rankova Zorya is a railway halt in the Volkodlak Tundra of Snezhnaya that was nearly abandoned until Alyosha, Odette and Vodyanitsa, with the Traveler's help, renovated it. It now has a furnace, a stage, a Bing-Bang Finchball stall and a restaurant, and new residents have arrived. In 7.1 the battle against Ronova, the Ruler of Death, took place here.

The in-game description calls it a temporary station on the verge of abandonment. At a time when Snezhnayans' desire to develop the tundra has weakened, someone wanting to maintain it is described as quite romantic. The name means 'dawn'.

Geography: A small station village on the open tundra with a train track, a platform, a stage for dancers, a furnace that provides stable heat, a restaurant (Restaurant Zorya) and a carriage that serves as a base. Snowmen near the stall can be decorated with hats and scarves after 'Newcomers in the Snow'. A Teleport Waypoint, Prime Ice and a Stellar Vortex are nearby.

A cliff north of the village holds a Jack Frost puzzle. Vodyanitsa says the rumbling of arriving trains hides her singing practice, and jokes that her voice might delay a train's departure.

Places: Restaurant Zorya, with the restaurant vendor Tolstaya, opens after 'Daybreak After the Snow'. Bing-Bang Finchball stall: a game booth run by Mayskaya on behalf of Basima, decorated by Vodyanitsa. The stage, where Odette coaches Rytova. The furnace, which was repaired using a Smelted Kristall Ore obtained from a fae gang. A Bulletin Board and a Vestnik stand that sells newspapers.

Vestnik articles available here include 'The Headless Train Attendant in the Snow', a Transport Bureau statement about unusual disturbances along the railway line, and 'The Myth of Al-Ahmar, the False King'.

People: Alyosha, Odette and Vodyanitsa are the founders and recurring presences: Alyosha picks guard dogs (including Lyumina) and makes Rimecurrant ice cream; Odette keeps the place safe and coaches the dancer Rytova; Vodyanitsa manages the station, builds the Finchball stall and sings on the restaurant roof. Domovoy friends of Rytova, whom she is teaching to dance, live nearby; Zarubina and Tomilina join her practice.

Other named residents: Mayskaya, Shatskaya, Knyazev (a general goods vendor), Shishkina, Cherkassky, Dorokhov, Golovin, Ignatov, Khrustalev, Nezhdanov, Vakhrushina, Yarkova, Zheleznov, Zimnyakov and Krivda (tied to a hidden exploration objective). Vesna may appear as a confused traveller who got off at the wrong stop, and Tartaglia and Vodyanitsa are seen talking at the restaurant, where he says he and his siblings are fans and that he waits in line for show tickets for his sister Tonia.

History: The renovation began with a chain of World Quests after the Mistilteinn Archon Quest. 'Atop the Floating Snow': Odette coaches Rytova. 'Awaiting the Dawn': Vodyanitsa and Mayskaya set up the Finchball stall. 'A Thread of Dawn-Light': Alyosha wants to repair the heat source and, with the Traveler, obtains a power core. 'Daybreak After the Snow' completes the restaurant and the heat. 'Newcomers in the Snow' adds Vodyanitsa's snowmen, which stand in for her, Odette and Alyosha.

Alyosha says the idea began as something Vodyanitsa randomly raised at a party. He explained that the government is too busy with a grander plan to notice a small station, so citizens must step up, which he can do without taking up his gun for the Rokot. Odette drove bandits out of the area to keep the trains safe; Vodyanitsa arranged an extra trade route with merchants she knows.

Atmosphere: Cosy and slightly chaotic: bright restaurant windows against the dark tundra, a snowman 'supervising' practice, dogs trotting among stalls, Vodyanitsa singing from the roof and the roar of arriving trains. Money is tight but optimism is high.

Dangers: Bandits and dangerous elements have been removed from the area by Odette; ambient dangers elsewhere on the tundra remain.

Status as of 7.1: A living village as of 7.1. Its founders are busy with other work, so they visit instead of living there permanently.

The 7.1 battle damaged the site, but the structures were restored within a few days.

76.content: The restaurant opens after 'Daybreak After the Snow' with a signboard that Vodyanitsa drew of herself, Odette and Alyosha as ingredients in a pot, and a free meal for the first customer, who turns out to be Mitya. Vodyanitsa has been studying a book called '100 Train Station Delicacies' and teases that nobody eats her cooking. She admits to a three-bowls-a-week limit on Rimecurrant ice cream, which she is tempted to stretch.

77.content: A game booth where players launch Finchballs into scoring rings. Mayskaya runs it because Basima is busy with a new Finchball mode. Vodyanitsa, who manages the station, wants the pieces dressed fancy, beautiful and cute (in that order) and offers clothes from her own closet; she later toys with dressing them as Odette and Alyosha.

78.comment: Rankova Zorya: The Battle of Rankova Zorya
78.content: Ronova, the Ruler of Death, attacked the researchers delivering Mistilteinn equipment while the Tsaritsa met Rhinedottir elsewhere. At the Jester's request the Traveler stalled her, with Dainsleif, Odette and Vesna. Her Curse of Death sent the Traveler to the afterlife temporarily, and Vesna's Authority of Life created Seals of Life from the Traveler's memories to escape it. Once Celestia reclaimed her authority she was stripped of power and defeated, and the curse was undone.

79.content:
Relics of the Fallen Grace: Relics of the Fallen Grace is a Domain of Mastery on Fellfrost Peak, the great snow-sloped mountain south of Snezhnograd. According to its text it is a sanctuary once built by the ancient fae and now despoiled by petty brigands. Clearing it grants talent materials, described in game as insight and enlightenment.

The longer description tells of fae who had lost their homeland and raised a secluded sanctuary here, hoping to ease the pain of extinction through cold, solitary asceticism. Over hundreds of epochs, those who mourned the golden realm and the followers who never knew it died one after another like scattering snow. The last hermit left, and only a freezing silence remained. It appeared in 7.0.

Gameplay data (labelled as such): the Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday rewards are the Charity, Fortitude and Glory teaching series; enemies include Volkodlak raiders, sharpshooters and lobbers, Winged knights, Juvenile Tree Segments and a Rugged Elder Leshy. Its Ley Line Disorder triggers an Electro shockwave on Superconduct or Stellar-Conduct reactions.

Atmosphere: Cold, abandoned stillness: a once-sacred place gone silent under snow, now trodden by armed squatters. Suited to scenes of loss and fading faith.

Dangers: Volkodlak brigands, winged armoured foes and leshy-type tree creatures; the surrounding Fellfrost Peak has heavy snowstorms, and an in-game notice there warns that hiking is prohibited.

Status as of 7.1: Permanent domain as of 7.1. The sanctuary is empty of its original inhabitants; canon names no founder.

80.content:
Restaurant Zorya (also: Rankova Kafe, Zorya Restaurant): Restaurant Zorya is a re-opened restaurant in Rankova Zorya, in the Volkodlak Tundra. Tolstaya runs it and sells food and recipes there.

It is rebuilt during the world quest Daybreak After the Snow and cannot be used before then. The sign reads "Rankova Kafe" in Snezhnayan script.

People: Named NPCs are Tolstaya (the proprietor), Ignatov, Nezhdanov and Vakhrushina. Tolstaya keeps the shop open at all hours.

History: In Daybreak After the Snow, Alyosha, Odette and Vodyanitsa have made the station town warmer and busier: a furnace now supplies heat, an extra trade route is agreed, and Odette has driven off bandits so trains can pass safely. Vodyanitsa insists a station needs a restaurant and, with a book of train-station dishes in hand, holds a cleaning "ceremony" to open the building. A hand-drawn signboard shows her, Odette and Alyosha as little chefs.

Culture: The restaurant is part of a station community. Vodyanitsa calls train-station food a major culinary institution.

Atmosphere: A warm, crowded station restaurant with a freshly hung sign, mismatched cheerful decor and the smell of hot food against the frost outside.

81.content:
The Ruined Hvergelmir (also: Ruined Hvergelmir, Hvergelmir research institute, Hvergelmir ruins): The Ruined Hvergelmir is what remains of the Hvergelmir research institute in Snezhnaya's White Birch Snowgrave, below the Belyi Tsar's Pale Crown Palace. It was a secret bio-alchemy and Shadow Realm institute founded by the Belyi Tsar and entrusted to his human ward Aksinya, with a goal of engineering a "Proto-Man" who would let the Tsar become the Primordial Human. It holds four laboratories belonging to Aksinya, Alvis, Koshchei and Pavlina.

The Traveler first sees it as a Shadow Realm vision on the train to the palace in the world quest To Gaze Upon the Dreaming Pale Crown (7.0). The institute is shown intact about 500 years ago, with its researchers, assistants and a cat.

Geography: Hvergelmir lies in the hidden chambers of the Belyi Tsar's private palace outside Snezhnograd, reached through the White Birch Snowgrave by hidden train tracks. The Eye of Graeae calls it only a corner of the palace's shadow. The vision places the institute at the edge of the Shadow Realm's "Font", into which Aksinya falls at the end of the flashback.

Locked gates and concealed doors separate the laboratories; a painting hides a secret passage in Pavlina's lab, and Prime Ice seals some of the notes.

Places: Four laboratories fill the institute: Koshchei's (alchemy and chimeric beasts), Pavlina's (Prime Ice facilities and preserved Hyperborean relics), Alvis' (potions and the Shadow Realm secret chamber) and Aksinya's (the plan to create the Proto-Man). A hidden room behind a painting in Pavlina's lab holds the starving cat, and a locked gate nearby is guarded by the assistant Vsevolod.

Koshchei's lab holds notes on the Prime Chimeric Nexus and the Eitr; Alvis' lab has the scales and potion formula used in the quest puzzle, and Alvis' notes about moving Hvergelmir to a new Kitezhgrad; Pavlina's has a Mora chest sealed in Prime Ice with her notes; Aksinya's contains Note VI of the Belyi Tsar's papers and a letter reading "All for a world free of sorrow".

People: Aksinya, Court Jester and de facto head, is joined by Alvis (Grand Duke of the Domovoy), Pavlina (Grand Duchess of the Snegurochka) and the alchemist Koshchei. Their assistants Izmaylov (Aksinya's Domovoy pupil), Azazel and Vsevolod appear in the vision.

Pavlina's cat Lara is left in Koshchei's care. The four leaders have different ideologies yet were close; the Eye of Graeae, reviewing the records, finds it strange that they would betray one another.

History: The Belyi Tsar entered the Shadow Realm, found an infant (Aksinya) in a Hyperborean time capsule and, inspired by its life-preserving technology, founded Hvergelmir to seek "the stairway to the vacant seat in the court of the stars" where sorrow would end. The researchers explored Hyperborean ruins in the Shadow Realm, adapted energy-storing devices into firearms and created chimeric monsters; their final creation was the Eye of Graeae. After the Tsar's death about 500 years ago, a vision shows Aksinya pushed into the Shadow Realm Font, an act that later texts attribute to Pavlina, Alvis and Koshchei.

The institute's work crossed into forbidden territory and survived only through the Tsar's tacit protection. When the new Tsaritsa took the throne, researchers feared a ban on alchemy. Koshchei's notes call Aksinya's idea of eternal shared love a dead end and side with the person in the egg; Alvis plans to take a share of the Eye's power and later to move Hvergelmir to Novokitezhgrad after Kitezhgrad's destruction; Pavlina considers the power rightfully the fae's.

Atmosphere: The rooms feel like a laboratory halted mid-experiment, pale, cold, and tense with whispered rivalries. The cat still cries for food, and the notes left on desks read as if addressed to someone no longer there.

Dangers: The Shadow Realm sends visitors into past scenes where they cannot be seen or heard, and the Traveler is trapped until puzzles are solved. Chimeric beasts and winged knights guard the approach, and the cold is deadly without Kresnik Kristall.

Travel: Reached via the quest To Gaze Upon the Dreaming Pale Crown: the player summons hidden tracks from a tower in the White Birch Snowgrave, rides the train, and falls into the vision. Co-op and the Serenitea Pot are locked for most of the quest.

Quests: To Gaze Upon the Dreaming Pale Crown opens the quest chain On One Side a Palace, On the Other a Tomb. Its sequel, The Stone Beasts, Like Ghouls Seated, and An Ark That Used to Be a Soul continue to the Court of Bliss where the Traveler defeats Aksinya and the Primordial Human.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the institute is a ruin. Aksinya remains trapped in the Shadow Realm after her defeat.

The Eye of Graeae's records say Alvis has recently passed away. What became of Koshchei is unclear; Pavlina is met in the present at the House of Hesperides.

82.comment: The Ruined Hvergelmir: Hvergelmir's Four Laboratories
82.content: Koshchei studied the Prime Chimeric Nexus (three, perhaps five, embryo types) and the Eitr, a living bio-furnace that dissolves embryos into one perfect form. Pavlina, a Snegurochka princess, built Prime Ice facilities and kept Hyperborean relics. Alvis, Domovoy Grand Duke, made potions from Kresnik crystal and planned his own advancement. Aksinya's research produced the Eye of Graeae.

83.comment: The Ruined Hvergelmir: Aksinya's Fall into the Shadow Realm
83.content: In a vision, Aksinya, newly bearing the Eye of Graeae, intends to show it to her colleagues in the hope of continuing her plan, believing all differences return to a single path. Someone pushes her into the Font of the Shadow Realm; she says she will return and does not understand why they abandoned the grand undertaking. In the present she leads the Traveler to the Belyi Tsar's tomb and the Court of Bliss.

84.content:
Sadov-Arbat (also: Garden Arbat): Sadov-Arbat is a long-established handicrafts and souvenir shop in Snezhnograd. According to its map description, in the Belyi Tsar's time the site was a market where fae bartered with one another before it became a proper shop.

Its owner is Blyushko, and the shop also employs staff such as the clerk Yevlena. The wiki records that its goods cannot be bought because newly arrived stock is still being inventoried and organised.

People: Named NPCs here are Blyushko (owner), Yevlena (salesclerk), Lopushina and Tsoslina. Blyushko's only recorded idle line is an invitation to step inside and discuss the details.

History: It is said that during the rule of the Belyi Tsar the original site was a market where fae traded with each other, and that it later developed into an ordinary shop. This is stated as hearsay in the map description, so treat it as local tradition rather than established history.

Atmosphere: A craft shop full of boxed, unsorted new stock, with staff busy counting and sorting it.

85.content:
Sanctuary of Grief (also: Signora's tomb): The Sanctuary of Grief is the tomb of Signora, the Eighth Fatui Harbinger, in the Everfrozen Earth of Snezhnaya. It is an ice-sealed palace built after she died in Inazuma, where she lost to the Traveler and was executed. The remaining Harbingers arranged her burial here, and Fatui work was halted for half a day to mourn her. The mood is cold, quiet mourning.

During the Archon Quest Mistilteinn (7.0) Odette goes there to say a private farewell. In-game text frames the place as perhaps the gentlest end for someone who suffered the agony of loss and faded amid hatred and madness.

Geography: Set in the Everfrozen Earth, the northern tundra of Snezhnaya. The sanctuary is a palace-like building entombed in ice. Frostfairy Flowers grow nearby. The wiki notes its architecture resembles Neo-Byzantine church design, a real-world comparison rather than a canon statement.

The Eye of Graeae's database holds no description of the building, only a record that it was frozen on the day work across Snezhnaya was suspended for half a day to commemorate a Harbinger's passing. Do not invent where the ice came from.

Places: The mausoleum is the centre of the area and the destination of Odette's scene. A viewpoint here is titled Where Frost Entombs All Sorrows. Near the mausoleum Odette passes a flame moth that triggers visions of past conversations between her and Signora.

The area has its own mourning music: with Columbina in the party and conscious, her vocal line from the earlier Elogia Cinerosa piece joins it; otherwise it is a piano arrangement. This is a presentation detail, not lore.

People: Signora lies entombed here. Odette, who trained under Signora, comes to say goodbye. Arlecchino, who gives Odette Signora's final message, is the other person tied to the scene.

In the cinematic's flashbacks Signora says she understands Odette's hatred of the Fatui, that she never opposed Odette's dancing though she became an enemy of her ballet, and that if she died Odette should be free to dance. Treat this as the quest's characterisation of Signora in this one relationship.

History: Signora lost the duel before the Raiden Shogun's throne to the Traveler and was executed in Inazuma. The Harbingers in Snezhnaya arranged her burial in the sanctuary; Pulcinella decreed that Fatui work halt for half a day, as the interlude teaser A Winter Night's Lazzo shows.

Five years after her death her Harbinger seat was filled by another. In Mistilteinn, after the Snezhnograd events, Odette lays a letter and her Cor Ignis before the mausoleum, dances, then shatters the Cor Ignis with an ice dagger and leaves.

Atmosphere: Silence, pale light, ice that does not melt and a faint warmth of flame remembered. Scenes here should be solemn and restrained; grief shows as stillness.

Dangers: The wiki lists no enemies for the sanctuary itself; only a local specialty, Frostfairy Flower.

Quests: Mistilteinn (Archon Quest, Chapter VII, 7.0) has Odette visit the tomb: a flame-moth sequence of visions, then a cinematic ending with the Cor Ignis broken.

The scene ties the place to the Fatui's grief for Signora and to Odette's choice to accept her past.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the sanctuary stands intact as Signora's tomb in the Everfrozen Earth.

Odette has said her farewell and left her Cor Ignis shattered. No later event at the sanctuary is recorded through 7.1.

86.comment: Sanctuary of Grief: Odette's Farewell at the Tomb
86.content: In the Mistilteinn cutscene Odette places a letter and her Cor Ignis before the mausoleum and dances Spirit Seeker. Flashbacks show Signora telling Arlecchino she hopes Odette can live to see the Tsaritsa succeed and, if Signora dies, be free to dance, and Arlecchino explaining that her own Two Worlds' Flames can burn away memories of the Fatui. Odette finishes, summons an ice dagger and breaks her Cor Ignis; the flames inside the ice burn the letter and become crimson moths. Odette's choice is to accept everything and move on.

87.content:
Scars of Cursed Obsession: Scars of Cursed Obsession is a Forgery domain in Snezhnaya's Everfrozen Earth. Its description calls it a secret haven where rebels chased the dream of a return to the old order, a dream that died in crimson fire and left only ash. Clearing it grants weapon ascension materials.

The longer text sets the story in a peaceful era when the Belyi Tsar's conquests had become legend and the succession turmoil was mere history. Fae who never lived through those days still yearned to revive that ancient glory. A leaden dream, stained by countless souls' blood, left its dreamer unshaken, convinced it was the way to honour. At the road's end there was no glory and no old world, only blood that had grown cold and foul and drowned her. It appeared in 7.0.

Gameplay data (labelled as such): the Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday rewards are the Cast Iron, Chain Track and Severed Steel series (with Pale Star Army, Cellared Spiritual Nectar and Frost Emperor themed names); enemies include Volkodlak raiders, sharpshooters, lobbers and bashers, a Leomastiff Guard, a Voywolf Hunter and a Fanged Zealot. Its Ley Line Disorder boosts Swirl damage.

Atmosphere: Ash-grey ruin of a failed uprising; zeal curdled into grief. Scenes here suit themes of nostalgia, obsession and futile restoration.

Dangers: Armed Volkodlak bands and wolf-like fighters, plus a fanatical zealot at the end of the trial; the winter cold of the Everfrozen Earth.

Status as of 7.1: Permanent domain as of 7.1. The rebels are gone; canon gives no further detail.

88.content:
Snezhnaya (also: Snezhnayan, Land of Snow, Nation of Eternal Winter): Snezhnaya is the Cryo nation of perpetual winter in the far north of Teyvat. It worships the Tsaritsa (Anastasya Feodorovna Snezhnaya), Cryo Archon and God of Love, who unlike most Archons rules directly and absolutely from Zapolyarny Palace in the capital, Snezhnograd. Her Fatui act as government, diplomats and army, and her goal is to overthrow the Heavenly Principles. Humans share the land with the Snowland Fae, the old aristocracy of her predecessor the Belyi Tsar, and survive the cold by burning Kresnik Kristall in great furnaces called Kresnik's Torches.

It is Teyvat's most militarily and technologically advanced nation (railways, factories, firearms, Delusions) and reputedly the second-wealthiest after Liyue. The autonomous region of Nod-Krai is its southernmost part. Snezhnaya became explorable in Version 7.0, the setting of Archon Quest Chapter VII.

Geography: Frozen earth and ice fields with month-long blizzards and night auroras. Explorable areas: Volkodlak Tundra (southwest, the entry from Nod-Krai), Everfrozen Earth (north, with Snezhnograd), Fellfrost Peak (south of the capital), Flamefeather Valley (west) and White Birch Snowgrave, the Belyi Tsar's old court and tomb. Novokitezhgrad and Port Belovodye cannot yet be visited.

Government: The Tsaritsa holds absolute power; her decrees, called Edicts, are the highest law, and she reviews ministers' reports at court herself. The Fatui, headquartered in Glupov and led by Director Pierro and the Eleven Harbingers (all appointed by her), handle most governance. The Snezhnograd Veche, a council she created to replace the fae aristocracy, legislates by majority vote; its Speaker is the Harbinger Pulcinella, also Mayor of Snezhnograd and Glupov, and the Fatui usually get their way there. Nobles hold titles at her pleasure and mostly lack political power. The Druzhna, mostly Vila fae under Commander Vesna, is her personal guard. Nod-Krai is fully autonomous by Edict.

Other state bodies: the Royal Energy Commission (torches and Kristall), the Royal Railway Transport Bureau, Sandrone's Armory Palace, Pantalone's state-owned Northland Bank, and Fatui Internal Affairs (the "Okhranka"), which investigates Fatui misconduct and reports to the Tsaritsa. Veche debate is real but limited: Harbingers argue openly in session, and reform councillors such as Euphrosiniya Trubetskaya complain that the Speaker dismisses their proposals to heat the poor Zolnyy district.

Religion: Devotion centres on the Tsaritsa's throne ("In Snezhnaya, all shall be offered unto the throne of Her Majesty"); no organised church has been shown. Her divine name is Vassaga and her regnal titles include Holy One of All Winters; ordinary people call her only by her title.

She refuses to use her authority of love, seeing the love the Heavenly Principles force on gods as a false curse. Dainsleif says she has no love left for her people, nor they for her, and that her followers hope only to stand with her when she rebels against the heavens; yet in 7.1 people eagerly volunteered to help her fight Death, and intimates such as Vesna and Danica think her kinder than she believes. A Statue of the Seven stands in Snezhnograd.

Economy: Pantalone sets economic policy; factories mass-produce household goods for export, and the Northland Bank and Adventurers' Guild, both founded here, operate across Teyvat. Energy is the binding constraint: Kresnik Kristall is mined chiefly at Novokitezhgrad and shipped by rail.

Novokitezhgrad is also known for liquor, and Port Belovodye earns vast revenue. Snezhnayan merchants once offered Fire-Water to Mondstadt, but Diluc declined after one drink knocked him out for three days. Factories live on energy quotas, so Project Stuzha set industrialists against households.

History: Long ago the land was green and held golden Hyperborea, destroyed about 6,000 years ago. The Belyi Tsar united the fae and became the first Cryo Archon 2,000 years ago; he died fighting the Abyss in the Cataclysm 500 years ago, and Anastasya succeeded him.

Hyperborean experiments on the Cryo Dragon's corpse froze the land and crystallised its ley lines into Kresnik Kristall. The Belyi Tsar founded Kitezhgrad and the Pale Star Court, admitted humans to his realm, built the first Kresnik's Torches and moved his seat to Snezhnograd. On her accession the Tsaritsa crushed fae princes who refused her, founded the Fatui with Pierro, created the Veche and cut ties with the other Archons. Shortly before the Traveler's journey she began gathering the other Archons' Gnoses.

Her Harbingers took the Anemo and Geo Gnoses (via Signora), Electro and Dendro (via Dottore) and Hydro (via Arlecchino); Capitano was excused from taking the Pyro Gnosis, which burned with Irminsul. Signora was entombed in ice at the Sanctuary of Grief.

Customs: Life is spent indoors, being alive is itself a blessing, and families are close. Loyalty is prized; betrayal and unpaid debts are deeply personal affronts, as a nursery rhyme about breaking a pinkie promise and being thrown on the ice shows. Fire-Water, the strongest liquor known, is downed a glass at a time out of respect. People use name and patronymic and say "comrade".

Rye replaces wheat, milk becomes smetana, coastal towns eat mostly seafood, and borscht is called an authentic dish. Alchemy is banned on the mainland, imposed by the Harbingers after Belyi Tsar-era alchemists bred chimeric monsters. The Korolevskiy Theater is a pilgrimage site for performers, and the Snezhnaya Vestnik newspaper sells at stations.

Festivals: Krsnik Noc is a Snezhnayan festival; it is known only from a Snezhnayan merchant likening Lantern Rite's mood to it during that limited-time event.

Military: The Fatui are Teyvat's strongest army; all known fighters use elemental attacks through technology or Delusions. Skirmishers wear mechanised suits, Oprichniki carry elemental guns, Landcruisers patrol. Snezhnayans are conscripted into military training, though not all trainees join the Fatui; each Harbinger commands personal troops, and the House of the Hearth raises orphans as agents.

Foreign relations: The Fatui conduct nearly all diplomacy, and their aggressive encroachment makes them distrusted abroad, though ordinary Snezhnayan merchants meet little prejudice. Jean counts Snezhnaya, like Mondstadt, an independent nation. The Khaenri'ahns descend from the Tsaritsa and honour her as the "Mother of Khaenri'ah".

Dangers: Lethal cold away from heat, month-long blizzards, Shadow Realm rifts that leave the lost as soulless husks, chimeric monsters from banned alchemy, hostile rogue fae, and banditry born of poverty in remote towns.

Atmosphere: Birch forests, steel railways, towns huddled around a torch's glow; Snezhnograd is beautiful under auroras and endless blizzards but increasingly industrial, and fae of many kinds live openly among humans.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Snezhnaya has defeated the Shade of Death, Ronova, whose curse killed anyone developing anti-Celestia technology. The Tsaritsa holds six Gnoses, Project Mistilteinn has resumed, and the Traveler serves her as a consultant.

Ronova lost her authority after the Tsaritsa slowed time around Rhinedottir with the six Gnoses, and Pierro's new Delusion mortally wounded her. Dying, she fused the "Eitr" with the Nail of Retribution above the Cryo Dragon's corpse as a "parting gift"; the Nail began to crumble, threatening to spread Holy Soil across Teyvat.

The energy rationing of Project Stuzha was suspended during the crisis; whether it resumed is unclear. Corruption reviews are under way. Rhinedottir spared the Tsaritsa and told her she had earned her respect; Dainsleif agrees that Ronova's defeat begins a new era, though "not a peaceful era."

89.content:
Snezhnograd ("Snow City") is the capital, in Everfrozen Earth. It holds most of the state's headquarters: Zapolyarny Palace, the fortress-city Glupov, the Snezhnograd Veche State Hall, Druzhna HQ, the Adventurers' Guild and Northland Bank headquarters, and the nation's most important Kresnik's Torch in Kresnik's Burning Heart. It also has the Korolevskiy Theater, Central Station and the popular Podvorye Restaurant, and Zolnyy, the poor industrial "Ash District". Zapolyarny Palace ("Palace Beyond the Arctic Circle") was the Belyi Tsar's seat and is now the Tsaritsa's; she rules from a throne of sculpted ice and sometimes stands alone on a high balcony overlooking the plaza.

Fae live in the city in fair numbers, though fewer than in Novokitezhgrad. Pulcinella is the city's second mayor, having succeeded the human I. Ivanovna N. A hidden chamber beneath the palace holds a huge crystalline seal left by the Third Descender, which reacts only to Gnoses; the Tsaritsa believes all seven are needed to open it. The palace treasury keeps the chariot-sized skull of King Miscislav, still marked by the Belyi Tsar's spear.

90.comment: Snezhnaya: Glupov and the Armory Palace
