90.content: Glupov ("city of fools") is a satellite fortress-city inside Snezhnograd and the headquarters of the Fatui, built on the Tsaritsa's order in the fourth year of her reign. Entry requires a permit or invitation. Deep within lies the Royal Armory Palace, managed by Sandrone, where weapons such as Landcruisers are developed and where Project Mistilteinn's underground research site is located.

91.comment: Snezhnaya: The Snezhnograd Veche and Rokot
91.content: The Veche is described as a large council where interest groups meet to discuss the nation, issue decrees and assess policy. In 7.0 it renewed Project Stuzha with sixty-one percent support, narrower than before. Outside it works the Rokot ("Rumble"), a civilian organisation serving "the common people": members take codenames so their political voice is not tied to their status, rarely meet, and avoid violence, instead gathering evidence of abuses so that official investigations follow. Because it opposed Stuzha (and sometimes the Tsaritsa herself), the Fatui monitor it as an enemy, though some Fatui consider it peaceful. Alyosha, Vodyanitsa and the Traveler are members; Odette was the infiltrator "Lelek" and is suspended.

92.comment: Snezhnaya: Kresnik Kristall and Kresnik's Torch
92.content:
Kresnik Kristall is a crystalline ore that burns with intense heat. It formed when the Cryo Dragon's released authority turned Snezhnaya's ley lines into crystal veins; early settlers found the veins by following Kristall Bugs. Without it humans could not live here: the land was once so cold that only fae survived. Kresnik's Torches, furnaces burning Kristall, were built by the Belyi Tsar once he accepted humans; every city is built around at least one, with smaller civilian models scattered across the wilds. The Royal Energy Commission maintains them and manages the ore's transport and use.

The prototype torches remain in the Pale Crown Palace, where the Belyi Tsar experimented before building Snezhnograd's great torch. Under Project Stuzha, Kristall became a ration distributed by Fatui detachments, and local officials such as Sretomorozsk's liaison officer Shishkin and its mayor were caught stashing deliveries.

93.content: The Snowland Fae were created by Hyperborean artisans using forbidden methods taught by the first Seelie, Koitar; the "Evolved Children of Humanity" were said to be made of the Frost Moon's light upon the bones of giant beasts. Common kinds are Vila (winged), Domovoy (household), Leshy, Volkodlak (beast), Snegovik (snow; females are Snegurochka) and the mute, prankish Jack Frosts; rarer ones include Augury Birds, Lantern Fae and Water Imps. All can wield elemental power without Visions, many can change shape, and they have their own language and script. Under the Belyi Tsar they were the ruling aristocracy; after his death they lost their monopoly on power. Most now accept the Tsaritsa and live ordinary lives, while small pockets still long for the old order.

94.comment: Snezhnaya: Hyperborea and the Cryo Dragon
94.content: Over 6,000 years ago the golden city of Hyperborea flourished in a warm, green Snezhnaya. Its people tried to make a Primordial Human from the corpse of the Cryo Dragon, one of the Seven Sovereigns. The Dragon's unchecked authority covered the land in primordial ice and crystallised its ley lines, and a Celestial Nail destroyed Hyperborea, whose ruins now lie in the Shadow Realm; survivors fled to Nod-Krai and became the Frostmoon Scions. A Nail of Retribution still hangs over the Dragon's corpse; in 7.1 the dying Ronova fused the "Eitr" into it and it began to crumble. Fae legend, recorded in Saint Strivozha's Songbook, tells a different myth of a King of Light destroying Hyperborea; Snezhnayan historians treat it as legend.

95.comment: Snezhnaya: The Belyi Tsar and the Pale Star Court
95.content: Monomakh Snezhnyi hatched from an icy egg in the Cryo Dragon's remains 5,000 years ago, the incomplete Primordial Human of the Hyperborean experiment, though he and everyone else believed him a fae. Taught the spear by Yalyane Morevna of the House of Hesperides, he founded Kitezh, Snezhnaya's first city and the Pale Star Court's capital. When King Miscislav of the Volkodlak attacked Kitezh, Monomakh killed him, and Grand Dukes Skoldyryt and Vodyanoy, with hurled spears; the fae clans submitted and he took the title Belyi Tsar ("White Tsar"). He became Cryo Archon and God of Love 2,000 years ago, opened his realm to humans, and secretly sought to complete his ascension and overthrow the Heavenly Principles. In the Cataclysm he led an expedition to Khaenri'ah against the Abyss and was killed. His body, still biologically alive, was entombed in the Pale Crown Palace in White Birch Snowgrave and grew into the giant Tsar's White Birch. In the world quest An Ark That Used to Be a Soul, Aksinya transferred the Primordial Human's power into the remains; the Traveler defeated the resulting being and the body crumbled to dust.

96.comment: Snezhnaya: Anastasya and the Third Descender
96.content: More than 6,000 years ago Anastasya loved Saarelainen, the Third Descender, who came from the sea of stars; their son's four-pointed star pupils passed to their descendants, the Khaenri'ahns. Much later, as a herald of the Pale Star Court, she and Saarelainen were incited by the Belyi Tsar to open a gate to the Abyss, creating a passage into the Shadow Realm. The Heavenly Principles erased her. Saarelainen traded his own life for her resurrection and a promise that their descendants would be spared; his remains became the seven Gnoses, and all memory of him was erased, hers included. The Belyi Tsar, hidden in the Shadow Realm, kept the memory and later told her. Unable to trust her own mind, she records every day in a memory prism that Irminsul changes cannot alter.

97.comment: Snezhnaya: Project Stuzha and Project Mistilteinn
97.content: Project Stuzha ("severe cold") is a set of energy-austerity policies passed by the Veche, diverting energy from the public to the Armory Palace. It cost far more and lasted far longer than planned: stoves went cold, small-town stations closed, and Kristall was rationed. Its real purpose was Project Mistilteinn, overseen by Pierro: a weapon capable of fighting the Heavenly Principles, powered by energy drawn from Stellar Linchpins. Ronova's curse halted Mistilteinn (and with it Stuzha) in 7.0; it resumed in 7.1 once her authority was revoked.

98.content: Ronova, Shade of Death, cursed Snezhnaya so that anyone conceiving a breakthrough that threatened Celestia, and everyone near them, died, passed through an afterlife and revived without memory, while Rhinedottir secretly revived the victims before Celestia's monitoring noticed. In 7.0 a snowbound night at the Korolevskiy Theater turned out to be such an afterlife, with Ronova disguised among the audience. In 7.1 Vesna used a fragment of the Ruler of Life's authority to draw "Seals of Life" (cherished memories) from donors to counter death, a scheme that also lured Rhinedottir into the open. At a tea meeting the Tsaritsa stalled her with the six Gnoses, Ronova lost her authority, and Pierro, the Traveler and Dainsleif defeated her at Rankova Zorya.

99.comment: Snezhnaya: Volkodlak Tundra, Sretomorozsk and Rankova Zorya
99.content: Volkodlak Tundra, the "Tundra of Ancient Beasts" in the southwest, is where the capital of King Miscislav's Volkodlak alliance once stood; after the Belyi Tsar killed him, it was razed so that no trace remains. Sretomorozsk is a quiet border town, railway station and port where travel to and from Nod-Krai passes. Rankova Zorya is a village built around a nearly abandoned temporary station, later restored with the Traveler's help. Alatyr is an abandoned remote village.

100.comment: Snezhnaya: Everfrozen Earth, Morepesok and Svetloledovka
100.content: Everfrozen Earth in the north holds Snezhnograd and birch forests whose pioneering-era forestry industry still operates. Morepesok, Tartaglia's home village, is a coastal fishing station where the best catch earns respect. Svetloledovka is a Prime Ice mining town at the foot of Fellfrost Peak whose workers commute from Snezhnograd by train. The domed Sanctuary of Grief holds Signora's tomb, frozen in thick ice by the Tsaritsa after her funeral.

101.comment: Snezhnaya: Fellfrost Peak, Flamefeather Valley and White Birch Snowgrave
101.content: Fellfrost Peak, a huge snowy mountain south of Snezhnograd, is said to belong entirely to Pavlina, a reclusive Grand Duchess of the Snegurochka who lives in the House of Hesperides; hiking its storms is prohibited. Flamefeather Valley, west of the capital, is named for trees with leaves like flaming feathers and bird-shaped monsters; it is not closed, but many visitors never return. White Birch Snowgrave was the Belyi Tsar's itinerant court and holds his mausoleum, the Pale Crown Palace, from which the giant Tsar's White Birch grew.

102.content: Novokitezhgrad, southeast of Snezhnograd, replaced Kitezhgrad after the Abyss destroyed it; built under the Domovoy Grand Duke Alvis, it is known for liquor and Kristall mining and has a large fae population. Port Belovodye is a very rich port. Neither is accessible as of 7.1.

103.content: Snezhnayan chronicles date events by numbered Cycles. In the first year of the 799th Cycle, during the Cataclysm, Anastasya was crowned Tsaritsa of All Snezhnaya, taking the surname Snezhnaya, the feminine form of her predecessor's Snezhnyi. Many fae princes refused to recognise a non-fae ruler, and the Dalegrad clan of Water Imps broke with Snezhnograd. In the second year the humans of Port Belovodye declared self-government; in the third she founded the Fatui (Pierro its first member), which seized the lands of the Drevogorye, Volkhovan and Cirnareka clans, killed Grand Duke Drevogorye, and ended the revolt by offering amnesty for the instigators' surrender. Glupov was built in the fourth year, the Veche founded in the sixth with the human Ioanna Ivanovna as its first chairperson, and in the seventh the Imperial Order Reformation Edict led many princely fae to renounce their titles and leave. Shortly after the Cataclysm she also granted Nod-Krai autonomy at the request of Solovei.

104.content: Before Pantalone became a Harbinger, Snezhnaya had only self-serving private banks; he founded the state-owned Northland Bank by combining human rules with fae customs. Its Snezhnograd headquarters sits above a vault complex so deep that reaching it takes a train ride.

105.content:
Snezhnograd (also: Snow City, Snezhnograd City, Capital of Snezhnaya): Snezhnograd, "Snow City", is the capital of Snezhnaya, a blizzard-country city kept habitable by Kresnik's Torch. It holds the Tsaritsa's Zapolyarny Palace, the Snezhnograd Veche, the Druzhna headquarters and the Adventurers' Guild's headquarters. Pulcinella, "The Rooster", is its Mayor.

The Fatui's headquarters at Glupov lies beside it. Alchemy is outlawed in Snezhnaya, and Snezhnograd is the only main city in the game without a Crafting Bench. Flins calls it beautiful, with a brilliant night sky and endless blizzards, though recently much more industrial.

Geography: Snezhnograd lies in the Everfrozen Earth of Snezhnaya. Snowstorms rage outside, but Kresnik's Torch holds a temperate zone over the city; a resident, Gorchakova, says she still prefers it in a snowstorm, since that is when the Torch's warmth is truly felt. The great torch core, Kresnik's Burning Heart, lies in a chamber beneath the central plaza. Zapolyarny Palace overlooks the plaza. A Statue of The Seven stands in the city; only Snezhnograd and the Court of Fontaine among the main cities have one.

The industrial district of Zolnyy, the "Ash District", sits within the city. A local specialty is the Frostfairy Flower, and the city has a bulletin board, a bookshop (Torchlight Books), a blacksmith, a Northland Bank branch and the Podvorye Restaurant.

Places: Principal places: Zapolyarny Palace, home of the Cryo Archon; the Snezhnograd Veche State Hall; the Druzhna headquarters; the Adventurers' Guild headquarters; Kresnik's Burning Heart; Snezhnograd Square, with the Podvorye Restaurant in front of it; and Zolnyy, the Ash District.

Glupov, the Fatui's satellite fortress-city, lies near Snezhnograd and is called a satellite city of it. A research organisation of some kind is also said to have a base in the city (a Nod-Krai loading screen mentions it, without detail). Details of each major site are in the sub-entries.

People: Citizens are mostly human, with a fair number of Snowland fae living among them, though fewer than in Novokitezhgrad. Volkodlak and fae staff run the Podvorye Restaurant. Notable officials are the Mayor, Pulcinella; Veche councillors such as Eteri and Euphrosiniya; and a Veche advisor, Golitsyn. The Adventurers' Guild has adventurers posted here.

The Savage Bears, a local group with named members Miroslava, Krylov and Anfissa, and a pair of "Mystery-Hunters", Pasha and Vadim, are among the colourful locals the wiki lists. These are minor residents; do not turn them into plot-relevant figures.

Governance: Anastasya, the Tsaritsa and Cryo Archon, rules Snezhnaya from Zapolyarny Palace. Administration is carried out by the Snezhnograd Veche, the council she founded, presided over by Pulcinella. The Fatui act as government, diplomatic corps and military; the Druzhna are the older soldiery. Pulcinella is the second and current Mayor of Snezhnograd, the first being his mentor.

The Veche meets at the State Hall, where citizen representatives deliberate on new laws, a custom kept since the early days. In 7.0 a Veche vote on Project Stuzha was held; a minority opposed it and the project continued until the next Veche period.

Culture: Daily life revolves around heat and work: the Torch is the city's centre, a resident (Gorchakova) says snowstorm days are when its warmth is truly felt, and the Podvorye Restaurant is known for refined takes on traditional food and fire-water. Alchemy is forbidden, which shapes what shops can sell. Fae and humans mix, with a longstanding awareness of the old fae aristocracy that the Veche replaced.

History: Kitezh was Snezhnaya's first city and imperial capital from the 417th Cycle. After the Belyi Tsar pardoned humanity and admitted it to his realm, he moved his seat to Snezhnograd. He ruled from Zapolyarny Palace until his death, after which Anastasya took his place. She was crowned Tsaritsa in the first year of the 799th Cycle; many fae princes refused to come to Snezhnograd to seek an audience, and the Dalegrad clan broke ties with the city. The Fatui built Glupov nearby in year four, and the Veche was established in year six with the human Ioanna Ivanovna as its first chairperson.

Kresnik's Torch was built almost as soon as the Belyi Tsar finished his experiments in the Pale Crown Palace, and the city's most important Torch burns in Kresnik's Burning Heart. The Pale Crown Palace text places the Belyi Tsar's death in the Cataclysm five hundred years ago. In the seventh year of the 799th Cycle the Imperial Order Reformation Edict was published; many fae princes gave up their titles and left Snezhnaya. The Royal Energy Commission oversees the Torches and Kresnik Kristall.

Atmosphere: A glittering, orderly northern capital: deep snow, the glow of Torch heat, steam and iron in industrial streets, a night sky Flins admires. Officials bustle, and the memory of the old fae nobility and the Tsaritsa's distant presence hang in the air.

Outdoor scenes in a blizzard still feel warm within the Torch's range; scenes in the Veche hall feel formal and slightly tense.

Dangers: Inside the city, ordinary danger is low and mostly political. Beyond its limits the blizzards, the Shadow Realm and Fatui patrols matter. Outsiders may be investigated by the authorities, though in Light and Shadow, Intertwined (7.1) the Tsaritsa ordered all investigation of the Traveler to cease.

Travel: Snezhnograd is the hub of Snezhnaya, near the Fatui fortress of Glupov. Zapolyarny Palace is not freely open to visitors; the Traveler was given unrestricted access by the Tsaritsa's decree after meeting her.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Snezhnograd is the working capital of Snezhnaya under the Tsaritsa and Mayor Pulcinella, with its Torch burning and alchemy still outlawed.

The Traveler has visited and been granted free entry to Zapolyarny Palace.

106.content:
The residence of the Cryo Archon, whom the official map text describes as ruling from a throne of sculpted ice and standing alone on her high balcony as if holding the plaza and the world in her sight. The Belyi Tsar ruled from it until his death, after which Anastasya took his place. Named from a Russian word for "beyond the Arctic Circle". Two NPCs are listed: Avreliya and Yermolay.

The Tsaritsa's decree after meeting the Traveler gave them unrestricted access. Pulcinella and Pantalone attended an audience with her there when Dottore presented the Gnoses he had taken in Sumeru.

107.content:
The hall where the Snezhnograd Veche holds its regular meetings, where citizen representatives from various groups deliberate on new laws, a tradition kept since Snezhnaya's early days. Established by Anastasya to replace the fae aristocracy and first chaired by Ioanna Ivanovna, it is now presided over by Pulcinella. Listed NPCs: Councillors Eteri and Euphrosiniya, Privy Advisor Golitsyn, Slavina and Zotov.

The Veche voted on Project Stuzha during the Traveler's visit; Chugunov voted against it, but sixty-one percent were in favour and the project survived. Pulcinella, as Speaker, announced the result.

108.content:
A large chamber beneath the central plaza containing Snezhnaya's most important Kresnik's Torch, a furnace fuelled by Kresnik Kristall. The Belyi Tsar made the Torches so humans could survive the cold; every Snezhnayan city is built around one. Figures listed there include Yelagina, Zarechnaya (acting chair of the Royal Energy Commission), Zaretsky (vice president), Zavyalov and Zybina.

Smaller civilian-model Torches are scattered across the country. The prototype Torches remain in the Pale Crown Palace.

109.content:
Snezhnograd's industrial district. Official text says that even among the ashes one can hold fast to a dream with a heart as steadfast as tin, perhaps how it got its name. Local figures include Agrafena, Artyem, Iryna, Raissa, Scheffield and two shopkeepers, Grigory ("Bratskaya") and Zyryanov ("Kvasnik").

The World Quest "Disputes Without Honor and Humanity" starts here and involves the Luchkin family, Zmei and a rival Izmaylov family base. Afterwards a children's drawing at the Luchkins' base becomes interactable.

110.content: A long-established Snezhnayan restaurant in front of Snezhnograd Square, serving refined takes on traditional local cuisine and fine fire-water. Its owner and whole staff are volkodlak and fae. Staff include Nefedov (owner), Gromov (cook), Smirnov (bartender), Eliseev and Buturlina (servers).

111.comment: Snezhnograd: Druzhna HQ and the Adventurers' Guild Headquarters
111.content: Druzhna HQ is the base of the Snezhnayan soldiery, with listed NPCs Malinina, Musina, Rozhdestvensky, Shakhovskaya and Yarovaya (a podporuchik). The Adventurers' Guild's headquarters stands in the city because the government founded the Guild; adventurers such as Khitrov and Lesnova are posted there.

112.content:
Project Stuzha is a Fatui-run set of energy reforms passed by the Veche: a framework for rationing and allocating Kresnik Kristall that makes everyone cut back, redirecting the saved energy to the Armory Palace. Pulcinella and Pantalone are among its organisers, and the Fatui handle Kristall shipments. In Silence Alone is Disfavored (7.0) the Veche voted on extending it: sixty-one percent were in favour, a shrinking margin after the Veche member Chugunov voted against it, and Pulcinella declared it would stay in effect until the next Veche period. Later events presented it as a lead-up to Project Mistilteinn.

In the quest Mistilteinn (7.0) Pierro revealed that Project Stuzha consolidates the nation's resources to serve Project Mistilteinn, a weapon meant to let the Tsaritsa contend with the Heavenly Principles using energy reverse-engineered from the Stellar Linchpins. Ronova's curse of death blocked the Fatui's technological breakthroughs and the project was briefly suspended; per the wiki it resumed after Celestia revoked Ronova's authority for misusing it. The wiki's Pulcinella page also records Stuzha's suspension. This is major spoiler material; use only if the scene calls for it.

113.content:
Snezhnograd Veche State Hall (also: Veche State Hall, Snezhnograd Veche meeting hall): The Snezhnograd Veche State Hall is where the Snezhnograd Veche, Snezhnaya's legislative assembly, holds its regular meetings. Citizen representatives from different groups discuss newly issued laws there, a tradition kept since the early days of the nation. It is presided over by 'The Rooster', the Fatui Harbinger Pulcinella.

Because members of the Eleven Fatui Harbingers are entitled to take part, the debates blend popular representatives with Fatui officials, and often turn on Kristall and Project Stuzha.

People: Pulcinella, as The Rooster, chairs the sessions and is Speaker of the Veche (the previous Speaker was I. Ivanovna N.). Named at the hall: the Veche Councillors Eteri and Euphrosiniya, the Privy Advisor Golitsyn, Slavina, Zotov and a guard named Stepan. In the 7.0 session delegates and speakers include Tartaglia as 'Childe', Pantalone as 'Regrator', Sandrone as 'Marionette', the scholar Arapov, the Druzhna officer Akvilina and Sharova, who speaks of the Energy Commission's reports.

Spectators include the troupe singer Vodyanitsa, who brings the Traveler, and the reporter Mironova of 'Bring Out the Kvass', a street-stall newspaper.

Governance: Decisions are made by majority vote in sessions chaired by a Speaker. The Veche was founded by Anastasya to replace the aristocracy of the Snowland Fae from the Belyi Tsar's reign. Motions are drafted by the usual procedure and raised later for evaluation, as when the Rooster supports drafting a proposal on collecting regional Kristall data.

Although nominally deliberative, the Fatui are usually able to carry the policies they favour with little resistance. Its chair, Pulcinella, gives statistics on energy commitments and the stabilising production and consumption of Kresnik Kristall, and presents disaster-relief figures supplied by Pantalone.

Culture: Debate is formal: the chair calls 'Order', opens the floor to representatives, and moves to a vote when no new substantive issue remains. In the audience seats, a reporter supplies a running commentary.

Vodyanitsa says the Veche covers the same ground every time and that people are not seeing tangible benefits; in the aftermath of Project Stuzha's suspension the atmosphere is said to have lightened.

Atmosphere: A hall of long speeches: rows of delegates, a dull and lifeless room that livens up when statistics are challenged, and the slam of a hand on the table when tempers rise.

Quests: Archon Quest Silence Alone is Disfavored (Chapter VII, Act I, 7.0): the Traveler listens from the audience seats to a session about extending Project Stuzha. Arguments include whether Fatui families in remote areas receive 15 percent less Kristall than the average civilian family in Snezhnograd, according to Tartaglia, and how Pantalone justifies the current framework.

The scene introduces the Rokot and their most infamous member, Lelek, who in Vodyanitsa's words is obsessed with ending Project Stuzha and uses any means to change votes. Tartaglia argues for a clear and consistent rationale for allocation; Pantalone answers that fairness is relative and that census data are outdated.

Status as of 7.1: In use. After Project Stuzha was put on hold, the mood at the Veche eased, as Tartaglia says in 7.1.

114.comment: Snezhnograd Veche State Hall: Snezhnograd Veche
114.content:
The Veche is Snezhnaya's legislative body for administration and governance, based in this hall. Anastasya established it to replace the Snowland Fae aristocracy. Pulcinella is Speaker, and Harbingers can take part in sessions.

The name echoes the veche, an assembly in medieval Russia where citizens debated key matters.

115.comment: Snezhnograd Veche State Hall: The Veche Session of Silence Alone is Disfavored
115.content:
In the Archon Quest the Traveler sits through a Veche session in which Childe presses for fairer Kristall allocation for Fatui families, and Regrator answers that consistent allocation fails when equipment breaks down and census data are old. Arapov defends Project Stuzha as a framework rather than the cause of hardship.

Akvilina proposes taking Childe's suggestion to Commander Vesna, warning of the Druzhna's workload; the Rooster supports drafting a proposal, and Sharova points out the Energy Commission already collects statistics for each city.

116.content:
Snowmelt Drainage Channel: The Snowmelt Drainage Channel is an underground system beneath Okurov, the strange town in Flamefeather Valley. It was meant to carry snowmelt away so the valley basin would not flood. According to the wiki it was built on the orders of Koshchei, who also used it as a laboratory.

The Traveler and Paimon land in it by accident in the quest Down in the Dumps and have to find a way back up.

Geography: Three map levels: the mouth, an upper level, and a lower level. Okurov lies in a low basin, and the channels were dug beneath it. The tunnels are collapsing and abandoned, with gates, flooded sections, rotary mechanisms, and a control room with tanks. Key terminals control the gates and the water level.

Three kinds of keys open the way: red, white and blue. Inserting either the white or the blue key into the control console lowers the water level; inserting both drains it completely. All three keys must be inserted at once at a control board to open the gate out, which the guide describes as three rounds of authentication.

People: No living residents in the quest beyond Leshy. The Traveler and Paimon are guided by the Eye of Graeae. Zhara, the large bird that attacked them, is what sent them down; the Eye suspects Zhara exists to preserve Okurov's status quo.

Furiosa's name is on the post-op observation reports found in the control room. The Eye of Graeae recalls Koshchei the Deathless as one of the four who made its body and a leading figure of Snezhnaya's vanished school of bio-alchemy.

History: In Down in the Dumps the Traveler falls from Okurov into the channel after Zhara attacks them, while trying to get Goggles' body part back and bring Nastya home. The Eye of Graeae says the town's mutated residents and the half-bird creature remind it of Koshchei's approach to life. The channel's written guide, whose cover bears the name "Doctor Moreau", explains that Okurov sits in a basin where, under the influence of something redacted, temperatures may rise and snowmelt may flood it, so an underground channel system was dug first for drainage and second for something redacted, from which a "tender sprout" emerged.

The guide closes with a wish that when the floodwaters become nourishment for life and useless memories fade into echoes, the author will make his way to a redacted place. The wording echoes the Furiosa report, where new branches and leaves have covered the old body and unneeded memories and emotions are fading.

Atmosphere: Dank, dim and half-forgotten: collapsed paths, standing water, glass tanks in a control room, and notes written by someone who clearly expected to come back.

Dangers: Leshy roam the tunnels and some must be defeated, and the water level changes with the gates. Paimon describes the sewer as crawling with them.

Quests: Down in the Dumps, part of the series In the Dwelling of Life. The Sewer Entrance/Exit Guide can be read only during that quest.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the channel is a derelict, mostly abandoned network. Leaving takes all three keys at the control board; no later content in the sources changes it.

117.content:
Sretomorozsk (also: Candlemas-Frost City, Sretomorozsk Station): Sretomorozsk is a quiet border town in the southwest of Snezhnaya, a railway station and port that connects the country with Nod-Krai. In Chapter VII it is where the Traveler first sees the effects of Project Stuzha: homes are cold, inns are closed and the station is shut. Alyosha, who keeps a small place there, uncovers a Kristall-hoarding scheme.

Most people who board a train here are going to or from Nod-Krai. The name combines the Russian words for Candlemas and frost, and may echo the Candlemas frosts.

Geography: The town lies in the Volkodlak Tundra, in the far southwest, with a station and an eastern port. The wiki's Navigation text calls it a little deserted. Shishkin offered to open the lower combustion chamber of the Kresnik's Torch to residents so they could at least boil water and cook.

Alyosha's house, the station, the Kristall distribution booth, residents' houses and a tunnel from the station to the mayor's house are all in the town. The Snezhnaya Vestnik newspaper is sold here.

People: Eastern port: Buranova, Gryaznov (the mayor after the quest), Obolensky, Ryabov and Vetrova. Station: Burtsev, plus the Transport Bureau conductors Shagova and Vyorskaya. Other residents include Cherkasskaya, Ermolov, Guseva, Samirka, Yarugin and Zolotova. The Fatui representative who handles Kristall deliveries is Polonsky, and the liaison officer who mediates between the Fatui and the townspeople was Shishkin.

Repnina, an elderly woman with failing memory who also comes from Alatyr, lives here; Alyosha visits her, cleans her stove and tidies her room. Alyosha himself spends time here but, in his own words, does not stay at his place often. His dog Tugarin joins him.

Governance: A mayor leads the town, helped by a Fatui liaison officer and a Fatui representative who handles deliveries. The Veche's border-support resolution lets residents buy Kristall from the Fatui. The old mayor and Shishkin were arrested and sent to Snezhnograd for judgment, and the Fatui took over energy distribution until new officials were named.

Alyosha's evidence was arithmetic: he counted train carriages during the snowstorm and compared the train's energy use with the quota figures, finding one or two missing carriages every time and three on the last delivery.

Economy: Under Project Stuzha businesses have closed, the price of Kristall rose by about a third while the town's quota fell, and the Fatui deliver only twice a month. Burtsev complains that a shipment does not last a week. Residents cannot afford to heat their homes, let alone run inns.

Dangers: Cold and shortages are the main dangers. The Traveler's train ride out of town passes through a Shadow Realm distortion full of twisted Oprichniki troopers. The Fatui keep an eye on the Rokot, a covert group Polonsky mentions (Alyosha is later shown aligned with it).

Quests: 'Gunfire in the Silent Lands' (Archon Quest, Chapter VII, Act I, part 2) begins here. Alyosha shelters the Traveler and Paimon, exposes Shishkin and the mayor, and the Traveler then drives the train using the Eye of Graeae; the ride runs into Shadow Realm trouble and the next quest begins at Rankova Zorya.

Status as of 7.1: By 7.1 the corruption has been exposed, the Fatui supervise distribution and have promised that the station will resume service, but the shortages are not over: Alyosha notes Project Stuzha is not going away soon. Sretomorozsk continues to serve as the transit town for Nod-Krai traffic.

118.comment: Sretomorozsk: Shishkin and the Kristall Scheme
118.content: The liaison officer Shishkin smoothly calmed angry residents while secretly stockpiling Kristall. With the old mayor, who picked the workers who unloaded cargo, he moved crates through a tunnel to the mayor's house and sold them out of town, so the town stayed cold. Alyosha and Tugarin tracked the scent to a tunnel behind Shishkin's home; the Fatui recovered stolen crates and arrested both men, while Gryaznov became mayor.

119.content:
Svetloledovka (also: Light-Ice Village, Prime Ice Excavation Site): Svetloledovka ('Light-Ice Village') is a Prime Ice mining town and railway station in Snezhnaya, built in the shadow of Fellfrost Peak. Many of its workers live in Snezhnograd and commute by train. In Chapter VII a malfunction and a monster trapped miners here, and the Traveler first met Odette during the rescue.

It is also where the Traveler finds the mysterious Exaiphanes Blade deep in the cavern. A Local Legend, the Bandersnatch, becomes available afterwards.

Geography: The town stands below Fellfrost Peak, the great snow-sloped mountain south of Snezhnograd. The Cavern of Prime Ice Mountain is entered through a mining area at the settlement, with a notice at the entrance warning people away. A tavern stands in the middle of the town and a lower level holds work areas and machines. The giant excavators are heavy enough that the town can be endangered by snow load.

The site's heat sources matter: one worker, Zhuravlev, is found freezing on a lower level and thanks the Traveler for placing a heat source next to him.

People: Named residents and workers include Demidov, Ignat, Klim, Lyubava, Nekrasov, Pashkov (the Safety Officer), Sobolev (Engineering Supervisor), Veselov, Vorontsov, Vvedensky, Zaleskaya, Zhuravlev and Zvezdina. The trapped miners in the 7.0 incident include Pevtsova, Ryabushinsky and Gornova.

Zhuravlev, after the Traveler warms him, gives them Glaciafruit sent by his family and a modest reward; he says a rough fellow like him has nothing valuable to offer. A Fatui staff member, Zverev, reports the failure to Sandrone.

Economy: Prime Ice is mined here and the settlement is run around it; the train Navigation text says many workers who mine Prime Ice live in Snezhnograd and commute. Sandrone says relief takes weeks to months, because Pantalone must approve the budget and Pulcinella sign off the plan before work can proceed.

History: During unusually heavy snow, a support on one of the giant excavators broke and fell, which woke a dormant burrowing beast in a cave and trapped miners. Odette's Fatui team, which was nearby, started the rescue; Sandrone, who was in the middle of a tea break with the Traveler in Snezhnograd, came with the Traveler to help. The Traveler and Odette led out the five trapped people, found the Exaiphanes Blade deep in the cave and escaped as the cave collapsed behind them, trapping the Chimeric Burrowbeasts inside.

Sandrone reinforced all the equipment so that it could stand months of heavy snowfall. A notice at the cave entrance, placed by Odette's team, was later edited to warn that monsters are active inside and that mining there is suspended. The incident report still had to go through Snezhnograd's slow processes, and the Traveler left with the feeling that there ought to be a better way.

Dangers: The Cavern of Prime Ice Mountain holds chimeric burrowbeasts, electro slimes and the Bandersnatch (Ice Marauder, Lurking Burrowbeast), with a Local Legend, Bandersnatch Grounded Snowhawk, available later. Mining has been suspended. Snow load and cold are constant dangers.

Quests: The town is the setting for the second half of 'Great Deeds on the Tundra' (Archon Quest, Chapter VII, Act I, part 3). A notice and the 'Zhuravlev's Troubles' puzzle are found here.

Status as of 7.1: Inhabited and functioning as of 7.1, with the monster's cave closed and the machines reinforced. Sandrone expected relief to take weeks to months.

120.comment: Svetloledovka: The Svetloledovka Rescue and the Exaiphanes Blade
120.content: When Zverev reports the failure of the Svetloledovka equipment, Sandrone drops her tea party, and the Traveler goes along. Odette tells them five people are trapped and a hostile monster of unknown type is nearby. In the cave, a spotlight mechanism casts a huge shadow of the creature on the ice; Pevtsova shouts at the creature to stay back. After the fight the Traveler touches a strange star floating in the cave and receives the Exaiphanes Blade. Sandrone later introduces Odette to the Traveler as the prima ballerina of Snezhnograd and a rising Fatui figure, and says the two crowning jewels of the Korolevskiy Troupe are Odette and Vodyanitsa.

121.content:
Tartaglia's Home (also: Ajax's family home, Tartaglia family home): Tartaglia's Home is the home of Tartaglia's family in Morepesok, a small seaside fishing village in Snezhnaya. Tartaglia, called Ajax at home, grew up here, and his younger sister Tonia and little brother Teucer live there. He seldom visits, which is the main thing the people at the house talk about.

Morepesok is a station on the West train line from Snezhnograd. The house is where Tartaglia's Anecdote quests about his family take place.

Geography: The home stands in Morepesok, by the coast, in the Everfrozen Earth area. Morepesok is described as a station by the coast where fishing is the livelihood; locals compare their catches, and the most impressive catch earns respect.

Morepesok has a train station and a harbor. The wiki gives no further description of the house itself.

People: Tonia, Tartaglia's younger sister, and Teucer, a young boy and younger brother of Tartaglia, Tonia and Anthon, are the NPCs at the home. Tartaglia's dialogue also speaks of his father and mother. Tonia is extremely close to Tartaglia and holds him in high regard, while he writes to her as 'Dearest Sister' and signs as her 'loyal knight'.

Tartaglia is the third son of the family; two older brothers are mentioned in his character stories, and Anthon is also a younger brother. His father taught him ice fishing in childhood and told him adventure stories.

Culture: An ordinary family home: his father's headaches are eased by medicine that Ajax brings back from his travels, and gifts of scarves, boots, toys and snacks are the way Tartaglia makes up for missed family gatherings.

He sends letters addressed to Tonia, with medicine from Liyue and kites, dolls and snacks for the family.

History: Ajax grew up in Morepesok. At fourteen he ran away with a shortsword and a bag of bread, fell into a chasm and met a swordswoman in the Abyss. When he came back, his father found him changed and brawling, and eventually handed him over to the Fatui.

His worried mother and sisters found him in the forest after only three days, though he felt three months had passed. Tonia says that because he was always picking fights, their father would not let him stay in the village.

Atmosphere: A family home that revolves around waiting for Tartaglia, shadowed by Tonia's worry that if they are not holding his hand he might 'slip away to a place where nobody can ever reach him'.

Quests: Anecdote 'Tartaglia: A Promise' (part four of the Anecdote Chronicles, started by approaching the home): Tartaglia gives Tonia their father's medicine and snacks for Teucer and says he will come home when his work is done and stay a little longer. Related is 'Tartaglia: Back Home' at the Morepesok train station, where he packs gifts as apologies for a missed family dinner.

Tonia answers that he must not let them down again. In the open world, Tonia appears in Morepesok after Wraith's Nocturne, asking whether Ajax was trouble and, if he turns up, asking him to visit more often.

Status as of 7.1: Occupied. Tonia and Teucer remain at home, and Tartaglia still promises to come home more often.

122.content:
Tartaglia has siblings: Tonia, who wants him home, and Teucer and Anthon, younger brothers. In Morepesok he is called Ajax, a name given by his father after a hero's tale.

Teucer 'has really missed' him, according to Tonia. Tartaglia's letters send regards to his parents and siblings and ask Tonia not to make trouble for anyone at home.

123.content: A hidden Anecdote. Tonia asks if Tartaglia is coming too; he says he has work to tie up and promises to stay longer this time. 'I won't, Tonia. I promise.'

124.content:
Teeming Mire (also: Tree Swamp Where Lifeforms Live): The Teeming Mire is the sunken, tree-choked heart of Okurov, the hidden town in Snezhnaya's Flamefeather Valley. Below the assembly hall a giant tree grows among blue algae: the home of the so-called Perfect Tree, an experiment by the bio-alchemist Koshchei, who posed as Doctor Moreau. It is guarded by the firebird Zhara, and it is where the child Nastya chose to be transformed.

The quest chain that ends here, In the Dwelling of Life, is a world-quest series. It is a place of false comfort: inhabitants and algae murmur about happiness and eternity, while the experiment strips away meaning, speech and feeling.

Geography: A swampy, overgrown area reached through the assembly hall's lift and the secret passage behind it. A huge tree stands at the centre with a giant egg-like object that proved to be a part of the Eye of Graeae's body. Blue algae lines the walls and ground and gives off a warm glow. Compared with the frozen tundra outside, the air around the town is unnaturally warm, which Nastya explains is for the 'pretty leaves' to grow.

Flamefeather Valley is named for tall trees whose leaves look like flaming feathers and for bird-shaped monsters; stories hold it was once a human dwelling and is now a place from which many never return.

Places: The assembly hall's Hall of Prayers leads on to the lift and the Perfect Tree's home. Nearby stands Nastya's house, now occupied by a young tree segment called Shar. Blue algae terminals along the walls speak, once Chorus of Solace is complete, in six distinct voices.

Each algae voice repeats a single wish or fear: someone who wanted to catch frogs and finds none in eternity; an old person who says youth has come back as an inability to die; an infant weeping; a person asking where to go in a courtyard of happiness; one who feels growing up means doing all sorts of things; and a mother who thinks her daughter has come back into her arms.

People: Nastya, a young girl and the quest's guide, is transformed here. Koshchei speaks through her. Zhara guards the place. Furiosa, who opposed the plan, was beaten at the hall's door by the Traveler. Aksinya, the self-styled Royal Jester of the late Belyi Tsar, appears outside the tree afterward.

Okurov's other people are Leshy such as Aunt LePuy and No-Nose Ove. Nastya's mother is something she remembers lying ill in bed and whom she hopes to meet again within the Perfect Tree.

History: Koshchei, who posed as Doctor Moreau and seemed to cure the villagers' ailments, built the grand ritual that turns lives into the Perfect Tree, a rooted form that cannot move or speak, in pursuit of eternity. In the final quests the Traveler and Eye of Graeae fight through Zhara to reach the tree, but Nastya refuses to turn back. The Eye of Graeae recovers the ritual's power into the egg. The thing that was Nastya says it had once expected Aksinya to be the one to appear here instead.

Koshchei's notes in the sealed room argue that sorrow and individual love must be cast aside for eternal life, while acknowledging love may be the only thing that does not fade. The thing speaking through Nastya wonders what it wanted, finds that wanting has lost its meaning, and says it will return the Eye of Graeae's power, though everything will still end in a way no one wishes to see.

Atmosphere: Warm, humid, softly lit by glowing blue algae; calm, almost lullaby-like voices that are quietly horrifying. A scene should lean on contrast between cosy warmth and loss of self.

Dangers: Zhara, a huge firebird made by bio-alchemy, guards the area and attacks all outsiders as 'Badbugs'. Mindless Leshy wander the town.

Quests: In the Dwelling of Life: A Sprout Without a Gardener; Transplanted From 'Yesterday' to 'Tomorrow'; Down in the Dumps; Back on One's Feet; Forbidding Doors of Melancholy; To Rest in a Forgotten Field; Chorus of Solace (the last, set in the Mire).

Completing Chorus of Solace unlocks the achievement Gather for Everlasting Happiness. It also runs concurrently with On One Side a Palace, On the Other a Tomb and Hesperides of Love and Hate, which changes how Aksinya is introduced.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Mire holds the Perfect Tree with Nastya now blue algae, and the ritual's power has been returned to the Eye of Graeae.

Zhara is defeated and Aksinya says its body will break down. The experiment's wider consequences are not shown in 7.1.

125.comment: Teeming Mire: Nastya and the Perfect Tree
125.content: Nastya is a young quest NPC from Okurov who believes Doctor Moreau cured her mother and that becoming a Perfect Tree will let her be with her mother again. In Chorus of Solace she is taken over by Koshchei who confirms 'Koshchei or Doctor Moreau' are one and the same, then gives her time to say farewell. Despite Paimon's pleas she chooses to complete the ritual, saying she wants to see her mother's loving eyes once more, and she disintegrates into blue algae. Eye of Graeae says that the Perfect Tree is a form that cannot move, speak or know joy or love, and that already-changed life cannot be reversed even though the ritual can be stopped.

126.comment: Teeming Mire: Zhara and Aksinya at the Tree
126.content: Zhara is the firebird that guards Okurov's heart and the Perfect Tree. After it is slain, Aksinya, who calls herself the late Belyi Tsar's Royal Jester and the builder of the Eye of Graeae's mechanism, appears and says she has adjusted Zhara's body so it will break down. She says she was meant to claim the Eye of Graeae, and that she and the Traveler share the goal of helping the will in the Eye find its body and reclaim its power.

127.content:
Tidesong Cavern (also: Cavern of Melodic Tides): Tidesong Cavern is a hidden cave on Fellfrost Peak, the snowy mountain south of Snezhnograd in Snezhnaya, and the private practice space of the Water Imp Vodyanitsa. A flooded cave with a giant shell and a few Prime Ice echo pillars, it gives her voice the acoustics she wants and keeps her audience away.

The in-game description calls it a secluded cavern rarely visited by others, the private sanctuary of "a certain fae". Its map name is the Cavern of Melodic Tides, and it hosts a Meeting Point of the same name (introduced in 7.0).

Geography: The cave lies below the slopes of Fellfrost Peak and is entered by climbing down an ice wall from a hole near the surface; the last stretch ends in a freezing puddle. Beyond are pools of water, a huge shell or conch in which Vodyanitsa sits, and the Echo Pillars of Prime Ice that shape how sound carries through the chamber. Local specialties found on the peak include Flockingweed and Frostfairy Flower.

Vodyanitsa says she thought of flooding the entrance to seal it, but engineers warned that blasting the rock could cause landslides, avalanches and cracks, and that wrecking the cave's structure would ruin its acoustics, so she left it. The pillars glow softly and ring in harmony when correctly tuned; when she sings, cracked ones are marked out by lit notes above them.

Places: The giant shell is Vodyanitsa's seat, and she blows bubbles from it for fun. The Echo Pillars of Prime Ice are the cave's key feature: a few had cracked while she practised, spoiling the "echo chamber" until the Traveler repaired them in the world quest. A tent and campfire are sometimes found where travelling adventurers have sheltered overnight.

People: Vodyanitsa is the cave's occupant. Her fellow troupe members Odette and Alyosha visit and appear in post-quest open-world dialogue: Odette brings mints and stands unmoved by Vodyanitsa's teasing, and Alyosha shelters stray puppies there from the blizzard and offers to lend guard dogs, which Vodyanitsa declines.

Vodyanitsa tells the Traveler she once practised in The Korolevskiy Theater, but crowds gathered below the open window, and one young fan who had once sent her flowers and letters started reselling the tickets she was given at several times their price. Losing the innocent enthusiast, she moved her practice here. She also practises at Rankova Zorya (rendered "Dawn Station" in the English subtitles).

Atmosphere: Cold, damp and echoing, with dripping water, ice walls and the sound of a powerful voice rolling around the chamber. Small animals that flee when she practises return once the pillars are repaired.

Dangers: Mostly the climb and the cold. Vodyanitsa gives a freezing visitor a warming pill used by hunters rather than liquor. She is confident the blizzard and entrance keep wild animals and adventurers out, and that she could simply dive into the water and escape anyone who found her.

Travel: Reached from Fellfrost Peak beyond Snezhnograd's walls by following the singing to the cave entrance and climbing down. The Meeting Point unlocks after completing the world quest "Like a Land Where the Tide's Song Whispers", which itself requires finishing step 6 of "Silence Alone is Disfavored".

Quests: The world quest "Like a Land Where the Tide's Song Whispers" has the Traveler follow a singing voice to the cave, meet Vodyanitsa, and repair the broken Prime Ice Echo Pillars guided by her song, ending with her singing a cappella to the restored cave. It leads into "The Tides Echo Themselves". The Meeting Point's rewards and companion quests are gameplay features.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the cavern is Vodyanitsa's working private retreat, with its pillars repaired and the Meeting Point available.

128.comment: Tidesong Cavern: Vodyanitsa's Private Practice Room
128.content: Vodyanitsa's hidden practice room on Fellfrost Peak. She keeps it secret, spares the city from rehearsal noise, and relies on its Prime Ice Echo Pillars for acoustics. After the Traveler repaired the pillars she sang for them and said she would practise there that day and go to Rankova Zorya within days. Odette and Alyosha know the place.

129.content:
Torchlight Books (also: Enlightened Torch): Torchlight Books is a bookshop in Snezhnograd owned by Moes. It stocks books on Snezhnayan history and ballet.

Sandrone, one of the Fatui Harbingers, says the shop has a very nice selection of teas and cakes and takes the Traveler there to talk, remarking that Snezhnograd has some class compared with Nasha Town.

People: Moes is the owner. Other named people connected to the shop are Brovinov and Shchukina, who is listed as a fortune teller.

Quests: In the Archon Quest Great Deeds on the Tundra, Sandrone, speaking as the Harbinger Marionette, leads the Traveler to Torchlight Books to catch up over tea and insists the Traveler pay, since she says she already wasted a good cup of tea that day. What is discussed belongs to that quest, not to the shop.

Culture: The sign reads "Enlightened Torch" in Snezhnayan script. The shop's books tie into the city's culture of ballet and historical scholarship.

130.content:
Train (also: Your Train, the Traveler's train): The Train is the Traveler's personal base in Snezhnaya: a large train summoned by the Eye of Graeae and made to run on the iron rails crossing the frozen tundra. It lets the Traveler reach the region's stations and carries a shooting range, crafting bench and firearm loadout display.

It is made of the first two carriages of the defunct train in which the Traveler originally found the Eye of Graeae, renovated and upgraded by the Eye after the quest Gunfire in the Silent Lands. Calling it from the Eye's gadget near any track brings it in with the line "After some time, the train arrived...", and it displaces any public train on that stretch.

Places: The first carriage holds the controls and most of the equipment: the Eye of Graeae terminal with Navigation FoV (a station map), a pyramid-shaped Shadow Realm Analyzer, a diamond-shaped portal into the Shooting Range, a display wall for firearms and tactical gear, a crafting bench and a front window for watching the tundra. In-game, a Prime Ice Communicator also connects to Katheryne of the Adventurers' Guild once the Snezhnaya guild quest is done.

The second carriage is more homely. A window carries a drawing by Paimon, and a table gathers keepsakes from Snezhnaya as the Traveler collects them. Paimon comments on several: matryoshka dolls modelled on Odette and Vodyanitsa, a poster for Odette's final performance, a Jack Frost figurine, a doll that Ikhor turned into, a model locomotive and a picture of Nastya. Character stickers appear on the wall as Meeting Points rise in level. The interior is a warm zone, extending just outside the rear door and between carriages.

Travel: The Navigation FoV lists stations the Traveler can ride to: Snezhnograd, Morepesok, Rankova Zorya, Svetloledovka and Sretomorozsk, with Pale Crown Palace listed until the Traveler has started the related quest. The train's position is marked on the map and the player can teleport to it or to the Shooting Range.

The station blurbs give flavour. Snezhnograd's central station is the nation's largest, with inspections by the Royal Railway Transport Bureau before the elevator up to the city. Morepesok is a fishing coast station. Rankova Zorya was a temporary stop nearly abandoned. Svetloledovka serves Prime Ice miners who live in Snezhnograd and commute. Sretomorozsk, in the southwest, mostly serves people travelling into and out of Nod-Krai. Pale Crown Palace is described as a stop where no one arrives, a snow-covered grave where the Belyi Tsar is buried.

History: The train began as a wrecked, defunct train where the Traveler found the Eye of Graeae. After Gunfire in the Silent Lands, the Eye restored two of its carriages into the current train, which was introduced with Snezhnaya in Version 7.0. Its in-game description calls it a massive train built to traverse the iron rails over the frozen tundra, to be used well on expeditions.

Atmosphere: A cosy, slightly cluttered refuge from the cold: steady motion over the rails, snow sweeping past the windows, Paimon's drawing and small souvenirs of past adventures on the table.

131.content: The table in the Train's front carriage fills with keepsakes tied to Snezhnayan quests, each prompting a reminiscence from Paimon, such as the dolls of Odette and Vodyanitsa, a poster from Variations on Belyi and Chernyi, a model locomotive and a picture of Nastya. They are the main place the Train recalls the Traveler's journey.

132.content:
Train Boneyard: The Train Boneyard is a point of interest in Everfrozen Earth, a graveyard of old trains. In the world quest Disputes Without Honor and Humanity it is where Vasiliy, the Izmaylov family's "Young Sire", made his last stand. Zmei and Sofya say "train boneyard" is just a nickname used by locals.

The entrance has a door guarded by an Izmaylov guard who demands a password, and the area ends in a Shadow Realm fight and an exit by mine cart.

Geography: The wiki places it in Everfrozen Earth and tags the page as a stub, so no further layout is given. The quest has the party approach by train, pass the guarded door, move into the depths, and climb to an upper level beyond where Vasiliy is fought. A mine cart takes the party out afterward.

A note on the upper level, past Vasiliy's fight, is addressed to the Izmaylov members. The area is also where the Shadow Realm opens in the quest.

People: Vasiliy, the Young Sire of the Izmaylov family, and Izmaylov guards hold the place. The Luchkin side, with Zmei, Iryna, Sofya and Gureva, enters to stop him. The password is found out by Gureva, who says it is "Oedipus".

Zmei speaks for the Fae Gang Federation's High Table when thanking the Traveler afterward.

Culture: A door guard asks "What's the password?" and turns away guesses such as "Sweet Madame" and "Fire-Water" with an angry "No unauthorized personnel allowed". The locals treat the name as private.

History: In Disputes Without Honor and Humanity Vasiliy is working to open the Shadow Realm; Zmei says that if he had figured out how, he could have taken the entire High Table down with him. A note he left, Yet-to-be-Completed "New High Table Rules", says snow buries every story, that the Izmaylov were forced to live in the shadow of "great figures", and that he, Vasiliy, will lead them to stand as equals at the High Table and proudly call themselves Izmaylov.

Zmei recalls that the three of them (Zmei, Vasiliy and a third person) once played hide-and-seek, and Vasiliy hid in the deepest part of a collapsed tunnel to win. After the quest the tremors stop and the Shadow Realm's influence fades, and Zmei says the device that opened the Shadow Realm has been destroyed.

Atmosphere: A rusting, snow-covered scrapyard of train carriages that doubles as a gang's last hiding place. The note found there is more sorrowful than menacing.

Dangers: Izmaylov guards at the entrance and fights in the Shadow Realm before the Vasiliy boss fight. The entrance is closed to anyone without the password.

Quests: Disputes Without Honor and Humanity, in the chapter Mean Streets of the Despicable.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Izmaylov incident is over; the High Table is deciding what happens to the Izmaylovs. The sources do not show it changing in 7.1.

133.content:
VIP Lounge (also: Lounge for Honored Guests, House of Hesperides VIP room): The VIP Lounge is a room on the second floor of the House of Hesperides, the mountain manor of the Snegovik in Fellfrost Peak, Snezhnaya, set aside for honoured guests. A guard at the door admits only holders of a VIP Pass, a gilded letter said to be issued by the manor's mistress. Inside, a main hall and a side room hold tables for guests who come to drink and rest.

Ordinary visitors are turned away politely. The Traveler can get in by finding a lost pass, after which the lounge becomes the setting of a small seating puzzle.

Places: The lounge has a main hall, nearer the bar, and a side room with a gap in one wall. Only two tables are free in the whole lounge. A hat-wearing Jack Frost by the entrance offers a catching game (a time trial).

The Hidden Exploration Objective "Please, Be Seated" (the name is unofficial) is played here. Prime Ice Cubes can be used to block the gap in the side room. Completing the objective, and the Jack Frost game, rewards chests.

People: A guard checks passes, and waiting staff look after guests. The guard is startled that a human holds a pass. Named guests: Zlatov, who wants a quiet table away from the gap in the wall; Iskelina, a hard drinker who wants the main hall; the sisters Koshakova and Khmelyova from Novokitezhgrad; and Lazoreva. Abuzova, a harried staff member, appears only during the objective.

Zlatov is anxious that someone might peek at him through the gap. Iskelina rarely visits the manor and wants to drink more than usual. Koshakova is happy to sit with anyone, but her younger sister Khmelyova will not let her sit alone with a man and refuses to share a small table with two other people. Abuzova fears offending important guests and her superior Aglaya, and is thankful for a guest who solves problems instead of causing them.

Governance: The manor belongs to the Snegovik, and the lounge is under the authority of its mistress, Pavlina, whose pass admits guests; the guests refer to it as her VIP Room. Staff report to Aglaya.

Atmosphere: Quiet and slightly tipsy, with polite staff, murmured complaints about tables, and stray drinkers challenging each other. It is crowded with unusual guests because the manor is busy with preparations for a wedding.

Quests: "Please, Be Seated" starts at the lounge door. Steps: talk to a Snegovik waiter and a Snegovik who has had too much to drink, find the VIP Pass, show it to the guard, talk to Abuzova, and settle the four guests' seating so each is content. The reward is a chest.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the lounge is accessible to anyone who finds a pass.

Nothing about the room has changed since its release in 7.0.

134.content:
The VIP Pass is a quest item described as a gilded letter said to be issued by the master of the mountain manor, Pavlina. Those bearing it were once frequently invited to the House of Hesperides. It allows a brief respite in the VIP Lounge. In "Please, Be Seated" it is hidden near a drunken guest and her waiter, and appears only once they have been spoken to.

When the Traveler shows the pass, the guard remarks that he wonders whether such a pass has ever been granted to a human, but says his job is only to verify and stand guard, and lets them in.

135.content:
Volkodlak Tundra (also: Tundra of Ancient Beasts): The Volkodlak Tundra is called the "Tundra of Ancient Beasts". It is said to have been the site of the capital of the Miscislavli Alliance, a confederation ruled by the great Volkodlak lord Miscislav. When the Belyi Tsar's spear pierced Miscislav's head and his horsemen scattered the alliance, everything here was demolished and rebuilt, with no trace left of the old city. The Archon Quest of Snezhnaya begins in the tundra, at the village of Rankova Zorya.

The in-game description says the ordinarily merciful Tsar seemed almost afraid that something might arise from this place again.

Geography: Open snow-covered tundra with scattered settlements and rail lines. Rankova Zorya, a village built around an abandoned train station, is its best known place. The only boss recorded for the area is a Chimeric Winged Lion.

Rankova Zorya has been revived by Alyosha, Odette and Vodyanitsa with the Traveler's help, with a restaurant, a bulletin board and snowmen that can be decorated with hats and scarves. A Jack Frost sits on a cliff north of the village, restrained by a grappling gun, in a puzzle listed on the neighbouring area's page.

Places: Rankova Zorya: a small village around a former train station. The old Volkodlak capital: a vanished site, rebuilt beyond recognition.

History: About 3,000 years ago the Volkodlak were organised in the Miscislavli Alliance under King Miscislav, the "Blood-Devourer", to whom the Vila and others paid tribute. The Belyi Tsar (Monomakh Snezhnyi) of the Pale Star Court persuaded the Vila to stop paying; Miscislav demanded vast reparations and went to war.

Miscislav gathered clans of the alliance and allies and marched on the Tsar's city Kitezh, but poor tactics and bad weather doomed three campaigns. In the third, the Tsar hurled his spear through Miscislav's skull and killed him, then took the title Belyi Tsar and became the undisputed leader of Snezhnaya. Miscislav's skull was kept in the Zapolyarny Palace treasury. Some say he tried to invoke the Shadow Realm in his last battle.

Atmosphere: Wide, windy snowfields, old battlefields beneath the snow and trains stopping at half-forgotten stations.

Dangers: Volkodlak war bands and bandit gangs, winged chimeric beasts such as the Chimeric Winged Lion, blizzards and cold.

Quests: The Archon Quest Chapter VII, Act I "Everwinter Without Mercy" opens here: "Great Deeds on the Tundra" begins in Rankova Zorya. World quests such as "Daybreak After the Snow" and "Newcomers in the Snow" restore the village.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 nothing beyond the revival of Rankova Zorya is recorded here.

136.content: Rankova Zorya is a small village built around an abandoned train station. With the Traveler's help, Alyosha, Odette and Vodyanitsa restore it and life returns; it gains a restaurant, a news stand (Vestnik) and a bulletin board. Alyosha's dog Lyumina lives there. The Archon Quest "Great Deeds on the Tundra" starts with the Traveler boarding a train here to reach Snezhnograd.

137.comment: Volkodlak Tundra: Miscislav and the Miscislavli Alliance
137.content: Miscislav was King of the Volkodlak and ruler of the Miscislavli Alliance, a rival of Monomakh Snezhnyi. His head was said to be the size of a chariot, earning him the fae name "Gorynishche", meaning Son of the Mountain. His death in battle at Monomakh's hand let Monomakh consolidate rule over Snezhnaya.

138.content:
White Birch Snowgrave (also: Snow-Entombed Crownlands): White Birch Snowgrave was the itinerant court of the Belyi Tsar and became his mausoleum after he died in the Cataclysm five hundred years ago. Its palace, the Pale Crown Palace, is both palace and ruin: once the seat from which the ancient Tsars ruled, now their final resting place. From it sprang the giant Tsar's White Birch, a sign that the Tsar still watches over Snezhnaya.

The palace stands hidden beneath the great birch. Within lies the Hvergelmir research facility where the Eye of Graeae was created, and a beast called Zver still guards the Tsar's body.

Geography: A snow-buried crown land of drifts, ruins and a giant white tree. The Pale Crown Palace's gates are choked with snow, so visitors must find another way in; inside are the Frozen Royal Hall, hanging corridors and a spiral tower. A hidden railway leads to it, and a train stop there is described as one at which no one arrives, a snow-covered grave.

The Tsar's White Birch and its monuments dominate the area; the Tsar's White Birch drains energy from the Eye of Graeae if someone stands close. Local specialties: Frostfairy Flower. The area also holds Kresnik's Torch, Kresnik Kristall and Shadow Realm content.

Places: Pale Crown Palace: the Tsar's mausoleum and former palace, with the Frozen Royal Hall and the first Kresnik's Torch. The hidden Hvergelmir research facility lies within it. The palace also holds six readable "Notes by a Certain Noble Individual".

Pavlina kept a laboratory at the palace, and the facility holds a sealed egg containing a being called the Proto-Man, plus strange alchemical apparatus.

People: The Belyi Tsar lies buried beneath the birch. Zver, a two-headed beast, guards his remains. The researchers Izmaylov and Azazel appear in a vision of the past.

Aksinya, the Tsar's loyal servant and a Hvergelmir alchemist, and the bio-alchemist Koshchei, who created the chimeric monsters, are tied to the palace. Zver began as a failed prototype Koshchei abandoned until the Tsar took it in and gave it purpose.

History: The palace was a place where the Tsar welcomed humans alongside the fae, and where the flame of Kresnik was first kindled before spreading across the land. After the Tsar died fighting the Abyss and waves of beasts, five hundred years ago, his remains were returned here and part of his body became the Tsar's White Birch.

Hvergelmir, the institute housed in the palace, studied bio-alchemy for the Tsar's aim of reaching the vacant seat in the court of the stars. Researchers feared the new Tsaritsa would ban alchemy and halt their work, and an earlier experiment had gone disastrously.

Atmosphere: A cold hush of snow-muffled halls, stone beasts and cracked royal chambers, with the pale branches of an enormous tree glimmering above.

Dangers: Rugged Elder Leshy elites; winged halberd-knights and soarer knights; glacial wardens and glaciomancers; the guardian Zver; puzzle-locked doors and statues.

Travel: A hidden railway is summoned by a mechanism; an old prototype train operated by the Eye of Graeae takes the Traveler there.

Quests: The world quest series "On One Side a Palace, On the Other a Tomb": "To Gaze Upon the Dreaming Pale Crown" and "The Stone Beasts, Like Ghouls Seated". It forms part of the Eye of Graeae's search for its scattered power.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the grave is quiet, with the Tsar's White Birch still standing.

Zver was defeated in the quest, but the palace itself remains a mausoleum.

139.comment: White Birch Snowgrave: Pale Crown Palace
139.content: The Pale Crown Palace is the Belyi Tsar's mausoleum, once one of his palaces, where he is buried beneath the soil. Inside the Frozen Royal Hall stands the very first Kresnik's Torch, which must be struck to restart. The palace contains the old Hvergelmir laboratories.

140.comment: White Birch Snowgrave: Tsar's White Birch
140.content: The Tsar's White Birch is a giant tree that rose where the Belyi Tsar was buried. Official text calls it his body transformed, protecting everyone in Snezhnaya; the wiki describes it as an overgrowth of nerves from his corpse. It is an exploration mechanic that drains energy from the Eye of Graeae if the Traveler stands too close.

141.content: Zver is a two-headed beast, once a failed chimeric prototype abandoned by Koshchei, which the Belyi Tsar treated as a loyal companion. It has guarded his corpse for centuries and hates those who wronged its master. After being defeated, it warns the Traveler that the Eye of Graeae may not be wholly trustworthy.

142.content:
Zapolyarny Palace (also: Palace Beyond the Arctic Circle, Glacial Palace of the Polestar, Tsaritsa's palace): Zapolyarny Palace stands in Snezhnograd, Snezhnaya's capital, and is the residence from which the Cryo Archon rules. The Belyi Tsar held court here until his death in the cataclysm 500 years ago; Tsaritsa Anastasya has reigned from it since. It looks wrought from ice and snow, everything inside revolves around the Tsaritsa, and it holds her throne room (where she holds court with Harbingers and ministers), her private office and, in a hidden basement, a seal left by the Third Descender.

The name means "beyond the Arctic Circle". Venti named it as the Tsaritsa's seat as early as the Prologue, but the Traveler first entered it in the 7.1 Archon Quest, when Anastasya granted them unrestricted access.

Geography: The palace stands in Snezhnograd in the Everfrozen Earth area, above a plaza, with steps where crowds gather. The Tsaritsa is sometimes seen standing alone on a high balcony overlooking that plaza. Its highest point can be reached by gliding along a chain of Stellar Vortices nearby (the hidden achievement "Because the Palace Is There", 7.0).

Places: Rooms shown inside: a main hall; the throne room holding the Cryo Archon's divine throne of sculpted ice; the Tsaritsa's office beside the throne room; a hidden basement chamber holding the Third Descender's seal; the Tsaritsa's memory prism, in a corner of the office; and a visitors' lounge with a fire and hot tea for those waiting to be received. A Treasury is mentioned in lore.

The lounge sits next to rooms where the Tsaritsa rests, so guards ask visitors to keep quiet. According to "A Brief History of the Pale Starborn", the chariot-sized, bear-shaped skull of King Miscislav of the Volkodlak, still marked by the Emperor's spear that killed him, is kept in the palace Treasury. In the Belyi Tsar's day the palace had rotating galleries where banquets and dances seemed never to stop (Vessel of Plenty).

People: Tsaritsa Anastasya lives and works here. Danica, Head Maid of the royal household, and Vesna, Commander of the Druzhna and considered the Tsaritsa's right hand, are often at her side. Chayka, a Domovoy, is her Confidential Secretary and head of Her Imperial Majesty's Own Chancellery. Druzhna soldiers guard the palace; Harbingers such as Pierro and Pulcinella attend court.

Named staff: reception officer Lozkaya, who checks guests' identity, dress, audience times and knowledge of protocol and takes charge of any object unfit for the Tsaritsa's presence; Druzhna guards Mezhnaya, Myatezhnaya, Nevedomskaya and Gorkin (and Yermolay, placed here to uphold the old rites of courtesy); messengers Chistyakov and Shmeleva, who go out to summon Harbingers and other Fatui when the Tsaritsa wants them; the civil servant Innokenty, who handles Novokitezhgrad's affairs and struggles with letters full of archaic fae words; the maid Tropina; and the Druzhna officer Avreliya, on patrol nearby.

Governance: Snezhnaya is governed from here. Anastasya rules directly and with absolute power; her Edicts are the nation's highest authority. At morning court assemblies she sits before her ministers and Harbingers ("My Lords, Ladies, and Gentlemen"), hears reports, gives rulings and dismisses court. Tartaglia says she dislikes excessive court etiquette: basic good manners and respect are enough.

At the assembly in 7.1 Pulcinella reported on civil affairs and Kristall rationing during her absence and submitted an Audit Office list of corrupt officials; Anastasya produced a further list from the House of the Hearth and assigned him the Druzhna's 3rd Company to review it. She also endorsed Pierro and Mitya's report halting their research until Ronova could be dealt with. At a later assembly she refused extra rail-maintenance funds to a Transportation Minister whose audit had missed a section, and instead honoured a child who had been maintaining it with the title "Track Captain". Her stated principle: let the wicked tremble and the righteous be rewarded.

History: The Belyi Tsar ruled Snezhnaya from Zapolyarny Palace until he died in the cataclysm 500 years ago, and Anastasya succeeded him. He was also the original guardian of the Third Descender's seal beneath it. At the end of 7.0 the Tsaritsa returned in triumph from slaying a blizzard-bringing monster and took her throne again, with Pierro bowing and Fatui ranks at attention. In 7.1 she received the Traveler at court, and later used the palace for her meeting with Rhinedottir that brought about Ronova's fall.

Under the Tsar, fae nobles fond of luxury treated banqueting at the palace as their chief duty, and affairs of state were often settled over wine. The foreign alchemist and astrologer Professor Rotwang, nicknamed the "mad monk", became the Tsar's favourite and a frequent courtier; rumours told that Grand Duke Photius failed to poison him and that he summoned the late wife of the fae shapeshifter Filipov, though he never confirmed either tale (Vessel of Plenty).

Atmosphere: Grand, solemn and cold, standing "majestic" amid wind and snow. Courtiers and guards are formal and anxious to be correct; the Tsaritsa herself is calm, brief and hard to read.

The maids are held to a standard of perfection: not a speck of dust on the tablecloth, every utensil in place, every light polished. Danica insists that every visitor, "an envoy of the heavens or a beggar on the street", is received with the same courtesy.

Quests: Archon Quest Chapter VII: "Mistilteinn" (Act II, 7.0, closing cutscene); "Light and Shadow, Intertwined", "Sparks Converging Upon the Tundra" and "One Move Left to Make" (Act III, "White Night, Like a Dream Upon Waking", 7.1); "Black Feathers Scattered at Parting" (Act IV, "A Rekviem for the Underworld", 7.1). World quests: Secret Tsarist Assignment Part I ("A Letter From Zapolyarny Palace", "The Tsaritsa's New Portrait", "Just the One Court Assembly"), 7.1.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the palace remains Anastasya's seat of rule. The Traveler may come and go freely and acts as her informal consultant. The Third Descender's seal beneath it is still closed; Anastasya holds six Gnoses, and the Pyro Gnosis is missing.

After Ronova's fall the research restrictions were lifted, and the Tsaritsa personally commended everyone involved. Each week Chayka hands the Traveler new Secret Tsarist Assignments at the palace.

143.comment: Zapolyarny Palace: The Third Descender's Seal Chamber
143.content:
In a hidden basement of the palace stands a massive crystalline seal. The Belyi Tsar, its first custodian, said it was the last thing the Third Descender left before the Heavenly Principles killed him, and it seems to have escaped their notice. Every attempt to open it over the centuries has failed. Only Gnoses (the Third Descender's remains) draw any response, so Anastasya believes all seven must be gathered to reveal what is inside. Opening it is her second reason for collecting the Gnoses, besides amplifying her power to face the Heavenly Principles. She showed it to the Traveler in 7.1 as compensation for their cooperation.

Its contents are unknown to everyone, the Tsaritsa included. In the same conversation she told the Traveler that her authority is "love", which she refuses to use or identify with, because the gods' love for humanity was imposed by the Heavenly Principles as a curse.

144.comment: Zapolyarny Palace: The Tsaritsa's Transcription Prism
144.content:
A large prism resembling a Starlight Prism stands in a corner of the Tsaritsa's office. Believing her own memory cannot be fully trusted, Anastasya has for a long time recorded each day's memories in it. Pierro explains that, like a Stellar Linchpin, it carries the Third Descender's power and so is immune to certain laws of Teyvat, including alterations made through Irminsul.

The wiki ties this to her past: when she was resurrected, the Heavenly Principles erased her memories of Saarelainen, the Third Descender, and the Belyi Tsar later told her about him. Pierro calls such objects variables from beyond this world and indispensable in the fight against the Heavenly Principles.

145.content:
Tartaglia arranged the Traveler's first audience by having their application approved for a court session. Anastasya opened by announcing the death of the blizzard-summoning beast, dealt with corruption and the Ronova problem, then turned to "the Traveler from afar": she called them a formidable adversary worthy of respect, proposed cooperation, ordered all investigations into them stopped and granted them unrestricted access to the palace. Afterwards she took them to her office, asked where the Pyro Gnosis was, explained why she wants the Gnoses and why Snezhnaya, having long pushed its technology to the limits the Heavenly Principles permit, lives under threat of a Nail of Retribution.

In the office she introduced Danica, who had already sounded out the Traveler at Podvorye Restaurant; Anastasya told her that such methods risked the trust of a potential friend, and Danica promised to change her approach. The Traveler said the Pyro Gnosis had burned with Irminsul and gone into the Ley Lines; Anastasya answered that, as part of the Third Descender, it cannot coexist with the Ley Lines for long and will be cast out eventually. Pierro then took her to the Armory Palace for the Seals of Life experiment.

146.comment: Zapolyarny Palace: Rhinedottir's Audience and the Fall of Ronova
146.content:
In Act IV Anastasya invited Rhinedottir, the Ruler of Life, to the palace, offering her information about Asmoday, whom she had glimpsed with a hooded figure beside the storm-beast. While Rhinedottir and Anastasya talked over tea, the Traveler, Pierro and Dainsleif held Ronova at Rankova Zorya. As she rose to leave, Rhinedottir sensed that the flow of time was wrong: Anastasya had used her six Gnoses as the nodes of a Gnosis-amplified Cryo field that slowed time in the hall. The window for resurrection that Ronova and Rhinedottir had agreed on passed unnoticed, Celestia reclaimed Ronova's authority, and Anastasya reminded Rhinedottir of her duty to resurrect those Ronova had killed, which she agreed to do.

Naberius urged punishment for overstepping her authority, but Rhinedottir declined, praised the Tsaritsa as a worthy rival and left her unharmed. Anastasya credited both the Gnoses and her own insight over the past thousand years, and admitted the trick would not work twice. Earlier, Danica had escorted the guest in without fear, and Rhinedottir remarked that the Tsaritsa's taste differs greatly from the Vinster King's; Anastasya said she had visited Khaenri'ah's royal palace only once, after the cataclysm.

147.content:
Vesna lured the Traveler to the palace with a "prize" letter. Anastasya wants an adviser of real skill who answers to no faction, so she can understand the nation she is supposed to "love" without leaving the palace or relying on biased ministers. Danica doubted a free traveler would obey. The Traveler refused to become a servant of the court but agreed to help as a friend.
